item.content:encoded:
Game 5 of the ALCS between the Tampa Bay Rays and Cleveland Guardians takes place on Sunday afternoon, and these teams are knotted at two games apiece after Tampa Bay won Game 4.
There are a ton of props to consider in Game 5 of the ALCS, including a home run prop or two as these teams look to deliver a key blow before the series shifts back to Tampa Bay on Monday.
Drew Rasmussen (14 home runs allowed in the regular season, two in the postseason) and Parker Messick (17 home runs allowed in the regular season, one in the postseason) are on the mound in this game.
The total (6.5) is pretty low in this matchup, so we may not see a ton of offense.
While betting on home runs is a fun way to get involved in the action, these props are extremely tough to hit with the pitching in the postseason. Still, there have been a few long balls in this series, and I’m targeting one player that has already gone deep over the course of the first four games to stay hot on Sunday.
Best MLB Home Run Prop Bet Picks for ALCS Game 5
Chase DeLauter to Hit a Home Run (+970)
Chase DeLauter homered 16 times during the regular season, and he took Drew Rasmussen deep in Game 1.
The Guardians youngster was 1-for-3 against the Rays ace in the series opener, and he’s 2-for-4 against him in the regular season in his career.
DeLauter is dangerous against right-handed pitching, homering 13 times while posting an .808 OPS during the regular season.
He’s also been hot in this series, picking up five hits, three RBIs and three runs scored in four games. Overall, he’s hitting .294 with two doubles in a homer in the 2026 postseason.
There are worse bets to make at nearly 10/1 odds in Game 5.
Junior Caminero to Hit a Home Run (+497)
During the regular season, Junior Caminero hit 42 home runs and was elite against left-handed pitching.
He had a .287 batting average, a .916 OPS and homered eight times against southpaws. He has not had a ton of success against Messick in his career (1-for-12), but the lefty did allow 17 home runs in the 2026 regular season.
At some point, Caminero is going to get a hold of a ball, as he’s yet to go deep in the playoffs. Still, Caminero is hitting, picking up at least one hit in three games in this series, including two doubles.
This prop has skyrocketed all the way to +497 with Messick on the mound, but the Guardians’ bullpen has been taxed over the last few days and could be vulnerable to a long ball.
With just one game to bet on, I’m going to take a shot on the best power hitter for either team to leave the yard on Sunday.
Odds refresh periodically and are subject to change.

item.title: [mlb.com] Who should Brewers want to face in the World Series?
item.dc:creator: Zach Sweet

item.content:encoded:
When the Brewers finished off the Dodgers on Thursday night, their World Series opponent was the last thing on anyone’s mind. An MLB official closed the postgame press conference by telling manager Pat Murphy and NLCS MVP Jake Bauers, “We’ll see you in Milwaukee at the World Series.”
Murphy’s reply said everything: “When’s that start?”
Next Friday, Oct. 23, at American Family Field, where Milwaukee holds home-field advantage thanks to its franchise-record 103 wins. The Guardians took a 2-1 ALCS lead over the Rays into Friday night's scheduled Game 4 at Progressive Field. Milwaukee, meanwhile, will have a full week to rest, which leaves plenty of time to watch and wonder.
Here’s a guide to each potential matchup. You decide which one you’d rather see.
If the regular season is a guide ...
It doesn’t tell us much. The Brewers went 2-1 against both teams.
Milwaukee won the first two games against Cleveland on June 16-17 before rookie left-hander Parker Messick struck out nine over six innings in the finale. Cleveland was without José Ramírez, Angel Martínez and Chase DeLauter. All three are back.
When the Brewers hit
Milwaukee’s lineup is built on pressure. The Brewers ranked in the top five in doubles, runs, hits, walks, batting average and on-base percentage.
That approach might get more of a test against Tampa Bay. The Rays issued the fewest walks in the Majors (409) and ranked second in defensive runs saved (87). Drawing walks and finding holes gets tougher against that combination. And their top starters have carried it into October: Drew Rasmussen has a 1.29 ERA through two postseason starts, while Peralta has allowed one earned run in 10 2/3 innings, including six shutout innings in Game 2 of the ALCS.
Cleveland offers a different challenge. Gavin Williams has been a monster, striking out 33 over 16 2/3 innings this postseason. The Guardians have a 2.54 ERA this October, slightly better than Tampa Bay’s 2.72. But Cleveland issued 530 regular-season walks to the Rays’ 409, giving Milwaukee more reason to believe its patient approach can create traffic.
When the other side hits
The regular-season numbers favor facing Cleveland. The Guardians had the lowest OPS (.696) and fewest runs (678) of any postseason team. Tampa Bay offered a more complete attack, with Junior Caminero’s 42 homers anchoring a lineup that tied for fifth in on-base percentage (.326).
October has told a different story. Through Thursday, Cleveland was averaging 4.25 runs per game with a .685 OPS, compared with Tampa Bay’s 3.00 runs and .563 OPS. The Guardians haven’t suddenly become an offensive powerhouse, but they’ve been more productive than the Rays, whose lineup managed just three hits in Game 3 of the ALCS.
The larger sample still points toward Cleveland as the preferable opponent. The way these teams are hitting right now makes that a tougher call.
The bullpens
Neither ninth inning looks inviting. Tampa Bay’s Bryan Baker has saved all four Rays wins this postseason without allowing a hit in four innings. Ian Seymour has been a strong bridge, allowing one earned run in 6 1/3 innings.
Cleveland counters with Cade Smith, who has allowed two hits and one run while striking out 13 in nine innings this October. Hunter Gaddis has added six scoreless innings across seven appearances. Both teams have arms capable of shortening games.
The Brewers have made a habit of coming back this postseason, and their bats have shown they can pick at a bullpen late. Against either opponent, getting a lead before the closer enters would make life easier.
What about the intangibles?
The Guardians’ championship drought dates to 1948. The Rays, like the Brewers, have never won a World Series.
The Rays mirror Milwaukee in many ways. Brewers president of baseball operations Matt Arnold worked in Tampa Bay’s front office alongside current Rays GM Erik Neander. Add Peralta facing his former team, and the storyline writes itself.
Cleveland manager Stephen Vogt played for Milwaukee and interviewed for the job that went to Murphy three years ago. And a Cleveland-Milwaukee World Series comes with a built-in movie reference: Major League, filmed in Milwaukee with Bob Uecker’s Harry Doyle calling Cleveland's improbable run.
The verdict
Give the Guardians a slight edge as Milwaukee’s preferred opponent, though their October bats have made that a tougher sell. The Rays were the more complete team over six months. Cleveland has spent the past two weeks making those six months feel a little less relevant.
The Brewers? They just sent the back-to-back champs home. They’ll let the AL sort this out. Somebody remind Murph what time Friday’s game starts.

item.content:encoded:
Milwaukee Brewers superstar Jackson Chourio is the odds-on favorite to win the World Series MVP in the 2026 Fall Classic.
The Brewers advanced to the World Series for the first time since 1982, when they took down the mighty Los Angeles Dodgers, the reigning two-time World Series champions, with an eye-opening 4-0 sweep in the NLCS.
It was an absolutely incredible performance by the Brewers, who are now four wins away from capturing the first World Series championship in franchise history.
If they do end up winning it, then the oddsmakers like Chourio’s chances to be a big part of them doing so.
Jackson Chourio Is the World Series MVP Favorite
Per DraftKings Sportsbook, Chourio is the odds-on favorite to win the World Series MVP award this season.
Chourio is currently at +600 odds, putting him just ahead of his Brewers teammates, C William Contreras at +650, SP Jacob Misiorowski at +700, and 2B Brice Turang at +900, to capture this year’s World Series MVP award.
Since the ALCS between the Cleveland Guardians and the Tampa Bay Rays has not yet been decided, the odds will change from now until the start of the World Series one week from now.
Still, Chourio will be among the favorites to capture the World Series MVP award when the Brewers try to win the first championship in club history.
Jackson Chourio Is a Young Stud
Just 22 years old, Chourio is a young stud who has proven that he is one of the best young players in MLB since making his debut in 2024.
This season, Chourio hit .291 with a .837 OPS and a 129 OPS+ for the Brewers, indicating that his bat was 29% above league average.
He also belted 25 home runs and racked up 4.9 bWAR for the Brewers, along with stealing 23 bases.
Defensively, he had a strong year in LF and is a finalist for the Gold Glove Award.
During the postseason this year, Chourio has struggled a bit with just a .171 batting average, .553 OPS, and two home runs in eight games. But that is a very small sample size, and the oddsmakers know that he can turn it on at any moment.

item.content:encoded:
As summer comes to a close and the air turns crisp, you know what's coming: the MLB Playoffs. The NFL season is already underway, and if you're also a baseball lover, this next month is essential viewing. The MLB has been through a number of changes in recent years. From the universal DH and the pitch clock to video replay and an automated strike zone, baseball may look very different if you haven't been paying attention.
Earlier today, the Guardians took on the Rays, and tonight, the Dodgers will go head-to-head against the Brewers in the best-of-seven Championship series. Which team will come out on top? Here's how you can watch live.
What Time Is the Los Angeles Dodgers vs. Milwaukee Brewers Game?
Today's game between the Dodgers and Brewers will take place on Thursday, October 15 at 9 p.m. ET.
How to Watch the Los Angeles Dodgers vs. Milwaukee Brewers?
Tonight's Dodgers vs. Brewers game will air on Fox and FS1. This year, the American League Division Series games will be broadcast on TBS, while the National League games will be on Fox and FS1. You can also watch them with a live TV or sports streaming subscription from DirecTV, Fox One, Fubo, HBO Max, Hulu, Sling, Sportsnet+ (if you're in Canada), or YouTube TV.
How to Watch the Dodgers vs. the Brewers for Free
If you don't want to subscribe to any of the above platforms, you may be able to sign up for a few free trials to gain access to this weekend's games. Fox One and Hulu offer three-day trials, DirecTV and Fubo offer five days, and YouTube TV gives you 10 days for free.
2026 MLB Playoffs Game Schedule
MLB's expanded postseason means more teams on the playoff schedule. Things started off with the best-of-three Wild Card Series, where the Braves, Padres, White Sox, and Yankees advanced. The best-of-five Division Series put them up against the Los Angeles Dodgers, Milwaukee Brewers, Cleveland Guardians, and Tampa Bay Rays, respectively. All of whom managed to advance
Now, the Rays and Guardians and Dodgers and Brewers meet in the best-of-seven Championship Series to determine the best team in each league. The winner from each league will then advance to a best-of-seven World Series to begin on October 23. Who will make it all the way?
Los Angeles Dodgers vs. Milwaukee Brewers - MIL lead 3-0
- Game 4 on October 15 @ 9 p.m. ET - Fox/FS1
- Game 5 on October 16 @ 9 p.m. ET - Fox/FS1*
- Game 6 on October 18 @ 8 p.m. ET - Fox/FS1*
- Game 7 on October 19 @ 8 p.m. ET - Fox/FS1*
Cleveland Guardians vs. Tampa Bay Rays - CLE leads 1-1
- Game 3 on October 15 @ 1 p.m. ET - TBS/HBO Max
- Game 4 on October 16 @ 6 p.m. ET - TBS/HBO Max
- Game 5 on October 17 @ 8 p.m. ET - TBS/HBO Max*
- Game 6 on October 19 @ 5 p.m. ET - TBS/HBO Max*
- Game 7 on October 20 @ 8 p.m. ET - TBS/HBO Max*
*if necessary
How to Stream the 2026 MLB Playoffs
This year's MLB postseason is stretched across multiple networks and streaming services. All Wild Card Series games for the American League and National League were broadcast on NBC, NBCSN, and Peacock. Additional rounds will be on other networks. ALDS and ALCS games are on TBS/TruTV and HBO Max, while NLDS and NLCS games are on Fox/FS1. For the World Series, all games will be broadcast on Fox and the Fox One streaming service.
- DirecTV: DirecTV's MySports base pack costs $45 per month for the first six months to see every game on Fox, FS1, NBC, and TBS/TruTV.
- Fox One: Fox's own streaming app lets you watch the NLDS, NLCS, and World Series on Fox and FS1 for $20 per month.

item.content:encoded:
The Philadelphia Phillies were eliminated from the MLB playoffs in the National League Wild Card Round.
The Atlanta Braves beat the Phillies 2-1 in the Wild Card Series at Truist Park.
The Braves have since been eliminated. Currently the Milwaukee Brewers hold a 3-0 lead over the Los Angeles Dodgers in the National League Championship Series, and the Cleveland Guardians hold a 2-1 lead over the Tampa Bay Rays in the American League Championship Series.
Amid the ALCS and NLCS, Phillies president of baseball operations Dave Dombrowski met with the media. During the session, Dombrowski announced news involving Bryce Harper and Kyle Schwarber.
Philadelphia Phillies Announce Bryce Harper, Kyle Schwarber Updates After Playoff Elimination
ATLANTA, GEORGIA – SEPTEMBER 30: Kyle Schwarber #12 of the Philadelphia Phillies celebrates a home run with Bryce Harper #3 of the Philadelphia Phillies against the Atlanta Braves during the eighth inning in game two of the National League Wild Card Series at Truist Park on September 30, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images)
Dombrowski said that Harper will be the full-time first baseman in 2027, according to Justin Heinze of Patch.com.
The Phillies’ POBO also said that Schwarber is expected to get more reps at first base to help manage Harper’s workload.
PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA – MAY 06: Bryce Harper #3 high fives Kyle Schwarber #12 of the Philadelphia Phillies after a run in the eighth inning against the Athletics at Citizens Bank Park on May 06, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images)
Harper began the 2026 season as the Phillies’ starting first baseman.
However, the Phillies had Harper play some right field, his old position, after they acquired second baseman Luis Arraez at the trade deadline.
SEATTLE, WASHINGTON – AUGUST 25: Bryce Harper #3 of the Philadelphia Phillies makes a catch for an out during the eighth inning against the Seattle Mariners at T-Mobile Park on August 25, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images)
Acquiring Arraez led to Bryson Stott moving to third base and Alec Bohm taking more reps at first base.
The Arraez acquisition also led to Schwarber getting some reps at first base. The primary DH appeared in eight games at DH this past season. He also appeared in two games at left field.
Looking at Bryce Harper’s 2026 Season
NEW YORK, NEW YORK – JUNE 27: Bryce Harper #3 of the Philadelphia Phillies catches a throw to first during the first inning against the New York Mets at Citi Field on June 27, 2026 in New York City. (Photo by Caleb Bowlin/Getty Images)
Harper posted 3.3 fWAR and a .269/.380/.485 (135 wRC+) slash line with 29 home runs and 87 RBI over 162 games in 2026.
Defensively, Harper posted 0 Defensive Runs Saved and -5 Outs Above Average over 923 2/3 innings at first base. In right field, Harper recorded -5 DRS and -3 OAA over 363 2/3 innings.
Harper went 3-for-13 with a home run and a double in the Wild Card Series against Atlanta.
Looking at Kyle Schwarber’s 2026 Season
ATLANTA, GEORGIA – OCTOBER 01: Kyle Schwarber #12 of the Philadelphia Phillies walks to first base against the Atlanta Braves during the fourth inning in game three of the National League Wild Card Series at Truist Park on October 01, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images)
Schwarber posted 2.9 fWAR and a .232/.354/.503 (130 wRC+) slash line with 45 home runs and 97 RBI over 156 regular-season games in 2026.
During the Wild Card Series, Schwarber went 4-for-11 with a home run and two walks.

item.title: [MLB.com] LIVE: Brewers-Dodgers NLCS Game 4 (FS1/FOX One)
item.dc:creator: Sonja Chen; Adam McCalvy; AJ Cassavell
item.description: Milwaukee brings a commanding 3-0 lead into Game 4 of the National League Championship Series on Thursday night. item.content:encoded:
Milwaukee brings a commanding 3-0 lead into Game 4 of the National League Championship Series on Thursday night. But the Dodgers are the champs until they’re not, and they’ve faced plenty of adversity on their way to World Series titles in each of the past two seasons.
Never like this though. In all best-of-seven postseason series, teams with a 3-0 lead have gone on to win that series 41 times out of 42 -- with 32 of those series ending as sweeps. Only two teams have ever even forced a Game 7 after trailing 3-0, and only the 2004 Red Sox, in the ALCS against the Yankees, have come all the way back to win.
“It's certainly possible,” said Dodgers manager Dave Roberts, himself a fabled part of that Red Sox rally. “I've lived it. And I think the thing is that our guys have been battle-tested. … It's an elimination game. We've played in a lot of elimination games. We've just got to get a win.”
While the Dodgers chase baseball history, the Brewers can make a bit of their own with a win on Thursday. A year ago, they were swept by the Dodgers in the very same round. If they can return the favor, they would become the first team to be swept out of the playoffs, only to sweep the same team -- in any postseason series -- a year later. But they’re not getting ahead of themselves.
“We have yet to complete anything,” Brewers outfielder Jackson Chourio said through an interpreter. “The job's not finished for us. So we have to come with the same mentality. Which is to win.”
Here’s what you need to know about Game 4:
When is the game and how can I watch it?
Game 4 is currently airing nationally on FS1.
All series are available in the US on MLB.TV with authentication to a participating Pay TV provider. Games also are available live internationally, although not in Canada. Sportsnet is MLB's exclusive English language broadcaster in Canada for every Postseason game, while TVA Sports will be covering the entire AL Postseason and the World Series in French and Broadcaster RDS will cover the entire NL Postseason in French.
The Brewers picked Drohan from among a plethora of fresh options to start what amounts to a bullpen game. Left-handers Kyle Harrison and Drohan and right-hander Chad Patrick have been on the roster for both the NLDS and NLCS, but have yet to pitch in any of the Brewers’ first seven games. Midseason pickup Dustin May, the former Dodger who won a World Series ring with L.A. in 2020, pitched an inning in NLCS Game 2 on what would have been a bullpen day had he been lined up to start Thursday. They are all options to come in behind Drohan, who had a 4.19 ERA in 33 games/19 starts and shifted to the bullpen late in the season when he came upon a loose innings limit. He thrived in short stints, posting a 1.47 ERA as a reliever. It will be his career postseason debut.
The Dodgers' 7-0 postseason record when Glasnow pitches is more of a quirk than anything else, but the right-hander has gotten the results to back it up. In four starts and three relief appearances, Glasnow has recorded a 1.73 ERA (five earned runs in 26 innings). Glasnow had command issues when he last pitched against the Braves in NLDS Game 4 -- issuing five walks -- but limited the damage to one run in 4 2/3 innings.
What are the starting lineups?
Brewers: The lineup the Brewers used against right-hander Yoshinobu Yamamoto in Game 2 produced the second postseason game in franchise history in which five different players tallied multiple hits. Against Glasnow in Game 4, they hope for a similar result with the same group.
Dodgers: Not only are the Dodgers sticking with Shohei Ohtani despite his lingering right biceps and left knee issues, they're bumping him up to leadoff for a must-win game. He and a scuffling Will Smith -- batting cleanup for Game 4 -- were dropped in the lineup in the past couple games, but the fact that both contributed to L.A.'s lone run-scoring rally in Game 3 likely played a role in Roberts' decision to elevate them Thursday.
How will the bullpens line up after the starter?
Brewers: Right-handed setup man Abner Uribe, who has appeared in each of the first seven games of the postseason, finally wilted a bit in Game 3, walking three batters ahead of Smith’s two-run double in the sixth inning. But left-hander DL Hall kept the game on track by stopping the rally there and recording seven enormous outs. Then Trevor Megill logged a four-out save. That’s a lot of work for those last two arms, so lefty Aaron Ashby figures to play a prominent role in Game 4 if the score is tight.
Dodgers: It's all hands on deck, with the possible exception of Justin Wrobleski, who threw 32 pitches to cover the final 1 2/3 innings of Game 3. Roberts made a point of saying that he will get closer Edwin Díaz --- the only Dodgers reliever who has not pitched this series -- into Game 4.
Any injuries of note?
Brewers: None.
Dodgers: Ohtani (right biceps, left knee) and Freeman (right knee) are managing lingering injuries. World Series hero Will Klein (right elbow discomfort) has faced hitters, but he has not pitched in a game since July 31 and is viewed as more of a depth option. Blake Treinen (right shoulder inflammation) is unlikely to pitch this postseason.
Who is hot and who is not?
Brewers: Chourio’s .642 OPS in this postseason doesn’t tell anything about his impact. His leadoff home run in Game 3 marked his second homer of the 2026 postseason and sixth of his career, breaking a brief tie with William Contreras for the most homers in Brewers’ postseason history. Three of them have led off a postseason game, which matched Hall of Famer Derek Jeter, Jimmy Rollins and Ohtani for the second-most in history, trailing only Kyle Schwarber, who has five leadoff home runs in the postseason. And with his 18th career postseason RBI, Chourio also broke a tie with Hall of Famer Andruw Jones for the most postseason RBIs prior to a player’s 23rd birthday. … With his eighth-inning base hit, Contreras became the first Brewers player with 10 hits in this postseason.
Dodgers: Tucker (.304) has consistently swung the bat well through seven games, but he has been the exception to the rule for a cold Dodgers offense. In Game 3, Ohtani (113.5 mph single) and Smith (two-run double) showed some positive signs, but they have been L.A.'s most notable slumping bats this postseason.
Anything else fans might want to know?
•  Orel Hershiser and Mike Scioscia will throw out the ceremonial first pitch and say, "It's time for Dodger baseball!" as part of the pregame ceremonies.
• According to the Elias Sports Bureau, this is the eighth time two teams met in the postseason one year after one swept the other in the previous postseason. The only team to be swept and then win a rematch the following postseason is the 1923 Yankees, who won that year's World Series over the New York Giants in six games.
• Brewers owner Mark Attanasio said it struck him that it’s been 44 years since the Brewers made it to the World Series, and 44 is one of the franchise’s retired numbers for Hall of Famer Hank Aaron. This year marked the 50th anniversary of Aaron’s 755th and final home run, which he hit while playing for the Brewers in 1976.
• This marks the sixth time a team has taken a 3-0 series lead against the reigning World Series champion in a best-of-seven series. Four of the previous five -- 1990 WS, Reds vs A’s; 1966 WS, Orioles vs Dodgers; 1963 WS, Dodgers vs Yankees; 1914 WS, Boston Braves vs Philadelphia Athletics -- ended in a sweep. The other (2017 NLCS, Dodgers vs Cubs) concluded with the Dodgers winning in five games.

item.content:encoded:
The Philadelphia Phillies were eliminated from the MLB playoffs by the Atlanta Braves in the National League Wild Card Series.
The Braves won Games 1 and 3, and the Phillies won Game 2.
The Braves have since been eliminated. Four teams remain in the playoffs. The Milwaukee Brewers have a 3-0 lead over the Los Angeles Dodgers in the NLCS, and the Cleveland Guardians and Tampa Bay Rays are tied 1-1 in the ALCS.
During the Championship Series, the Phillies announced news involving shortstop Trea Turner.
Philadelphia Phillies’ Dave Dombrowski Announces Trea Turner News After Early Playoff Exit
ATLANTA, GEORGIA – SEPTEMBER 30: Trea Turner #7 of the Philadelphia Phillies runs the bases during the first inning against the Atlanta Braves in game two of the National League Wild Card Series at Truist Park on September 30, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images)
“He did not have a good year. He needs to fix things with his swing. He knows he has to be better at shortstop. I told him that is mandatory. I told him he cannot play shortstop like he did in 2026, going into 2027.”
Dave Dombrowski told him if he plays shortstop like he did in 2026, then he won’t be playing shortstop. Trea will be working with Carlos Mendoza.
Dave says Turner prefers the infield.
Sounds like Turner will be moved from shortstop if it is not going well in spring training
Trea Turner does not think he had a good season. He takes complete accountability. He is already working on his swing.
Turner flew back into town to speak with Dave Dombrowski for a few hours
Looking at Trea Turner
PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA – SEPTEMBER 25: Trea Turner #7 of the Philadelphia Phillies reacts after a strikeout in the fourth inning during a game against the Tampa Bay Rays at Citizens Bank Park on September 25, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images)
Turner arguably had the worst season of his career in 2026.
The shortstop hit .242/.297/.378 with 19 home runs and 58 RBI over 157 games. He recorded -17 Defensive Runs Saved and -8 Outs Above Average over 1,343 1/3 innings at shortstop.
PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA – SEPTEMBER 24: Trea Turner #7 of the Philadelphia Phillies looks on during a game against the Milwaukee Brewers at Citizens Bank Park on September 24, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images)
Turner signed an 11-year, $300 million contract with the Phillies in the 2022-23 offseason.
He accumulated 14.4 fWAR in his first three seasons with the Phillies. This year, he posted just 1.1 fWAR.
Turner began his career with the Washington Nationals in 2015.
The Nationals traded Turner to the Los Angeles Dodgers at the 2021 trade deadline. He played for Los Angeles through the 2022 season then signed his deal with Philadelphia.
Throughout his MLB career, Turner has posted 48.4 fWAR. He is a World Series Champion and a three-time All-Star.

item.title: [MLB.com] Rays-Guardians ALCS Game 3 FAQ, lineups (1 ET, TBS/HBO Max)
item.dc:creator: Tim Stebbins; Keegan Matheson; Adam Berry
item.description: CLEVELAND -- It’s a new day in the ALCS, as the Rays and Guardians have shifted their matchup back to Cleveland tied up at 1-1. The Rays' 3-1 win in Game 2 shifted this series back into focus after the Guardians pulled off a 7-3 come-from-behind win in the opener. item.content:encoded:
CLEVELAND -- It’s a new day in the ALCS, as the Rays and Guardians have shifted their matchup back to Cleveland tied up at 1-1.
The Rays' 3-1 win in Game 2 shifted this series back into focus after the Guardians pulled off a 7-3 come-from-behind win in the opener. We’ve seen each team’s best, and as these pitching staffs get stretched even thinner as the series wears on, they’ll need to lean on the identities they’ve built in 2026.
“It’s going to be a challenging place to play,” said Rays manager Kevin Cash. “We played there not too long ago in the postseason. That's as good an atmosphere as you're going to see. They've got a great fan base that's going to be behind their team. I'd like to think we can carry our momentum into there and just play good baseball for Game 3.”
Step back a few feet for a wider view, and this Guardians team has still won four of its past five games. The club ran into a Game 2 buzzsaw named Freddy Peralta, whose fastball was nearly unhittable, but Cleveland is still in an excellent spot after stealing Game 1.
“We feel great. Obviously we would have loved to have taken [Game 2],” Guardians manager Stephen Vogt said. “That would have been really big. And we had our position and our opportunities to do that. But going home 1-1, to go have three games in front of our fans in Cleveland, we feel really good about that. And we're excited to get it going.”
The pitching matchup has the potential to lean in the Guardians’ favor, too, with Gavin Williams starting on regular rest, fresh off a dominant outing against the White Sox to clinch the ALDS. For the Rays, Griffin Jax has been officially named the starter, and while he spent the majority of the season working in a true starter’s role, he pitched two innings of relief against the Yankees in Game 3 of the ALDS, throwing just 32 pitches.
This series is still waiting for its first show-stopping moment, too, with all eyes on José Ramírez for the Guardians and Junior Caminero for the Rays. Ramírez's series has been up-and-down so far, from a solid Game 1 to a crucial error that opened the door in Game 2, while Caminero is still searching for his first career postseason home run.
There’s history on the line here, too, for whichever team advances to represent the American League in the World Series. The Rays haven’t won the World Series since entering the league in 1998 and have only reached the big stage twice (2008, 2020). The Guardians, on the other hand, still carry the weight of the longest World Series drought in the big leagues at 77 seasons, stretching all the way back to 1948.
When is the game and how can I watch it?
First pitch for Game 3 of the Rays-Guardians American League Championship Series is scheduled for 1 p.m. ET on Thursday at Progressive Field. Due to inclement weather in the forecast, the original start time of 6 p.m. was moved up. The game will be broadcast on TBS and HBO Max. 
Spanish-language game broadcasts will be available on UniMas for the ALCS, and Spanish-language radio broadcasts will be available on Univision’s TUDN Radio.
Who are the starting pitchers?
Rays: Griffin Jax, RHP
Key Stats: 0.90 ERA over his past five appearances
Nick Martinez started ALDS Game 3 for the Rays, but they will turn to Jax this time after using him as a reliever against the Yankees, with Martinez likely in line to pitch Game 4 on Friday. Jax has been excellent since a rough return from the injured list on Sept. 2 after a bout of right elbow discomfort, permitting only two runs on 10 hits and four walks while striking out 19 in 20 innings over his last four regular-season starts and his Game 3 relief outing at Yankee Stadium. Jax is presumably prepared for Cleveland’s inclement weather, having pitched for Minnesota for most of his career, and he’s put up impressive numbers (including a 2.19 ERA, 0.89 WHIP and 20 strikeouts) in 13 relief appearances at Progressive Field.
Guardians: Gavin Williams, RHP
Key Stats: 1.54 ERA, 24 strikeouts in 11 2/3 innings in ALDS
The Guardians officially named Williams their Game 3 starter on Wednesday afternoon, setting the 27-year-old up for a start on normal rest following his heroic performance in the ALDS, when he made two starts and an emergency relief appearance against the White Sox. After he recorded the final three outs of Game 4, Williams came back on one day’s rest in Game 5 and tied a franchise postseason record in strikeouts (12) to help Cleveland beat Chicago, 2-0, to advance. Williams starting Game 3 also positions him to start a potential Game 7 of this series on Tuesday, on normal rest.
What are the starting lineups?
Rays: With Williams on the mound, the Rays are going with their standard lineup against right-handers, with the “Big Three” followed by their other left-handed hitters. They're staying with Jonny DeLuca, who’s started every postseason game so far, over Cedric Mullins in center field.
Guardians: Patrick Bailey is back behind the plate in Game 3. He and Williams have been a customary battery this season, and Bailey is swinging a hot bat this postseason. The Guards are sticking with the standard lineup they’ve had in this series.
How will the bullpens line up after the starter?
Guardians: Vogt will have a full bullpen at his disposal after the off-day, and will work getting the ball to closer Cade Smith. He and Hunter Gaddis did not appear in Game 2, after both pitched in each of the Guardians’ first six contests this postseason. Setup man Erik Sabrowski also did not pitch in Game 2 and will be working off two days’ rest.
Rays: The Rays should be in good shape after Wednesday’s off-day, although this will be the first time since the regular season that they’ve played three consecutive days in a row. Left-hander Ian Seymour has clearly established himself as a top setup option in front of closer Bryan Baker, and lefty Cam Booser has also been tasked with getting big outs against left-handed hitters. Right-hander Kevin Kelly and Tyler Wells are also setup options in front of Baker, who has recorded the save in each of Tampa Bay’s four wins this postseason.
Any injuries of note?
Guardians: None.
Rays: Caminero and DeLuca said they were fine after a nasty collision while chasing a foul ball in Game 1. Left-hander Shane McClanahan, who finished the regular season on the injured list due to left forearm tightness, was shut down for the rest of the postseason, Cash said on Sunday. Otherwise, nothing new.
Who is hot and who is not?
Guardians: Shawn Armstrong has allowed just one hit and struck out five batters in 5 1/3 scoreless innings over four postseason appearances. It’s been an impressive comeback after he missed two months with a left calf strain, before returning the final week of the regular season. DeLauter is hitting .346 (9-for-26) with just one strikeout in seven postseason games.
Rocchio is hitting .091 (2-for-22) in seven games.
Rays: Pretty much everyone who touched the mound for Tampa Bay in the ALDS and Game 2 of this series performed well, which is certainly promising for the team moving forward, even after some shaky bullpen work in Game 1. The Rays are starting to find some rhythm at the plate, too, with Caminero leading the way despite not yet having the big moment everyone’s expecting. Hicks drove in a couple runs in Game 2, and DeLuca had his second straight multihit game. Díaz is just 5-for-21 in the playoffs, and Mesa is only 3-for-18.
Anything else fans might want to know?
• Cleveland Cavaliers guard Donovan Mitchell will throw the ceremonial first pitch before Game 3.
• With his fifth-inning single in Game 2, Ramírez moved into second place in franchise history in postseason hits (49), breaking a tie with Kenny Lofton. Omar Vizquel (57) ranks first.
• Game 2 of the ALCS was Díaz’s 30th postseason game with the Rays, matching Evan Longoria for the most in franchise history. Game 3 should give Tampa Bay’s DH the club record.
• The Rays are 89-0 this year, including the regular season and postseason, when leading after eight innings. The last team to go a full year with a 1.000 winning percentage and at least 89 wins when leading after eight innings? The 2022 Mets, who went 90-0. The last team to do so in the AL was the 2002 Athletics (93-0).

item.content:encoded:
The 2026 MLB playoffs are in full swing!
The 12-team postseason began with an action-packed wild-card round that featured eight teams battling for four spots to advance to the eight-team division series.
The Chicago White Sox became the first team to win a series this postseason with a wild-card round sweep of the Houston Astros. Then the New York Yankees swept the Boston Red Sox in two routs, recording the highest series run differential in the history of the current wild-card format. The San Diego Padresalso sealed their spot in the NLDS with a sweep of the Chicago Cubs. In the only wild-card series to go the distance, the Atlanta Braves held off the Philadelphia Philliesto move on.
The Los Angeles Dodgers beat the Braves to nab the first spot in the championship series, where they are facing the Milwaukee Brewers after they beat the Padres.
The Tampa Bay Rays swept the Yankees to clinch the first spot in the ALCS and face the Cleveland Guardians, who mounted a stunning comeback against the White Sox after dropping the first two games of the ALDS.
From the first pitch of the wild-card games to the last out of the World Series, we've got you covered with the postseason bracket, schedules, results and how to watch every game this October.

item.title: [MLB.com] Each team's all-time postseason home run leader
item.dc:creator: Jared Greenspan; Max Ralph

item.content:encoded:
After setting a franchise record with an MLB-best 103 wins in the 2026 regular season, the Brewers are vying for their first World Series appearance since 1982, which remains the only trip to the fall classic in franchise history.
Chourio pounced on the first pitch of Game 3 of the National League Championship Series from Dodgers left-hander Blake Snell, parking it over the right-center-field fence for a home run. It was his sixth career postseason dinger at just 22 years old, breaking a tie with Contreras -- who has three long balls in the 2026 playoffs -- for the most in Brewers postseason history.
With both in mind, who is each team’s all-time postseason home run king? Here’s a breakdown of the players who hold a franchise’s playoff home run record.
American League East
Blue Jays: Vladimir Guerrero Jr. -- 8
Vladdy put together one of the single greatest individual postseason performances we’ve ever seen in 2025, leading the Blue Jays all the way to Game 7 of the World Series. After starting his postseason career with six homer-less games, Guerrero hit all eight of his October long balls in ‘25. He surpassed José Bautista (six) for the most home runs in Blue Jays playoff history. The dinger that earned Guerrero the franchise lead came off of Shohei Ohtani in the World Series, no less.
Orioles: Frank Robinson -- 9
The Hall of Famer had a knack for the clutch. Robinson's 26 career walk-off hits (regular season and postseason) are the most by any player since RBI became official in 1920. That knack extended to the playoffs, where Robinson posted an .887 OPS and slammed 10 total homers, including a franchise-best nine with the Orioles. Robinson won World Series MVP in 1966 after hitting go-ahead home runs in Games 1 and 4 of a Baltimore sweep over the Dodgers.
Rays: Randy Arozarena -- 11
Arozarena put the Rays on his back in the 2020 postseason, recording 29 hits -- at the time the most in a single postseason. Ten of those hits were home runs, giving Arozarena another single-postseason record and pulling him ahead of Evan Longoria (nine) for the most playoff homers in Rays franchise history. Oh, and Arozarena did all of this as a rookie. He tagged one more postseason big fly with the Rays in '21 before joining the Mariners via trade in 2024.
Red Sox: David Ortiz -- 17
Big Papi was an October legend in the truest sense of the phrase. His walk-off heroics helped the Red Sox overcome a 3-0 series deficit in the 2004 ALCS, paving the way for a curse-breaking World Series title. Ortiz’s 17 playoff home runs included two walk-offs and six with the Red Sox facing elimination.
Yankees: Bernie Williams -- 22
Williams played in the postseason in 12 consecutive years from 1995-2006, with huge moments at several turns. His 1996 performance -- an 1.142 OPS with six homers -- is one of the best postseasons of all time. Overall, his 22 long balls are fifth most by any player in playoff history, sharing a list with other Yankees legends like Derek Jeter (20) and Mickey Mantle (18).
AL Central
Guardians: Jim Thome -- 17
Thome hit all 17 of his postseason homers with Cleveland. He’s one of three players with multiple postseason grand slams, along with Francisco Lindor and Jason Varitek. Thome's grand slams came in Game 6 of the 1998 ALCS against the Yankees and Game 2 of the 1999 ALDS against the Red Sox.
Royals: George Brett -- 10
Brett is one of just 12 players who have hit three home runs in a single postseason game. His herculean effort came in Game 3 of the 1978 ALCS against the Yankees. Even though in defeat, Brett memorably whacked three pitches over the fence, one out to left field, one over the center-field fence, and one to right field.
Tigers: Miguel Cabrera -- 9
Cabrera’s most memorable postseason may have come as a rookie with the championship-winning Marlins in 2003 (more on that soon). But his most impactful playoff performance happened in 2011, when he launched four home runs with a 1.261 OPS in 11 games for the Tigers. He later passed Delmon Young’s eight career playoff home runs as a Tiger with a solo shot in Game 1 of the 2014 ALDS.
Twins: Kirby Puckett -- 5
Goose Goslin is the Twins' franchise leader in postseason home runs with seven, but Puckett holds the record since the club moved to Minnesota in 1961. Puckett took two trips to the postseason with the Twins, winning the World Series both times (1987 and 1991). The Hall of Famer was particularly impactful in ‘91, when he hit four dingers on an overall .333/.396/.667 slash line. That included an iconic 11th-inning walk-off homer in Game 6 of the Fall Classic.
White Sox: Paul Konerko -- 7
Konerko mashed five of his seven postseason homers during Chicago's 2005 title run, narrowly besting teammate Paul Crede (four HR) for the franchise lead. Konerko hit two of his long balls while earning ALCS MVP honors, then later launched a go-ahead grand slam in Game 2 of the World Series to down the Astros.
AL West
Angels: Troy Glaus -- 9
Glaus hit seven of his nine postseason homers with the Angels during the club's World Series campaign in 2022. Three of those were go-ahead long balls in the sixth inning or later, which is tied with the Astros' Yordan Alvarez (2022) for the most such home runs in a single postseason.
Athletics: José Canseco -- 7
In addition to holding the club's all-time postseason home run record, Canseco holds a share of the record for the most homers in a single postseason by an A's player. He slugged four big flies in 1988, helping lead the Athletics to the AL Pennant. Two years later, Canseco passed Al Simmons for the most postseason home runs in A's franchise history with a dinger in Game 2 of the 1990 World Series.
Astros: Jose Altuve -- 28
Altuve added to his stature as one of baseball's best postseason hitters in 2026. He clubbed a solo shot in Game 2 of the AL Wild Card Series against the White Sox, putting him one home run behind Manny Ramirez for most all-time. And Altuve tends to meet the moment, too: A whopping 14 of his playoff homers have been of the game-tying or go-ahead variety, the most such homers in postseason history.
Mariners: Jay Buhner and Edgar Martinez -- 8
Buhner and Martinez each starred for the Mariners during the most successful era in franchise history, as the club made the playoffs four times between 1994 and 2001. Buhner took the early lead in career postseason homers, hitting four in ‘95 and two more in ‘97. But Martinez caught up to his longtime teammate in 2001 with a pair of long balls in the 2001 ALDS.
Rangers: Nelson Cruz -- 14
Cruz authored a historic postseason moment when he hit the first walk-off grand slam in postseason history in Game 2 of the 2011 ALCS against the Tigers. It remains one of just two walk-off postseason slams after Dodgers first baseman Freddie Freeman also accomplished the feat in Game 1 of the 2024 World Series. Cruz, the owner of 464 regular-season home runs, hit his last postseason homer at age 41 with the Rays, becoming the second-oldest player to go yard in a playoff game.
National League East
Braves: Chipper Jones -- 13
Jones starred for an Atlanta team that made 11 consecutive postseason appearances from 1995-2005. The eight-time All-Star broke onto the October stage in a big way in ‘95, slugging two home runs -- including the game-winning shot in the ninth inning -- in a 5-4 win over the Rockies in Game 1 of the NLDS. Jones and Austin Riley are the only two players in Braves history with multiple go-ahead homers in the eighth inning or later of a postseason game.
Marlins: Miguel Cabrera -- 4
A 20-year-old, baby-faced Cabrera looked at home in his first postseason in 2003, steering the Florida Marlins to the franchise’s second World Series title. Cabrera launched four home runs in the ‘03 playoffs -- his only with the Marlins -- which stands as the most home runs in a single postseason at age 20 or younger in MLB history. With a long ball off Yankees right-hander Roger Clemens in Game 4 of the World Series, Cabrera became the second youngest player to go yard in the Fall Classic.
Mets: Daniel Murphy -- 7
All seven of Murphy’s playoff home runs with the Mets came during a magical two-week stretch in 2015. The second baseman homered in six straight postseason games -- spanning Game 4 of the NLDS through Game 4 of the NLCS -- to steer the Mets to the NL Pennant. That’s the longest streak in a single postseason in MLB history. Even more impressive, Murphy homered off three former Cy Young winners: Clayton Kershaw, Zack Greinke and Jake Arrieta.
Nationals: Bryce Harper, Juan Soto, Anthony Rendon and Ryan Zimmerman -- 5
Four of the most iconic players in Nationals franchise history (since the team moved from Montreal to Washington) share this distinction. Youth is a popular theme here. At 19 years old and 362 days, Harper became the second-youngest player in MLB history to homer in a postseason game when he went deep in Game 5 of the 2012 NLDS. Seven years later, Soto (20 years, 346 days) became the sixth-youngest player to homer in the playoffs, teeing off for a two-run shot in Game 3 of the 2019 NLDS.
Phillies: Kyle Schwarber -- 13
Schwarber is one of the most prolific power hitters in playoff history: His 24 career playoff home runs rank third most all time, trailing only Ramirez and Altuve. He’s crushed 15 homers in a Phillies uniform, the latest being a 447-foot shot in Game 2 of the 2026 NL Wild Card Series against the Braves. In 2022, Schwarber keyed a stirring run to the World Series with three home runs in the NLCS against the Padres and three more dingers in the Fall Classic against the Astros.
NL Central
Brewers: Jackson Chourio -- 6
Chourio tattooed a pair of home runs to help the Brewers stave off elimination in Game 2 of the 2024 NL Wild Card Series, becoming the second-youngest player in postseason history with a multi-HR game (20 years & 205 days). He’s the only player in postseason history with a leadoff home run under age 22 -- which he’s done three times -- and the only player in MLB history with six playoff home runs before turning 23. Chourio's leadoff dinger off Blake Snell in Game 3 of the NLCS against the Dodgers as his latest feat of strength.
Cardinals: Albert Pujols -- 13
Who else but The Machine? Pujols slugged 19 career playoff home runs -- T-7th most all time -- including 13 with the Cardinals. The future Hall of Famer tagged Randy Johnson for his first career playoff homer in Game 2 of the 2001 NLDS, a surefire sign of things to come. Pujols is one of just 12 players to go deep three times in a postseason game, doing so in Game 3 of the 2011 World Series. He also launched one of the most iconic home runs in franchise history with a go-ahead, three-run shot onto the train tracks in Houston off All-Star closer Brad Lidge in Game 5 of the 2005 NLCS.
Cubs: Kris Bryant, Anthony Rizzo and Kyle Schwarber -- 6
Talk about a fitting trio: These three All-Stars propelled the Cubs to a curse-breaking, legacy-defining World Series title in 2016. Bryant (2) and Rizzo (1) each launched home runs in the Fall Classic, keying victories in Games 5 and 6 to spur a historic 3-1 series comeback. Schwarber, one of the best postseason power hitters of all time, launched six of his 24 playoff homers with the Cubs, including five dingers in his introduction to playoff baseball in 2015.
Pirates: Willie Stargell -- 7
The Hall of Fame slugger managed just two home runs while hitting .217 across his first 26 postseason games, spanning five different playoff appearances. But Stargell flipped the script in his age-39 season in 1979, smashing five home runs while earning NLCS and World Series MVP honors. Stargell’s two-run blast in the sixth inning of Game 7 of the ‘79 World Series proved to be the World Series-winning hit.
Reds: Johnny Bench -- 10
Bench played in 10 postseason series across his illustrious 17-year career and, rather remarkably, homered in all but one of them -- only going without a long ball in the 1975 NLCS. The Hall of Fame catcher’s only multi-HR playoff series came in the 1976 Fall Classic, when he swatted a pair of homers, posted a 1.667 OPS and took home World Series MVP honors for the Big Red Machine.
NL West
D-backs: Chris Young -- 5
Young only played in 12 postseason games for Arizona, but that was plenty of time to rewrite the franchise record books. His leadoff home run in Game 3 of the 2007 NLDS against the Cubs’ Rich Hill accounts for the only leadoff home run in D-backs franchise history. Four years later, Young slammed a pair of long balls in Game 4 of the NLDS against the Brewers. It remains the only multi-HR game by a Diamondbacks’ hitter in franchise history.
Dodgers: Max Muncy -- 19
Muncy homered three times in the 2026 NLDS against the Braves, pushing his total to 19 playoff home runs and extending the most in Dodgers postseason history. It’s a remarkable record for Muncy to hold, given his journey: He first joined the Dodgers organization on a Minor League contract in 2017, after he was released by the Athletics. The three-time All-Star owns some of the most important home runs in Dodgers history. That includes his 18th-inning walk-off in Game 3 of the 2018 World Series and his eighth-inning home run in Game 7 of the 2025 Fall Classic, which set the stage for a stirring late-game comeback.
Giants: Barry Bonds -- 8
Bonds made the postseason only four times in 15 seasons with the Giants. And while he launched more home runs (756) than anyone in baseball history, Bonds actually was held without a home run in three of those four trips to October. All eight of his playoff home runs with San Francisco came in 2002, when he posted a 1.559 OPS in 17 games while leading the Giants to the NL Pennant. The most memorable occurred in the ninth inning of Game 2 of the World Series, when he clobbered a blast to right field off closer Troy Percival. Arozarena (10, 2020 Rays) is the only player with more home runs in a single postseason.
Padres: Manny Machado -- 9
Machado extended his own franchise record in his first at-bat of the 2026 postseason, launching a home run in the first inning of Game 1 of the NL Wild Card Series against the Cubs’ Matthew Boyd. Machado ushered in a new era of baseball in San Diego when he signed a 10-year deal ahead of the 2019 season, and the Padres have made the playoffs in five of the eight years since. The seven-time All-Star was at his best in the 2022 playoffs, helping San Diego win a pair of postseason series thanks to four home runs in 12 games.
Rockies: Matt Holliday -- 5
Holliday is responsible for one of the defining moments in Rockies history, although it has nothing to do with a home run: He belly-flopped into home plate to score the game-winning run in Game 163 in 2007, giving Colorado the Wild Card tiebreaker over San Diego. That mad dash set the stage for Holliday's only postseason stint with the club, which was wildly successful. The seven-time All-Star homered in each of his first two playoff games in the NLDS against the Phillies, and wound up with five long balls as the Rockies earned the franchise’s first World Series berth.

item.title: [MLB.com] 11 on 11: Why José (NOT J-Ram!) is Cleveland's brightest star
item.dc:creator: Anthony Castrovince

item.content:encoded:
Well, OK, Guardians fans know it. And even casual fans know by now that Ramírez is a dynamic player. The "underrated" label has long since stopped applying to this seven-time All-Star.
With Ramírez’s Guardians in an ALCS that continues with Game 3 on Thursday night at Progressive Field, it’s a good time to share some fun and fascinating elements of his story that many fans might not be aware of. Though the prevailing narrative at this moment is his rare defensive miscue that opened the doors to the Rays’ win in Game 2, Ramírez is the primary reason the Guardians are in the ALCS in the first place, and his talent and personality are worth celebrating.
Here are -- appropriately, for the man who wears No. 11 for Cleveland -- 11 things every baseball fan should know about José Ramírez.
1) He hates being called 'J-Ram'
Let’s get this one out of the way right away. “J-Ram” is anathema to Ramírez, who is far too dynamic for such a dull nickname anyway.
If you must use a folksy nickname, “Hosey” works. But in Cleveland, Ramírez doesn’t need a nickname or a last name. He’s simply “José” (and it sounds best when sung to the stadium anthem “Ole! Ole! Ole!”).
2) He’s put the Guardians on his back
It’s funny to think that, a little more than a week ago, people were questioning Ramírez’s October clutchness. He had an injury-riddled regular season and struggled through Game 2 of the ALDS against the White Sox, with the Guardians down 0-2.
Be it the stakes or the crowd riding him, something snapped in Game 3. From that point on, he went 5-for-12 with five runs scored, seven RBIs, two homers, a double and a triple over three games. In the Game 5 clincher at home, he somehow golfed a curveball virtually in the dirt for a career-defining home run, then followed it up with a three-hit night in Cleveland’s Game 1 win in the ALCS.
As teammate Chase DeLauter put it: "He's the G.O.A.T. … When he comes out and has that kind of fire, it lights all of us up.”
3) He’s a likely future Hall of Famer
The postseason was the one element lacking from Ramírez’s resumé prior to this fall, but his Cooperstown case is already shaping up nicely. He sits at 60.3 bWAR, just 8.6 shy of the average of third basemen in the Hall of Fame, with a seven-year peak bWAR (44.7) just below Brooks Robinson’s (45.8).
At age 34, he is just three regular-season home runs shy of joining Alex Rodriguez as the only third basemen, shortstops, or second basemen with at least 300 homers, 400 doubles, 300 steals, and 1,000 RBIs. He’s finished as an AL MVP finalist four times. Last year, Sarah Langs made the definitive case for him as the best player never to win the award.
4) He’s a throwback
The stats are nice, but it’s the way this compact, 5-foot-8 player gets to them that makes him so fun to watch.
It’s pure hustle -- dirty uniforms, flying helmets and natural instincts. His steals stem from situational intelligence rather than elite speed, while his range, fluidity, and elite pitch-reading allow him to play an above-average hot corner and avoid strikeouts despite modest raw bat speed and arm strength.
5) His baseball smarts are off the charts
In the ninth inning of ALCS Game 1, Ramírez broke for third and came around to score when Jo Adell rolled a grounder through the left side of the infield. Cameras caught Ramírez laughing as he crossed home plate. 
Why? After the game, his agent relayed that Ramírez had planned the whole play out: He knew that Kevin Kelly was going to throw a changeup. He knew that Adell was going to roll over on it and hit a grounder to the left side. By stealing, he pulled Rays third baseman Junior Caminero to the bag -- and opened a hole exactly where the ball ended up going.
Ramírez will venture away from the on-deck circle just to get a better view of a pitcher's release point, playing the game through anticipation rather than mere reaction. One of his greatest joys is putting pressure on opponents by drawing throws, taking secondary leads and creating openings for his teammates.
Surrounded by younger players on a budget-conscious roster, he constantly tries to impart these nuances, noting, "When these guys really focus and pay attention to the game, we score a lot of runs."
6) He has humble roots
Hailing from Baní in the Dominican Republic, Ramírez grew up playing baseball on a rocky dirt square, crossing the Río Baní from a rural home that lacked running water.
Financial limitations meant playing with a glove that was too tight and using water jug caps as baseballs in games of "Vitilla.” A major childhood lifeline came when former AL MVP Miguel Tejada held a local clinic distributing equipment and food. Ramírez rushed to the front of the line.
“I never forgot it,” he said.
7) He was only scouted by accident
Undersized and often the youngest player in his league, a 13-year-old Ramírez played in rough adult leagues watched over by gamblers, with a machete dangling behind home plate as a warning for poor performance.
Scouts weren't watching him; he was usually just an extra man at showcases. But in 2009, Cleveland scouting director John Mirabelli and scout Ramon Peña happened to catch him filling in for another player and ripping hits in bunches. Peña pounded the table for him, and Ramírez was signed for $50,000.
“He’s not the guy that came in with a lot of acclaim,” Guardians president of baseball operations Chris Antonetti said. “He wasn’t afforded a ton of extra opportunities because of an investment.”
8) He’s incredibly loyal
That modest $50,000 investment bought an extraordinary level of allegiance.
Ramírez faced a crossroads in 2022, when the Guardians were contemplating a trade before his final two control years. Ramírez wanted no part of leaving. He implored his agent to secure a deal that would keep him in Cleveland, prioritizing happiness and stability over free-agent riches.
“I’m happier with $150 million in Cleveland,” he told his agent, according to an ESPN report, “than $200 million somewhere else.”
Now signed through his age-39 season, he explains it simply: "Cleveland is everything to me. When nobody wanted to give me a chance, they gave me a chance."
9) His community work is not just lip service
Crediting his late grandmother, Santa Ramírez, with teaching him the value of sharing his success, José insisted on partnering with the Guardians on community impact projects. He funded the $2.7 million José Ramírez Field alongside Cleveland Guardians Charities, serving the Lincoln-West High School team and Cleveland's Nike RBI program on a street the city proudly named José Ramírez Way.
He has also helped expand MLB's Fun At-Bat program locally and teamed up to completely refurbish the rough field in Baní where he first learned to play, making it a safe and usable space for the next generation of ballplayers.
“The reality,” he said, “is that those kids in the D.R. have no alternative. That’s why I feel it’s really important to help.”
10) He respects the game
While his famous 2023 altercation with Tim Anderson spawned popular Cleveland T-shirts celebrating the "Down Goes Anderson" moment, Ramírez was actually mortified by it. He never wants to show up an opponent or be viewed as a troublemaker, emphasizing that his goal is always to give 100 percent and set an example.
At its core, Ramírez has said what he loves most about baseball is that it is "a disciplined way of learning how to respect each other."
11) He’s hilarious
Cutthroat on the field, Ramírez loves to keep people loose off it.
He’s worn a chain with a picture of himself. Wearing a chain. He’s worn a belt adorned with his image, too.
He’s joked that he’s “more beautiful” than Shohei Ohtani. He’s yelled to Freddie Freeman, “You’re one of the best hitters … after me.”
He trash talks teammates during games of Mario Kart or playfully smacks them in the back of the head when it’s time to pay attention. Once, when a teammate was smashing an iPad after a bad at-bat, Ramírez calmly told him, “Bro, settle down, that iPad can’t hit.” He’ll field another player’s position during batting practice and josh about how easy it is.
Ultimately, he’s a connector of people, keeping things fresh with deadpan humor that keeps people guessing.
Now you know José Ramírez. He might not be your favorite player yet. But hopefully you understand why he’s a favorite to so many.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Jose Ramirez’ Playoff Run Is Making Guardians Franchise History
item.dc:creator: Tommy Wild
item.description: The Cleveland Guardians wouldn't be heading into Game 2 of the ALCS with a 1-0 series lead over the Tampa Bay Rays if it weren't for the heroics that superstar Jose Ramirez has put on all October long. Going back to the final three games of the ALDS, and now Game 1 of the ALCS, Ramirez has simply put Cleveland's lineup on his back. Terry Francona set it when he managed, and Stephen Vogt has echoed it: when Hosey goes, the Guardians go. Ramirez is doing more than just swinging a hot bat right now
item.content:encoded:
The Cleveland Guardians wouldn't be heading into Game 2 of the ALCS with a 1-0 series lead over the Tampa Bay Rays if it weren't for the heroics that superstar Jose Ramirez has put on all October long.
Going back to the final three games of the ALDS, and now Game 1 of the ALCS, Ramirez has simply put Cleveland's lineup on his back.
Terry Francona set it when he managed, and Stephen Vogt has echoed it: when Hosey goes, the Guardians go.
Ramirez is doing more than just swinging a hot bat right now; he's also setting Cleveland franchise history with how much success he's had at the plate so far this postseason.
In the top of the ninth inning on Monday night, Ramirez worked Cole Sulser into a 3-2 count with two outs and Angel Martinez standing on second base. The Tampa Bay pitcher left a cutter up in the zone, and Ramirez took it the other way
Martinez crossed home plate, and the floodgates opened for Cleveland to score two more runs and seal the deal for the Guardians in Game 1.
Looking back to Ramirez, though, this was his eighth hit and eighth RBI of the postseason up to this point.
Ramirez also tied a Cleveland franchise record, becoming just the third player to log an RBI in four straight playoff games. The other two were Jim Thome in 1998-99 and Sandy Alomar in 1997, who still coaches first base for the Guardians.
Ramirez is already one of, if not the best, players in franchise history.
That said, considering the legendary players who played for Cleveland in the 90s, like Albert Belle and Manny Ramirez, along with impressive offensive players in the late 2010s, like Francisco Lindor and Michael Brantley, it really shows how amazing Ramirez is doing.
Whether it's smacking home runs or just getting the ball in play, Vogt said after Game 1 that Ramirez just has a knack for getting on base and making things happen. There's nowhere in the box score or in a stat to measure that impact, but it's real, and the Guardians are feeling it right now.
Vogt went on to talk about how Ramirez's energy "100 percent" feeds off the rest of the team.
Who knows what will happen throughout the rest of the series, but the Guardians should be in a good spot to win the ALCS if Ramirez continues to play at this level.

item.title: [PCMag] Tampa Bay Rays vs. Cleveland Guardians Livestream: How to Watch Today's MLB Championship Game, Even for Free
item.dc:creator: Jason Cohen

item.content:encoded:
As summer comes to a close and the air turns crisp, you know what's coming: the MLB Playoffs. The NFL season is already underway, and if you're also a baseball lover, this next month is essential viewing. The MLB has been through a number of changes in recent years. From the universal DH and the pitch clock to video replay and an automated strike zone, baseball may look very different if you haven't been paying attention.
This week, the Dodgers will go head-to-head against the Brewers, and the Guardians will face the Rays in the best-of-seven Championship series. Which teams will come out on top? Here's how you can watch live.
What Time Is the Tampa Bay Rays vs. Cleveland Guardians Game?
Today's game between the Los Angeles Dodgers and the Milwaukee Brewers will take place on Tuesday, October 13 at 8 p.m. ET.
How to Watch the Tampa Bay Rays vs. Cleveland Guardians?
American League Division Series games will be broadcast on TBS, while National League games will be on Fox and FS1. You can also watch them with a live TV or sports streaming subscription from DirecTV, Fox One, Fubo, HBO Max, Hulu, Sling, Sportsnet+ (if you're in Canada), or YouTube TV.
How to Watch the Rays vs. the Guardians for Free
If you don't want to subscribe to any of the above platforms, you may be able to sign up for a few free trials to gain access to this weekend's games. Fox One and Hulu offer three-day trials, DirecTV and Fubo offer five days, and YouTube TV gives you 10 days for free.
2026 MLB Playoffs Game Schedule
MLB's expanded postseason means more teams on the playoff schedule. Things started off with the best-of-three Wild Card Series, where the Braves, Padres, White Sox, and Yankees advanced. The best-of-five Division Series put them up against the Los Angeles Dodgers, Milwaukee Brewers, Cleveland Guardians, and Tampa Bay Rays, respectively. All of whom managed to advance
Now, the Rays and Guardians and Dodgers and Brewers meet in the best-of-seven Championship Series to determine the best team in each league. The winner from each league will then advance to a best-of-seven World Series to begin on October 23. Who will make it all the way?
Los Angeles Dodgers vs. Milwaukee Brewers - MIL lead 2-0
- Game 3 on October 14 @ 8 p.m. ET - Fox/FS1
- Game 4 on October 15 @ 9 p.m. ET - Fox/FS1
- Game 5 on October 16 @ 9 p.m. ET - Fox/FS1*
- Game 6 on October 18 @ 8 p.m. ET - Fox/FS1*
- Game 7 on October 19 @ 8 p.m. ET - Fox/FS1*
Cleveland Guardians vs. Tampa Bay Rays - CLE leads 1-0
- Game 2 on October 13 @ 8 p.m. ET - TBS/HBO Max
- Game 3 on October 15 @ 6 p.m. ET - TBS/HBO Max
- Game 4 on October 16 @ 6 p.m. ET - TBS/HBO Max
- Game 5 on October 17 @ 8 p.m. ET - TBS/HBO Max*
- Game 6 on October 19 @ 5 p.m. ET - TBS/HBO Max*
- Game 7 on October 20 @ 8 p.m. ET - TBS/HBO Max*
*if necessary
How to Stream the 2026 MLB Playoffs
This year's MLB postseason is stretched across multiple networks and streaming services. All Wild Card Series games for the American League and National League were broadcast on NBC, NBCSN, and Peacock. Additional rounds will be on other networks. ALDS and ALCS games are on TBS/TruTV and HBO Max, while NLDS and NLCS games are on Fox/FS1. For the World Series, all games will be broadcast on Fox and the Fox One streaming service.
- DirecTV: DirecTV's MySports base pack costs $45 per month for the first six months to see every game on Fox, FS1, NBC, and TBS/TruTV.
- Fox One: Fox's own streaming app lets you watch the NLDS, NLCS, and World Series on Fox and FS1 for $20 per month.
- Fubo: Fubo's Sports plan costs $45.99 for the first month to watch the Wild Card Series, NLDS, NLCS, and World Series on Fox, FS1, and NBC/NBCSN.
- HBO Max: If you pay for the $18.49-per-month HBO Max Standard, you'll be able to watch the ALDS and ALCS games on TBS/TruTV.
- Hulu: For $90 per month, you can watch every game on Fox, FS1, NBC, TBS, and TruTV.
- Peacock: Instead of a live TV service, you'd need to pay $10.99 per month for Peacock Premium to see the Wild Card Series games.
- Sling: The $60.99-per-month Sling Orange & Blue bundle will let you watch the ALDS and ALCS on TBS/TruTV and the NLDS and NLCS on FS1. Day Passes are also available for Sling Orange, allowing you to watch games on TBS for up to seven days.
- Sportsnet+ (Canada only): The $30-per-month Standard tier lets you watch every postseason game.
- YouTube TV: Though the standard plan for YouTube TV costs $83 per month, you can actually now pay for the cheaper $65 Sports package to see all games on Fox, FS1, NBC/NBCSN, and TBS/TruTV.
Can I Watch Postseason Games on MLB.TV?
Are you already an MLB.TV subscriber? You can watch the Division Series, Championship Series, and World Series games through MLB's own streaming service—but there's a catch. To watch on MLB.TV, you'll first need to authenticate through a participating pay TV provider. It's such a sticking point that it makes the entire question moot. If you already have a TV provider, then you wouldn't need to use a streaming service. If you don't already have an MLB.TV subscription, don't pay for one now.
How can I listen to the 2026 postseason?
You can also listen to the games via ESPN Radio.
Which Teams Are In the Playoffs?
Since MLB expanded its postseason picture in 2022, a total of 12 teams make the playoffs each year. That includes six teams per league, including the three division winners and three Wild Card teams.
- American League Division Winners: Tampa Bay Rays (1), Cleveland Guardians (2), Houston Astros (3)
- American League Wild Card: New York Yankees (4), Boston Red Sox (5), Chicago White Sox (6)
- National League Division Winners: Milwaukee Brewers (1), Los Angeles Dodgers (2), Atlanta Braves (3)
- National League Wild Card: Chicago Cubs (4), Philadelphia Phillies (5), San Diego Padres (6)
Upgrade Your Streaming Experience
If you decide to watch the MLB postseason, there's still time to get a big-screen television for viewing this beautiful game. Pro tip: Turn on your TV's motion-smoothing option for the best picture while watching sports. Just remember to turn it off before watching other TV shows and movies to avoid the awful "soap opera" effect.
About Our Expert
As PCMag's editor of how to content, I have to cover a wide variety of topics and also make our stories accessible to everyday users. Considering my history as a technical writer, copywriter, and all-around freelancer covering baseball, comics, and more at various outlets, I am used to making myself into an expert.
I believe tech corporations are bad, but you might as well know how to use technology in everyday life. Want more how to content delivered right to your inbox? Sign up for the tips and tricks newsletter that I curate three times a week.
My job as how-to guru means I use just about every gadget under the sun, so I can figure out how everything works. I work from a Lenovo ThinkPad running Windows 11, but also have a very large Dell Inspiron 17 3000 and Apple silicon MacBook. I have a Google Pixel 6a for personal use and use a Galaxy Z Flip 4 for additional Samsung-related testing. For iOS coverage, an iPhone 13 mini works like a charm, though it's already becoming a little long in the tooth.
My desktop situation includes a dual monitor setup with a modest Acer monitor. I also use a Logitech vertical mouse (who can use these ThinkPad trackpads) and a Havit keyboard (my first mechanical keyboard; I love it but my wife hates it!). I'm a recent convert from wired headphones; I have Anker Soundcore Liberty Air wireless earbuds for personal use and have taken to the Sennheiser HD 450BT headphones for work.
Whenever I have a second to myself, I'm probably gaming on my Nintendo Switch 2, Steam Deck, or Xbox Series S. I also still have a bunch of classic consoles lying around as well.

item.title: [WSLS] Chase DeLauter and José Ramírez lead the Guardians to a 7-3 win over the Rays in Game 1 of the ALCS
item.dc:creator: Rob Maaddi; Associated Press
item.description: ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. – The Cleveland Guardians used small ball, the longball and played solid all-around baseball to keep winning in the postseason. Nathaniel Lowe snapped an eighth-inning tie with a two-run single after Chase DeLauter and Patrick Bailey homered off Drew Rasmussen, and the Guardians rallied past the Tampa Bay Rays 7-3 in Game 1 of the American League Championship Series on Monday night. Recommended Videos After losing the first two games at home to the Chicago White Sox in their
item.content:encoded:
ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. – The Cleveland Guardians used small ball, the longball and played solid all-around baseball to keep winning in the postseason.
Nathaniel Lowe snapped an eighth-inning tie with a two-run single after Chase DeLauter and Patrick Bailey homered off Drew Rasmussen, and the Guardians rallied past the Tampa Bay Rays 7-3 in Game 1 of the American League Championship Series on Monday night.
Recommended Videos
After losing the first two games at home to the Chicago White Sox in their AL Division Series, Cleveland has won four straight in the postseason for the first time since winning their first six playoff games in 2016 on the way to a World Series berth.
“It feels good to see some balls fall, to see some guys get on the barrel, to see some guys have some great at-bats, because the first two games of the White Sox series, we got beat. We did,” Lowe said. “We had to go get our backs against the wall and do something crazy, and this group did. It’s nice to feel some momentum coming here and to take Game 1.”
Jose Ramírez had three hits and DeLauter was a triple shy of the cycle as the Guardians banged out 14 hits against a Tampa Bay staff that allowed just 12 in its entire Division Series against the New York Yankees.
Junior Caminero and Jonny DeLuca had RBI singles in the first and Cedric Mullins hit a solo homer for the Rays, who never trailed in their three-game sweep of the Yankees.
“It’s been a while since we lost, so I think that’s a good thing, and I know the guys will come back and respond tomorrow,” Tampa Bay manager Kevin Cash said.
Game 2 is Tuesday night at Tropicana Field. Rookie left-hander Parker Messick starts for Cleveland, and right-hander Freddy Peralta takes the mound for the Rays.
Five relievers combined for five innings of one-run, two-hit ball for the Guardians, who became only the 11th team to overcome an 0-2 deficit in a best-of-five playoff series with a victory over the White Sox on Saturday night.
Hunter Gaddis worked a scoreless seventh for the win. Cade Smith, who pitched in all five games against Chicago, tossed a perfect ninth.
“Obviously we came off an emotional series, had a quick turnaround. But these guys come ready to play every day. Couldn’t be more proud of them,” Cleveland manager Stephen Vogt said. “We got punched early. And our pitching staff, credit to them, for stopping it and keeping us in the game as long as they did. And the offense came alive.”
Rasmussen took a 2-0 lead into the sixth before DeLauter led off with an opposite-field homer to left-center. Bailey started the seventh with a towering shot to center that went a projected 436 feet, ending Rasmussen’s night.
Rasmussen carried a no-hitter into the eighth in Game 1 of the ALDS against the Yankees.
Ramírez opened the eighth with an infield single off losing pitcher Tyler Wells, and DeLauter ripped a double to right. After Wells retired Jo Adell on a grounder to second, Ian Seymour entered. Lowe lined an 0-2 pitch up the middle to drive in two, giving Cleveland a 4-2 lead.
Lowe made his major league debut with Tampa Bay in 2019 and won a World Series with Texas in 2023.
“I love coming back here, I really do,” Lowe said. “It’s nice to see some familiar faces on the other side.”
Mullins connected off Erik Sabrowski for a solo shot in the bottom half.
Ramírez, whose two-run homer lifted Cleveland to a 2-0 win in Game 5 against Chicago, provided an insurance run with an RBI single in the ninth off Cole Sulser.
Ramírez then helped the Guardians get two more by breaking for third with two outs and two strikes on Adell. Caminero ran to cover the bag and was out of position when Adell hit a sharp grounder toward third. The ball rolled into left field for a two-run double.
A crowd of 35,361 fans waved yellow rally towels and rang cowbells at the Trop as Tampa Bay made its third ALCS appearance in the franchise's 29-season history.
They were fired up when the 98-win Rays jumped ahead 2-0 in the first and Rasmussen battled to keep it there until the sixth.
Coming off that dominant performance against the Yankees, Rasmussen went six-plus tough innings. The two-time All-Star right-hander, who was four outs from a no-hitter in a 1-0 victory against New York, allowed a hit to the second batter he faced and eight total, striking out seven.
Guardians starter Foster Griffin gave up two runs and five hits in four innings.
Glove work
The Rays helped Rasmussen with outstanding defense.
Nick Fortes threw out Ramírez trying to steal second in the first. Caminero made an excellent play to retire Adell on a hard bouncer to third. Caminero short-hopped the ball with his backhand and fired a strong throw to first.
The Guardians had a runner on first with one out in the third when second baseman Ben Williamson robbed DeLauter of a hit that prevented a first-and-third jam. Williamson, who wasn’t on the ALDS roster, made a diving grab on DeLauter’s sharp grounder, got up and threw him out.
Stranded runners
Rays slick-fielding shortstop Taylor Walls was 0 for 3 and left six runners on base. He struck out with the bases loaded to end the first, lined out with a runner on in the fourth and grounded out with runners on first and second to end the sixth.
Up next
Messick took the loss in Game 1 of the AL Division Series, allowing two runs over 4 1/3 innings. He threw 2 1/3 innings in relief during a Game 4 victory, giving up two runs. Messick had 11 strikeouts in the two appearances. He was 12-9 with a 2.56 ERA in the regular season.
Peralta allowed one run and three hits over 4 2/3 innings in Game 2 of the Division Series vs. the Yankees. He was 5-2 with a 3.25 ERA in 10 starts after joining Tampa Bay at the trade deadline. Peralta was 5-9 with a 4.99 ERA for the Mets this season.
___

item.title: [Sporting News] Junior Caminero trade, revisited: How Rays took advantage of 'bad' Guardians move for budding superstar | Sporting News
item.dc:creator: Daniel Chavkin
item.description: The Tampa Bay Rays have made it a habit of taking undervalued players and turning them into stars. No one exemplifies that more than star third baseman Junior Caminero.
