item.content:encoded:
The Tampa Bay Rays have made it a habit of taking undervalued players and turning them into stars. No one exemplifies that more than star third baseman Junior Caminero.
The Rays acquired Caminero from the Cleveland Guardians in a minor deal after the 2021 season, which turned out to be one of the biggest trade heists in recent memory. Caminero is now one of the premier sluggers in the entire league, making the Guardians miss their former prospect.
Caminero was confused at the time, wondering why Cleveland gave up on his so quickly.
"That happened really quick. In that moment, as a young player, I was surprised," he told MLB.com. "'Why did Cleveland trade me? We played just one year in the Dominican, and they traded me?' I said, 'Am I a bad guy? Why would they trade me?' But in that moment, I didn't understand baseball. Like, hey, if you get traded, it's good for you. It was an unbelievable trade. Thank God."
Now, Caminero has made the Guardians regret their trade, potentially even forcing them to change the way they approach certain deals. Here's a recap of that trade from 2021.
MORE: Comparing the payrolls for the ALCS, NLCS teams
Revisiting Junior Caminero trade
Rays receive:
- 3B Junior Caminero
Guardians receive:
- RHP Tobais Myers
In November of 2021, the Rays and Guardians connected for what at the time was a very minor deal involving two minor leagues. The Rays, needing to clear space on its 40-man roster, sent Tobias Myers to Cleveland, who was interested in adding the young pitcher. In return, the Rays got young infielder Junior Caminero, who had been in the Cleveland system for two years.
According to MLB.com, Caminero became the Rays' 30th-best prospect before the 2022 season, while Myers was ranked No. 22 for the Guardians' system. Neither had made their MLB debut up to that point, but both were considered intriguing young players.
Of course, the Rays went on to win the trade easily. The Guardians traded Myers to the San Francisco Giants in June of 2022 for cash considerations, and Myers would go on to play in the Chicago White Sox system before making his MLB debut with the Milwaukee Brewers. He currently plays for the New York Mets.
Caminero, meanwhile, has blossomed into being one of the best hitters in baseball, and is someone who Cleveland would love to have in their lineup.
MORE: Yankees playoff history with Aaron Judge
Why did Guardians trade Junior Caminero?
The Guardians seemingly just didn't value Caminero's talent as much as they should've, and they paid the price as a result. Just two years after the deal, when Caminero vaulted to become a top-five prospect in he league, Guardians president Chris Antonetti acknowledged how much the team lost the deal.
"That's a bad trade," he said.
In reality, the Rays did their due diligence and targeted Caminero when it became clear the Guardians were interested in trading for Myers. However, the Rays immediately realized they got a hidden gem in Caminero.
"The immediate reaction upon acquiring him was wondering how in the world we were able to make that acquisition," former Rays director of Minor League operations Jeff McLerran said. "Really from the get-go, the guys felt like we had something special with Junior. Just his ability to impact the baseball and what he could do at the plate was not something that they had seen much from a guy that age."
Caminero made his MLB debut in September of 2023, almost two years after the deal went through, at just the age of 20 years-old. Since Caminero was just 18 years-old at the time of the deal, the Guardians probably didn't see his potential success as more than a lottery ticket.
Junior Caminero stats
| Year | Games | Hits | Runs | HR | RBIs | BA | OBP | OPS |
| 2023 | 7 | 8 | 4 | 1 | 7 | .235 | .278 | .631 |
| 2024 | 43 | 41 | 15 | 6 | 18 | .248 | .299 | .724 |
| 2025 | 154 | 159 | 93 | 45 | 110 | .264 | .311 | .846 |
| 2026 | 162 | 170 | 100 | 42 | 101 | .276 | .360 | .885 |
After getting his feet wet in the majors in 2023 and 2024, Caminero broke out in 2025 with the first of two-straight seasons with 40 home runs. Since the start of 2025, Caminero has the most home runs in the American League and second-most in the majors, just short of Kyle Schwarber.

item.content:encoded:
Drew Rasmussen will face a familiar opponent when the Tampa Bay Rays open the American League Championship Series against the Cleveland Guardians on Monday. The right-hander is preparing to pitch against Steven Kwan, his former college teammate and longtime friend at Oregon State.
Rasmussen spoke warmly about Kwan ahead of the matchup, praising the Guardians outfielder's character as well as his ability. The two played together in college before establishing themselves in the major leagues.
"There's not enough great things I could say about the kid. He's perfect. He's unbelievable. He's one of the greatest human beings in the entire sport," Rasmussen said, according to ESPN reporter Buster Olney.
Drew Rasmussen is fired up to face his college teammate and longtime friend Steven Kwan in the playoffs: “There’s not enough great things I could say about the kid. He’s perfect. He’s unbelievable. He’s one of the greatest human beings in the entire sport.”
When Rasmussen faces…
— Buster Olney (@Buster_ESPN) October 11, 2026
Rasmussen also described the familiar exchange between the two when they meet on the field. "I definitely acknowledge every single time," he said. "Usually a little smile gets shot back in my direction. I mean, shoot, I was 19 the first time I faced him in fall ball at Oregon State."
The matchup carries added significance because Rasmussen enters the series after a dominant postseason start. He held the New York Yankees to one hit over eight scoreless innings in Game 1 of the American League Division Series, striking out 10 and allowing two walks as Tampa Bay won 1-0.
Rasmussen also delivered a strong regular season, finishing 2026 with a 16-5 record, a 2.67 ERA and 174 strikeouts across 172 innings. His performance gives Tampa Bay an experienced starter to lead its rotation into the matchup with Cleveland.
Kwan finished the regular season with a .282 batting average, a .382 on-base percentage, 152 hits and 10 stolen bases. The left fielder also helped Cleveland reach the ALCS after the Guardians defeated the Chicago White Sox in five games in the Division Series.
The Rays finished 98-64 and swept the Yankees in their ALDS, while Cleveland advanced after rallying from a two-game deficit against Chicago. The teams begin their best-of-seven series Monday at Tropicana Field, with Rasmussen scheduled to start for Tampa Bay.
The friendship between Rasmussen and Kwan will add a personal element to the opening game, but both players will have a clear job to do. Rasmussen will try to keep Cleveland's lineup in check, while Kwan will look to help the Guardians take an early lead in the series.

item.description: October baseball is a different animal for prop bettors — smaller sample, bigger stakes, and lineups built around whoever’s been carrying their team through the first two rounds. Monday’s slate gives us two of those players squarely in the spotlight: Shohei Ohtani trying to find his timing again in Milwaukee, and a pair of Tampa Bay bats that have already authored the signature moments of their ALDS sweep heading into Game 1 of the ALCS against Cleveland. None of these three lines are “free mone
item.content:encoded:
October baseball is a different animal for prop bettors — smaller sample, bigger stakes, and lineups built around whoever’s been carrying their team through the first two rounds. Monday’s slate gives us two of those players squarely in the spotlight: Shohei Ohtani trying to find his timing again in Milwaukee, and a pair of Tampa Bay bats that have already authored the signature moments of their ALDS sweep heading into Game 1 of the ALCS against Cleveland.
None of these three lines are “free money,” and we’re not pretending otherwise. But each one is backed by a real statistical case, and one of them is a legitimate longshot worth a small piece of your bankroll. Here’s the breakdown.
Shohei Ohtani Hits Over 0.5 (-115) vs. Logan Henderson
Ohtani’s .275/.377/.512 slash line with 30 home runs, 144 hits, and 268 total bases over 135 games this season is the baseline case for betting him to reach base in literally any game he plays. A .377 on-base percentage means Ohtani is getting on base better than one out of every three plate appearances even before you isolate hits specifically, and his contact skills remain elite even in a year where he split time managing a knee issue.
The matchup context matters here too. Henderson is a rookie-caliber arm who hasn’t faced a lineup with this level of postseason pressure attached to it, and the Dodgers as a group have shown they can grind out at-bats against less experienced starters. At just 0.5 hits, this line is asking Ohtani for a single knock in what will likely be 4-5 plate appearances. Even accounting for recent cold stretches, betting against Shohei Ohtani recording one hit in a full game remains one of the tougher outs in the sport to actually complete.
Jonathan Aranda Hits Over 0.5 vs. Franco Griffin
If you watched any of the Rays-Yankees ALDS, you already know the Aranda story. His third-inning solo shot off Gerrit Cole in Game 1 — a 417-foot blast to right-center — was the only run of a 1-0 series-opening win, and it set the tone for a clean three-game sweep. Across that series, Aranda hit .333/.385/.583 for a .968 OPS, numbers that dwarf his already-solid .274/.358/.434 season line.
That’s the core of the case: Aranda is seeing the ball well right now, has shown he can do damage against a well above-average Yankees pitching staff, and now draws a left-handed starter in Griffin to open the ALCS. First baseman with sticky contact skills facing a lefty he hasn’t built extensive familiarity with is a profile that tends to produce base hits, not shutouts. At 0.5 hits, the number is simply asking for one knock from a hitter who’s been getting multiple most nights since the calendar flipped to October.
Junior Caminero Home Run Over 0.5 (+525 BetRivers)
This is the one we’re framing honestly: a value shot, not a lock. Caminero is coming off a 42-homer season — his second straight 40-bomb campaign — and projection models still put him around a 0.24 expected home run probability for any single game, which sits below what the plus-money price implies you need for a coin-flip bet. In other words, this isn’t the kind of prop where the math says “take the over all day.” It’s a power bet on a player who has legitimate 40-plus-homer pop and a juicy price if he connects.
Where it gets more interesting is the matchup and the moment. Caminero is drawing another lefty in Griffin tonight, and left-on-right power threats like Caminero have shown they can turn a mistake into a souvenir in a hurry — he’s also shown an .817 OPS against the Yankees in this postseason run specifically, proof the bat is playing up on the biggest stage, not shrinking from it. At +525, you’re not betting that Caminero goes deep most nights. You’re betting that on a night where ESPN’s own expert panel has him tabbed as a leading ALCS MVP pick, the long ball is live enough to make the number worth a small stake.
Today’s Edge
Two contact-driven hits bets and one true power longshot — that’s the balance we’re carrying into Monday’s games. Always confirm the latest line movement with your sportsbook before locking anything in, since postseason numbers can shift quickly as lineups are finalized.
- Shohei Ohtani OVER 0.5 Hits (-115)
- Jonathan Aranda OVER 0.5 Hits
- Junior Caminero OVER 0.5 Home Runs (+525 BetRivers)
The hits props lean on two hitters who have been nearly impossible to keep off base in October, while the Caminero shot gives this card real upside if the Rays’ slugger connects early in the ALCS. If you’re shopping for better plus-money odds on power props like that one, it’s worth comparing a few books before locking in your DraftKings Promo Code or another book’s current offer.

item.title: [MLB.com] White Sox-Guardians ALDS Game 5 FAQ (Sat., 8 ET, TBS/HBO Max)
item.dc:creator: Tim Stebbins; Scott Merkin; Anthony Castrovince
item.description: CLEVELAND -- This must be how it had to be. The White Sox and Guardians have exhausted each other all year. They played 13 times in the regular season, with seven games decided by one run and four ending with a walk-off. Their AL Central battle came down to a single game. And now, their best-of-five ALDS has reached a decisive Game 5 on Saturday night, at what will be a packed and passionate Progressive Field. item.content:encoded:
CLEVELAND -- This must be how it had to be.
The White Sox and Guardians have exhausted each other all year. They played 13 times in the regular season, with seven games decided by one run and four ending with a walk-off. Their AL Central battle came down to a single game. And now, their best-of-five ALDS has reached a decisive Game 5 on Saturday night, at what will be a packed and passionate Progressive Field.
These teams’ scouting reports on each other are so detailed at this point that they include players’ childhood fears and preferred orders at the airport Cinnabon. There are old married couples that haven’t spent as much time together as the 2026 Sox and Guardians.
But only one of them can advance to face the No. 1-seeded Rays in the ALCS, which begins Monday at Tropicana Field. And with both Chicago and Cleveland having won two games apiece in the other’s domain, this deeply personal hard-fought series -- the only LDS to go the distance this year -- will now get the winner-take-all it deserves.
“Just on to the next,” White Sox shortstop Colson Montgomery said. “Flush these last two games. It’s out of our control now. All we can control is how we show up on Saturday.”
After Gavin Williams closed out the Guardians’ win in Game 4 with an emergency relief appearance, he will take the ball in Game 5 for his second start this series. Williams, who struck out an AL-best 248 batters in the regular season, struck out 11 more in only five innings in Game 2.
“It's a Game 5, win or go home,” manager Stephen Vogt said. “Gavin wants the ball. We want him to have the ball, and it's his game.”
Give Cleveland credit for pulling itself off the mat in a tough environment on the South Side. José Ramírez roared to life, and a Guards offense that had been flat in Games 1 and 2 scored 18 runs total across Games 3 and 4.
The last team to rally from an 0-2 hole in a best-of-five series and win it was the 2017 Yankees … against Cleveland. The Guardians could join the 2001 Yankees (vs. A’s), 2012 Giants (vs. Reds) and 2015 Blue Jays (vs. Rangers) as the only teams to come back from 0-2 in the Division Series after losing the first two at home. One figures that if the Guardians are going to end the longest active championship drought in the sport (dating back to 1948), they might as well do it the hard way.
“I think momentum's definitely going be big in this next one,” Steven Kwan said. “We kind of let the home crowd down those first two games. So hopefully it's another chance at redemption.”
As for the Sox, they missed their chance to clinch a playoff series at home for the first time since 1906. But that trivia is trivial compared to the ultimate goal of reaching the next round in any way, shape or form. No one expected Chicago to even reach the playoffs this year, but this No. 6-seeded team has made serious noise with its unorthodox pitching plan. And as bad as things went at home, at least they come into Game 5 with their best starter, Sean Burke, rested and ready.
“Play our baseball,” White Sox second baseman Chase Meidroth said. “Some at-bats we bounced back and had some good little runs. Couldn’t get that big hit. But they are a good staff and a great pitching staff. It’s not easy, it’s not easy against them ever.”
This exhausting, exhilarating AL Central rivalry has one game left to play. It’s the Central focus of the baseball world.
When is the game and how can I tune in?
Game 5 of the ALDS presented by Booking.com is scheduled for Saturday at 8 ET/7 CT on TBS/truTV/UniMas/HBO Max.
The ALDS will be available in Spanish on UniMas, while Univision’s TUDN Radio will provide Spanish-language audio coverage. ESPN Radio will provide live national coverage of all 2026 MLB Postseason games.
Who are the starting pitchers?
White Sox manager Will Venable committed to Burke starting Game 5 during a Friday afternoon Zoom session from Rate Field. The right-hander had a 2-0 record with a 1.04 ERA in three regular-season appearances (two starts) against the Guardians, so the White Sox have to feel confident.
Key stat: Williams is coming off his first relief appearance at any level as a professional. Before that, his previous bullpen experience came in 2021 while in college at East Carolina.
The Guardians’ advantage in earning a postseason first-round bye was their ability to get Parker Messick and Williams two starts apiece in the ALDS. Ironically, Messick’s 2 1/3-inning effort in Game 4 prompted an unplanned bullpen game in which Cleveland used seven additional pitchers -- including Williams, who got the final three outs.
Vogt on Friday announced Williams, who threw 18 pitches, will be his Game 5 starter.
“After the game last night, I was walking by his office and I told him I was ready to go,” Williams said Friday. “Whatever [I need to do] to help the team win, that's what I'm going to do. It doesn't matter the role at this point.”
What do the starting lineups look like?
White Sox: With the right-handed throwing power of Williams potentially on the mound, look for Venable to go back to his left-handed directed lineup.
Guardians: Patrick Bailey figures to be back behind the plate after he went 2-for-3 with a pinch-hit home run and two RBIs in Game 4. It will be curious if the Guardians make a switch in the outfield, given Angel Martínez is 0-for-15 with eight strikeouts this series. Daniel Schneemann, Petey Halpin and David Fry each are options on the ALDS roster.
How will the bullpens line up after the starter?
White Sox: Grant Taylor explained after Thursday’s rough showing (where he faced six hitters and didn’t retire any of them) how he will be ready to throw Saturday in any form even if it’s nine innings. The White Sox will be using whomever they have available, whether it’s relievers or starters, to get through Game 5.
Guardians: Whoever advances to the ALCS will do so with a pitching staff that has carried a heavy workload this series. The Guardians will worry about Game 1 of that series if they are fortunate to get there, Vogt said Thursday night. It will be all hands on deck coming out of the off-day on Friday.
“Obviously we need to see how everybody feels today,” Vogt said Friday. “We need to see how everybody feels coming in tomorrow. But I think if you're a pitcher on our roster, be ready to go tomorrow.”
Any injuries of note?
White Sox: None.
Guardians: Austin Hedges took a Teel foul tip off his right knee in the second inning in Game 4. He was sore on Friday, Vogt said, but the skipper expressed optimism Hedges will be ready to go on Saturday.
Who is hot and who is not?
White Sox: Miguel Vargas homered in the ninth inning off Cade Smith Thursday and reached base three other times via the walk. Munetaka Murakami singled while also walking twice.
Anything else fans might want to know?
- Vargas has reached base 12 times in total during the series.
- Bailey’s pinch-hit homer in the fifth inning of Game 4 was the first by the Guardians in the postseason since Jhonkensy Noel in Game 3 of the 2024 ALCS.

PETERSBURG – As he waited in the on-deck circle before an at-bat last Saturday in Game 1 of the American League Division Series, with more than 40,000 vociferous Rays and Yankees fans in attendance at Tropicana Field, Tampa Bay third baseman Junior Caminero remarked to manager Kevin Cash that he hadn't seen an atmosphere like that since the World Baseball Classic in March at Miami’s loanDepot park. item.content:encoded:
ST. PETERSBURG – As he waited in the on-deck circle before an at-bat last Saturday in Game 1 of the American League Division Series, with more than 40,000 vociferous Rays and Yankees fans in attendance at Tropicana Field, Tampa Bay third baseman Junior Caminero remarked to manager Kevin Cash that he hadn't seen an atmosphere like that since the World Baseball Classic in March at Miami’s loanDepot park.
In that tournament, Caminero tied for the overall lead in home runs with three and slashed .350/.409/.850 for the Dominican Republic in six games. This month, after coming into this postseason with just two playoff at-bats under his belt as a rookie in the 2023 AL Wild Card Series against the Rangers, Caminero is 3-for-10 with a double and two runs scored, helping the Rays sweep the Yankees in the ALDS.
Another member of the Rays who stood out in the World Baseball Classic has also had a solid start to this year’s postseason for Tampa Bay. That would be Jonathan Aranda, who had had just one postseason at-bat in his career before this season – also in '23 against Texas.
After slashing .357/.438/.643 with a home run for Team Mexico in four games at Houston’s Daikin Park in March, the Rays' first baseman came up big in the ALDS, producing the only run in Game 1 with a 417-foot round-tripper off Gerrit Cole and posting a .333/.385/.583 for the series, including an RBI single in Wednesday’s clinching victory.
Seeing Caminero and Aranda have that type of success in their first prolonged Major League postseason, Cash sees a correlation between their exposure to the atmosphere of the WBC and what they’re experiencing now in the postseason.
“I go back to the WBC,” Cash said. “If you ask those two individuals you’re talking about, I think they would say that that environment in the WBC is as intense as any environment that they’ve witnessed in their careers.
“We know that both of those guys really took off for their countries; whether it was the Dominican Republic or Team Mexico, they were huge parts of their success. The big at-bats, the big hits, I think it really helped them. And more than anything, they were excited to get the opportunity to do this now in Major League playoff baseball.”
In Miami’s Pool D, the atmosphere was electric, with the Dominican Republic and eventual tournament champion Venezuela among the countries playing in front of passionate sellout crowds cheering on their nations’ teams. And in Houston’s Pool B, Mexico also had large partisan crowds rooting for the bordering nation, an environment crescendoed with the matchup against the United States in pool play.
“I don’t think you can say the moment’s been too big for either of them,” Cash said, once again crediting their experiences in the Classic as part of their overall preparedness for the MLB postseason. “I think they had really good, strong series in the DS. I think those two guys have had tremendous at-bats for us.”

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] José Ramírez, just in time to save the Guardians' season, has rediscovered his MVP form in ALDS vs. White Sox
item.dc:creator: Russell Dorsey
item.description: CHICAGO — Even in the worst full season of his career, a true superstar can turn it on at any time. José Ramírez is arguably one of the five best players in Major League Baseball. He had a down year by his standards in 2026, but the Cleveland Guardians couldn't have picked a better time for their best player to get hot. With their season on the line in Game 4 of the ALDS against the Chicago White Sox and an opportunity to send the series back to Cleveland for a winner-take-all Game 5, the Guardi
item.content:encoded:
CHICAGO — Even in the worst full season of his career, a true superstar can turn it on at any time.
José Ramírez is arguably one of the five best players in Major League Baseball. He had a down year by his standards in 2026, but the Cleveland Guardians couldn't have picked a better time for their best player to get hot. With their season on the line in Game 4 of the ALDS against the Chicago White Sox and an opportunity to send the series back to Cleveland for a winner-take-all Game 5, the Guardians' superman found his cape.
"That's a future Hall of Famer," outfielder Chase DeLauter said after Cleveland's 9-5 victory on Thursday in Chicago. "It's special."
Through the first two games of the ALDS, Ramírez didn't look like the player Cleveland knows him to be, going 0-for-6 with three strikeouts. His early-series struggles seemingly carried over from the final month of the regular season, which saw him put up a paltry .198/.237/.264 slashline with just one home run.
But Game 3 on Wednesday seemed to have unlocked something for the Guardians' superstar. In that one, Ramírez went 2-for-4 with a double, a triple and a stolen base. He took over the game with his bat, glove and his legs. Then Ramírez had even more in store for Game 4.
Just like in Game 3, the White Sox took the momentum early on Thursday, taking a 2-0 lead into the fifth inning and running Guardians starter Parker Messick out of the game after just 2 1/3 innings. But once catcher Patrick Bailey cut the lead in half with a solo shot, it was time for Ramírez to make his mark on the game.
"It's contagious to the team, like the way he plays the game, the energy, his at-bat quality," second baseman Travis Bazzana said postgame. "I mean, we saw him [in Game 3] manufacture a run by himself. He got on, stole some bases and then scored. So he can make the impact so fast, but he plays with such intention."
Prior to Ramírez's fifth-inning at-bat, it felt like a big swing was coming. He flew out in his first at-bat before a sharp lineout in his second. But he found the barrel on both, with exit velocities of 98.9 mph and 97.5 mph, respectively.
Ramírez made sure the third ball he put in play wouldn't be caught. The Guardians' third baseman launched a two-run blast to put Cleveland ahead 3-2 and injected some much-needed confidence into the visiting dugout.
While he doesn't typically show a lot of emotion, Ramírez was sure to fire up his dugout before rounding the bases.
"It's a special moment when you have that type of energy from the guys," he said postgame. "I had a particular conversation with Messick before that. I told him, 'I'm going to get this turned around for you,' and I was able to execute it. It was really special."
Said manager Stephen Vogt: "It was José Ramírez being José Ramírez in the playoffs. Bring in a fastball, [Jordan] Hicks with a great fastball, and Josy got to it. To step up, say there he goes again. And a big moment for him, big moment for us, and he doesn't show a lot of emotion, but he was pretty excited tonight."
Although Cleveland's lead didn't hold long, with Chicago scoring two more in the bottom of the fifth, Ramírez for the second straight day galvanized the Guardians' offense. That three-run outburst in the fifth inning was just an appetizer. The entreé was a monster, six-run sixth inning that made it 9-4 and broke the game open.
As part of that six-run sixth, Ramírez added an RBI single, giving him back-to-back multi-hit games. Since that 0-for-6 in the first two games of the ALDS, the Cleveland superstar is 4-for-9 in the second pair of games, with a double, a triple, a home run, a walk, a stolen base, four runs scored and five RBI.
"It just starts with him. Whether he's hot, whether he's cold, just having him in the lineup, it's that presence," DeLauter said. "When he comes out firing, has that energy, has cool, big swings like that — it just rallies us together."
The numbers will tell you that Ramírez has not been at his best for much of 2026 — he had surgery on the hamate bone in his left hand in June, after all — but you wouldn't know it by his confidence. The seven-time All-Star might not be tall, but he walks around like he's a giant. And that confidence can be felt by everyone around him.
For the Guardians to fight back from a 2-0 series deficit while in Chicago and get back to Cleveland for a chance to reach the ALCS, they needed the best version of Ramírez to show up. And with not a moment to spare, it appears that he has rediscovered his elite form.
Now Cleveland has an opportunity to become the first team since the 2017 New York Yankees to win three straight games in a best-of-five series after losing the first two. Heading back home with a superstar who has gotten hot, an offense that's rolling and a White Sox team that's on the ropes, the Guardians appear to have all the momentum.
"It's going to be crazy," Ramírez said of what he expects for Game 5. "It's going to be an incredible energy. For us, it's going to be the same mindset: Try to win the game, and enjoy the environment that's going to be at Progressive [Field]."

item.content:encoded:
Oct 8, 2026, 11:35 AM ET
New York Yankees impending free-agent first baseman/designated hitter Paul Goldschmidt has expressed a desire to keep playing at age 39 in 2027, according to Gary Phillips of the New York Daily News. It is unclear if the Yankees will make an effort to re-sign the former MVP and seven-time All-Star in the offseason. Goldy had a nice bounce-back campaign in 2026 in his 16th year in the big leagues after he hit just 10 homers and drove in 45 runs in 146 games in 2025 in his first year in pinstripes. In 105 regular-season games across 380 plate appearances this year, Goldschmidt hit .252/.313/.452 with a .765 OPS, 18 home runs, 52 RBI, and 44 runs scored for the Yankees. He went hitless in eight plate appearances with two walks and a run scored in four postseason games for New York this year. Goldschmidt is obviously no longer in his prime and is no longer an everyday player, but he should still attract interest across the league for his ability to hit lefties. In 183 plate appearances against southpaws in 2026, he hit .299 (47-for-157) with 11 of his 18 home runs and 24 RBI.--Keith Hernandez
Source: New York Daily News - Gary Phillips
More Recent News
Oct 8, 2026, 11:28 AM ET
Tampa Bay Rays closer Bryan Baker shut the door in his team's 4-3 win over the New York Yankees in Game 3 of the American League Division Series on Wednesday, pitching a scoreless ninth inning with two strikeouts. Baker was a key part of Tampa Bay's three-game sweep of New York, logging saves in all three games while allowing just one baserunner to reach. The 31-year-old emerged as one of the best closers in baseball during the regular season, recording a 1.44 ERA and 0.91 WHIP with 63 strikeouts and 41 saves across 62 1/3 innings (65 games). Heading into the American League Championship Series, Baker's dominance at the end of games gives Tampa Bay a significant advantage if it can get an early lead on its opponents.--Will Brady
Source: ESPN.com
Jakob Marsee Having UCL Repair With Internal Brace


Keith Hernandez




Oct 8, 2026, 11:24 AM ET
Miami Marlins outfielder Jakob Marsee (elbow) will get a UCL repair with an internal brace of his left elbow on Monday, according to Christina De Nicola of MLB.com. The estimated return-to-play timeline for Marsee is around six months. Marsee battled through elbow issues down the stretch in 2026 in his first full season in the majors with Miami. In his first taste of the big leagues in 2025, Marsee hit .292 (61-for-209) with five home runs, 33 RBI, 14 stolen bases, and 28 runs scored in 55 games and 234 plate appearances. In 155 games and 616 plate appearances this year, Marsee slashed .231/.348/.359 with a .706 OPS, 11 home runs, 41 RBI, 23 stolen bases, and 83 runs scored for the Fish. The 25-year-old former sixth-round pick by the San Diego Padres in 2022 from Central Michigan University has a very intriguing power/speed profile as an outfielder in all fantasy leagues, but his availability for Opening Day in 2027 could be in question, depending on how he fares during his rehab after going under the knife early next week.--Keith Hernandez
Source: MLB.com - Christina De Nicola
Oct 8, 2026, 11:21 AM ET
Milwaukee Brewers outfielder Garrett Mitchell had a big game in his team's 3-1, series-clinching win over the San Diego Padres in Game 4 of the National League Division Series on Wednesday. At the plate, Mitchell went two-for-four with a triple, an RBI, and a run scored. In the field, Mitchell robbed Padres third baseman Manny Machado of what would have been a game-tying two-run home run in the eighth inning. The 28-year-old Mitchell was finally able to stay mostly healthy in 2026, hitting .262/.354/.416 with 11 home runs, 65 RBI, 74 runs scored, and 14 stolen bases across 531 plate appearances in the regular season. He was productive in the NLDS as well, logging four hits, three runs scored, an RBI, and a stolen base across 15 at-bats.--Will Brady
Source: ESPN.com
Hagen Smith Opening Game 4 of ALDS on Thursday


Keith Hernandez




Oct 8, 2026, 11:15 AM ET
Chicago White Sox rookie left-hander Hagen Smith will serve as the opener in Game 4 of the American League Division Series on Thursday at home against the division-rival Cleveland Guardians, according to Scott Merkin of MLB.com. The 23-year-old former fifth overall pick in 2024 from the University of Arkansas made 18 appearances (only one start) in his major-league debut during the 2026 regular season, posting a nice 1.29 ERA (2.35 FIP) and 0.96 WHIP with 41 strikeouts and 16 walks in 28 innings pitched. The talented young southpaw has already thrown 6 1/3 innings in his first experience in the playoffs, too, allowing just one earned run on three hits while walking five and striking out six. He started Game 1 of the ALDS against Cleveland and threw 2 2/3 shutout innings with three walks and four strikeouts in the team's 3-0 victory before allowing a run with two walks and a strikeout in two-thirds of an inning in Wednesday's Game 3 loss. Smith will probably have a short leash as the White Sox try to close out the best-of-five series, with right-hander Erick Fedde potentially piggybacking Smith in Chicago. In three relief appearances against the Guardians during the regular season, Smith allowed two earned runs with six walks and eight strikeouts in 5 2/3 innings pitched.--Keith Hernandez
Source: MLB.com - Scott Merkin
Victor Mesa Jr. Homers in ALDS-Clinching Win


Will Brady




Oct 8, 2026, 11:14 AM ET
Tampa Bay Rays outfielder Victor Mesa Jr. was one of the stars of his team's 4-3 win in Game 3 of the American League Division Series over the New York Yankees, hitting a two-run home run off Yankees left-hander Max Fried. Mesa Jr.'s home run was his only hit of the night, but it gave the Rays a 4-2 lead in the sixth inning that they would ultimately never give back. Across 262 plate appearances in the regular season, Mesa Jr. hit .260/.327/.498 with 14 home runs, 34 RBI, 37 runs scored, and nine stolen bases. After starting the year in the minors, the 25-year-old has emerged as an everyday corner outfielder for Tampa Bay and provides another dynamic power/speed bat for the Rays. If Mesa Jr. can get hot, he could help power a deep postseason run.--Will Brady
Source: ESPN.com
Oct 7, 2026, 10:01 PM ET
Los Angeles Dodgers closer Edwin Diaz picked up his second save in as many nights on Wednesday, pitching a scoreless ninth inning with a strikeout in his team's 4-1 victory over the Atlanta Braves in Game 4 of the National League Division Series. Diaz missed most of the 2026 regular season due to elbow and neck injuries. However, he's been dominant since returning from the injured list in mid-September. Diaz allowed just two baserunners while notching nine strikeouts in his final five innings pitched of the regular season, and he's now logged low-stress saves in each of his first two appearances of the playoffs. With Diaz rounding into form, Los Angeles' bullpen looks like a major strength heading into the National League Championship Series.--Will Brady
Source: ESPN.com
Oct 7, 2026, 9:52 PM ET
Cleveland Guardians left-hander Foster Griffin was dominant in a bulk relief appearance in his team's 9-3 win over the Chicago White Sox in Game 3 of the American League Division Series on Wednesday. Griffin followed Cleveland opener Daniel Espino and allowed two hits and one earned run while striking out seven across 2 2/3 innings of work. The 31-year-old was used exclusively as a starting pitcher during the regular season, posting a 15-6 record with a 3.60 ERA, 1.21 WHIP, and 158 strikeouts across 172 2/3 innings (31 starts) split between the Guardians and the Washington Nationals. However, Griffin struggled mightily late in the year, pitching to a 5.05 ERA in the second half and a 6.87 ERA across 18 1/3 innings in September. If Griffin can rediscover his early-season form in a bullpen role, he could help Cleveland mount a comeback in the ALDS.--Will Brady
Source: ESPN.com
Oct 7, 2026, 9:43 PM ET
Cleveland Guardians outfielder Jo Adell had a big night in his team's 9-3 victory over the Chicago White Sox in Game 3 of the American League Division Series on Wednesday, going 2-for-4 with a walk and three RBI. With the game tied 1-1 in the third inning, Adell put the Guardians ahead for good with a three-run triple off of White Sox left-hander Hagen Smith. Across 660 regular-season plate appearances split between the Guardians and the Los Angeles Angels, Adell hit .240/.298/.401 with 23 home runs, 94 RBI, 70 runs scored, and five stolen bases. He was better with Cleveland than he was with Los Angeles, posting a .740 OPS across 204 trips to the plate after the Guardians acquired him at the trade deadline. Adell has notched a couple of key hits for Cleveland in the ALDS and now has four RBI across the first three games of the series.--Will Brady
Source: ESPN.com
Oct 7, 2026, 9:32 PM ET
Los Angeles Dodgers outfielder Andy Pages had the key hit in his team's 4-1 win over the Atlanta Braves in Game 4 of the National League Division Series on Wednesday, logging a go-ahead two-run single off Braves right-hander Robert Suarez in the seventh inning. Pages finished the game with two hits and two RBI in three at-bats. The 25-year-old was a critical piece of the Dodgers lineup during the regular season, hitting .274 with 23 home runs, 85 RBI, 75 runs scored, and 13 stolen bases. However, Pages struggled mightily during the Dodgers' run to the 2025 World Series, notching just four hits in 55 postseason plate appearances. After his big night on Wednesday, Pages has already logged four hits in just 15 plate appearances in the 2026 playoffs.--Will Brady
Source: ESPN.com
Oct 7, 2026, 9:19 PM ET
Cleveland Guardians right-hander Cade Smith was lights out to secure his team's 9-3 victory over the Chicago White Sox in Game 3 of the American League Division Series on Wednesday. Smith entered the game in the eighth inning and recorded the final six outs, logging five strikeouts without allowing a single baserunner. The 27-year-old was one of the best closers in baseball during the regular season, pitching to a 1.95 ERA and 0.96 WHIP with 107 strikeouts and 41 saves across 74 innings (69 games). Smith has been dominant so far in the Division Series as well, as he's yet to allow a hit or a walk in his four innings of work. If Cleveland is going to mount a comeback in the series, it will likely need Smith to continue his dominance.--Will Brady
Source: ESPN.com
Oct 7, 2026, 9:11 PM ET
Cleveland Guardians third baseman Jose Ramirez was one of the stars of his team's 9-3 victory over the Chicago White Sox in Game 3 of the American League Division Series. In five plate appearances, Ramirez recorded a double, a triple, a walk, two RBI, two runs scored, and a stolen base. With Cleveland leading 5-3 in the 8th inning, it was Ramirez's two-run triple that sealed the win for the Guardians and kept the series alive to see Game 4. The 34-year-old battled through injuries and underperformance in 2026, hitting .235/.320/.368 with 12 home runs, 53 RBI, 71 runs scored, and 37 stolen bases across 544 plate appearances. Ramirez also got off to a slow start in the postseason, going hitless in his first eight trips to the plate against the White Sox. If Cleveland is going to rally all the way back from two games down in the ALDS, it will need Ramirez to stay hot in Games 4 and 5.--Will Brady
Source: ESPN.com
Robert Gasser Starting Game 4 of NLDS Against Padres


Keith Hernandez




Oct 7, 2026, 8:08 PM ET
Milwaukee Brewers left-hander Robert Gasser will start for the Brewers in Game 4 of the National League Division Series on Wednesday night at Petco Park against the San Diego Padres, according to Brewers reporter Sophia Minnaert. It will be Gasser's first career postseason start after throwing 2 2/3 innings of relief in the playoffs for the Brew Crew last year. The 27-year-old southpaw went 5-5 on the season with a 3.87 ERA (4.24 FIP) and 1.19 WHIP with a career-high 103 strikeouts and 35 walks in 109 1/3 innings across 21 appearances (20 starts). The problem for Gasser is that he has not made a start in almost two weeks, so he could be a bit rusty. Manager Pat Murphy will surely have a short hook on the young left-hander as the Brewers look to close the best-of-five series out in San Diego. Gasser was outstanding down the stretch in 2026, allowing two earned runs or fewer in each of his last six starts, walking 12 and striking out 31 in 32 1/3 innings during that span. He did not face the Padres at all during the regular season, which could give him a bit of an advantage.--Keith Hernandez
Source: Sophia Minnaert
Mason Miller Back From the Paternity List for Game 4


Keith Hernandez




Oct 7, 2026, 8:03 PM ET
The San Diego Padres announced on Wednesday that they returned right-handed closer Mason Miller from the paternity list, taking the place on the National League Division Series roster of left-handed reliever Wandy Peralta. Miller blew a two-inning save in Game 2 of the series in Milwaukee against the Brewers and was then unavailable for the win in Game 3 at Petco Park on Tuesday night. It is great news for the Padres, who did not have left-handed high-leverage reliever Adrian Morejon on Tuesday due to a left-shoulder issue. The Padres had to go to Game 1 starter, right-hander Michael King, for the two-inning save with both Miller and Morejon unavailable. It is uncertain if Morejon will be able to pitch late in the game in another must-win contest on Wednesday in Game 4, but the Padres will at least have their stud closer back in the fold. The two-time All-Star was lights-out during the regular season, his first full season with the Friars, posting a 1.67 ERA (1.17 FIP), 0.900 WHIP, a career-high and league-high 38 saves, a career-high 129 strikeouts, and 26 walks in just 70 innings pitched. With their season on the line, expect manager Craig Stammen to be aggressive in his usage of Miller if Game 4 is close in the later innings, even though he showed command issues in the ninth on Sunday in Milwaukee.--Keith Hernandez
Source: San Diego Padres
Miguel Rojas Not Worried About Back/Hip Injury


Keith Hernandez




Oct 7, 2026, 12:28 PM ET
Los Angeles Dodgers veteran infielder Miguel Rojas (back, hip) said he felt some tightness in his left lower-back/hip area during a swing in Game 3 of the National League Division Series on Tuesday against the hosting Atlanta Braves before he was pulled mid at-bat, according to Fabian Ardaya of The Athletic. However, Rojas was not concerned about his availability for the rest of the series and going forward. Rojas probably will not be in the Dodgers' starting lineup for Game 4 of the series on Wednesday at Truist Park against Braves right-hander Tyler Mahle, but it sounds like he should be available off the bench. The 37-year-old Venezuelan infielder has made two starts so far in the NLDS against the Braves and has gone 1-for-4 with a double and a strikeout. He was hitless in three at-bats with a strikeout in Tuesday's Game 3 win before being replaced at second base by Tommy Edman. Rojas has mostly been a bench player for the Dodgers in his 13th year in the league (fourth with L.A.) in 2026, but he proved in last year's World Series that he is still capable of coming through in the clutch when needed. He hit .267 (60-for-225) with four homers and 23 RBI during the regular season.--Keith Hernandez
Source: The Athletic - Fabian Ardaya
Oct 7, 2026, 11:57 AM ET
St. Louis Cardinals right-handed closer Riley O'Brien was a first-time All-Star in 2026 in his first full season as the team's closer, and he ended the year tied with San Diego Padres closer Mason Miller for the National League lead in saves (38) with a 4.08 ERA across a career-high 64 innings pitched. O'Brien also set a career high in appearances (66) in his first full year as a big-leaguer. He did not allow an earned run in his first 13 appearances of the year and ended the first half with a 3.43 ERA and a 7.9% walk rate in 39 1/3 frames. O'Brien had 24 saves in his first 28 opportunities. But in 27 appearances after the All-Star break, O'Brien had a 5.11 ERA in 24 2/3 innings, and his walk rate rose to 14.4% while he went 14-for-18 in save chances. Three of his blown saves in the second half came in September, and five of his losing decisions came in his final 13 outings. The 31-year-old said he experienced "fatigue" in the closing days of the season and that his legs have "been feeling heavy compared to how they felt early in the year," according to Daniel Guerrero of the St. Louis Post-Dispatch. As he tired, the velocity of O'Brien's pitches suffered. To be able to maintain velocity through the entire season, O'Brien said he plans to focus on putting on "as much muscle as I can."--Keith Hernandez
Source: St. Louis Post-Dispatch - Daniel Guerrero
Curtis Mead the Favorite to Start at Second Base Next Year


Keith Hernandez




Oct 7, 2026, 11:47 AM ET
Boston Red Sox infielder Curtis Mead is considered the favorite to open next season as the team's starting second baseman, according to Tim Healey of The Boston Globe. The Red Sox acquired Mead from the Washington Nationals at the trade deadline this summer, but he ended up playing in only one game for Boston due to a fractured wrist that he suffered in his second at-bat with the team. The 25-year-old will now have all offseason to heal up, and he will enter spring training as the team's primary option at the keystone as they attempt to get back to the playoffs in 2027. The Australian native was having a breakout 2026 campaign with the Nationals before being traded to Boston, and he finished the year with a .253/.353/.498 slash line with an .851 OPS, 17 home runs, 48 RBI, 49 runs scored, and six stolen bases in 285 at-bats in 88 combined games with Washington and Boston. "That would be, I would say, broadly our plan," said manager Chad Tracy when asked about second base. "He was acquired for a reason. You see the numbers that kind of project at least toward a 30-home run season. And adding that, we were really excited about that."--Keith Hernandez
Source: The Boston Globe - Tim Healey
Walker Buehler to Start Game 4 of NLDS Against Brewers


Keith Hernandez




Oct 7, 2026, 11:36 AM ET
The San Diego Padres announced that veteran right-hander Walker Buehler will make the start in Game 4 of the National League Division Series on Wednesday night at Petco Park against the visiting Milwaukee Brewers. Buehler will make his first postseason appearance this year after going 9-6 with a 4.63 ERA (4.51 FIP) and 1.35 WHIP with 131 strikeouts and 57 walks in 153 2/3 innings pitched across his 32 starts for the Padres in his first season with the team. The 32-year-old is no longer the high-end ace that he was with the Los Angeles Dodgers, but he does have plenty of postseason experience, posting a 3.04 ERA (3.21 FIP) with 114 strikeouts and 36 walks in 94 2/3 innings pitched. Buehler's last start came on Sept. 26 against the division-rival Arizona Diamondbacks, when he allowed four runs (three earned) with a walk and three strikeouts in just 3 2/3 innings for a no-decision. He picked up a win in his only outing against Milwaukee in 2026, giving up just one earned run with two walks and five strikeouts in six innings at Petco Park back on Aug. 11. Buehler will most definitely be on a short leash in a must-win game for San Diego if he is not on his game early on.--Keith Hernandez
Source: Padres PR
Adrian Morejon Dealing With "Stickiness in his Shoulder"


Keith Hernandez




Oct 7, 2026, 11:28 AM ET
San Diego Padres left-handed reliever Adrian Morejon (shoulder) was unavailable in Game 3 of the National League Division Series at Petco Park on Tuesday night against the Milwaukee Brewers due to "stickiness in his shoulder," manager Craig Stammen told AJ Cassavell of MLB.com. There is still a chance that Morejon will be available for Game 4 against the Brewers in San Diego on Wednesday night as the Friars attempt to force a Game 5 back in Milwaukee on Friday night. With Morejon unavailable and closer Mason Miller on the paternity list, the Padres' bullpen was very short on Tuesday night, but Game 1 starter Michael King came to the rescue and threw the final two innings for SD to pick up a save in the 4-3 victory. Morejon has already had two two-inning appearances in this postseason, once in the Wild-Card Series against the Chicago Cubs and again on Saturday against the Brewers in Game of the NLDS, when he allowed the game-winning home run to catcher William Contreras. The hard-throwing Cuban left-hander was one of the most effective late-inning setup men during the regular season, though, going 9-3 with a 2.83 ERA, 1.08 WHIP, three saves, and a career-high 107 strikeouts in just 86 innings out of the bullpen. With Miller unlikely to be back with the team on Wednesday, the Padres could really use Morejon's left arm on Wednesday evening.--Keith Hernandez
Source: MLB.com - AJ Cassavell
Oct 6, 2026, 10:58 PM ET
Los Angeles Dodgers first baseman Freddie Freeman was one of the stars of his team's 3-1 win over the Atlanta Braves in Game 3 of the National League Division Series on Tuesday. Freeman had just one hit in four plate appearances, but it was a solo home run off Braves ace Chris Sale. Freeman put together another strong regular season in 2026, hitting .288/.362/.430 with 16 home runs, 70 RBI, 74 runs scored, and seven stolen bases. The 37-year-old's production tailed off late in the year, as he hit just .184 in September and slugged just one home run across 249 plate appearances after the All-Star break. However, Freeman has looked like his vintage self so far this postseason. Across the first three games of the NLDS, Freeman has logged four hits, two home runs, two RBI, and three runs scored.--Will Brady
Source: ESPN.com
Oct 6, 2026, 10:40 PM ET
Los Angeles Dodgers utility man Enrique Hernandez struck one of the big blows of his team's 3-1 win over the Atlanta Braves in Game 3 of the National League Division Series on Tuesday, clubbing a two-run home run off of Braves ace Chris Sale to open the scoring in the fourth inning. It was Hernandez's only hit of the night, but it helped the Dodgers chase Sale out of the game after just five innings of work. Hernandez missed a large chunk of the regular season with an oblique injury and was not particularly effective when healthy, hitting .222 with four home runs across 96 plate appearances. However, the 35-year-old has a long history as an unlikely postseason hero. Across 332 career plate appearances in the playoffs, Hernandez has now hit .272 with 18 home runs and 44 RBI.--Will Brady
Source: ESPN.com

item.content:encoded:
After being swept out of last year's NLCS, Pat Murphy and the Milwaukee Brewers look to turn the page in this year's edition with a rematch against the reigning back-to-back champion Los Angeles Dodgers.
Milwaukee heads into the NLCS after defeating the San Diego Padres in the NLDS (3-1), with Los Angeles advancing thanks to its 3-1 series win over the Atlanta Braves.
Find everything you need to know about the series below:
The 2026 MLB postseason has arrived. Stay up to date with the latest results and more.
When is the Dodgers vs. Brewers 2026 MLB NLCS?
The Dodgers and Brewers will begin their best-of-seven series on Sunday, Oct. 11. See the full schedule below.
How to watch Dodgers vs. Brewers: TV channel, live stream
Fans can watch the entire Dodgers-Brewers NLCS on FOX and FS1. Spanish-language coverage will be available on FOX Deportes.
Dodgers vs. Brewers 2026 MLB National League Championship Series full schedule
| Game | Date | Location | Time |
| Game 1 | Sunday, Oct. 11 | American Family Field | TBD |
| Game 2 | Monday, Oct. 12 | American Family Field | TBD |
| Game 3 | Wednesday, Oct. 14 | Dodger Stadium | TBD |
| Game 4 | Thursday, Oct. 15 | Dodger Stadium | TBD |
| Game 5* | Friday, Oct. 16 | Dodger Stadium | TBD |
| Game 6* | Sunday, Oct. 18 | American Family Field | TBD |
| Game 7* | Monday, Oct. 19 | American Family Field | TBD |
* = if necessary
Where will the Dodgers vs. Brewers League Championship Series be played?
Games 1 and 2 will be played in Milwaukee at American Family Field, with Games 3 and 4 moving to Dodger Stadium in Los Angeles. Should the series go past four, Dodger Stadium will host Game 5 before the series heads back to Milwaukee for Games 6 and 7.
Dodgers vs. Brewers probable starting pitchers
Starters for Game 1 and beyond are TBD.
Dodgers vs. Brewers 2026 season series results
The Brewers narrowly finished on top in their season series with the Dodgers, winning four of seven in 2026.
Dodgers vs. Brewers playoff history
The Dodgers and Brewers have met three times in the postseason, where Los Angeles has defeated Milwaukee in each matchup.
- 2025 NLCS: Dodgers win 4-0
- 2020 Wild Card Series: Dodgers win 2-0
- 2018 NLCS: Dodgers win 4-3
How does the MLB League Championship Series format work?
The NLCS and ALCS are best-of-seven series. The higher seed receives home-field advantage for the series, with Games 1-2 and potential Games 6-7 hosted by the higher seed and Games 3-5 hosted by the lower seed. The first team to win four games will take the series and advance to the World Series.

item.content:encoded:
To the victors go the spoils and the Tampa Bay Rays have earned every right to crow.
The plucky upstarts, who happened to win the American League East with the junior circuit's best record this year, completed a three-game sweep over the mighty New York Yankees on Wednesday night to secure a spot in the ALCS.
MORE: Jazz Chisholm 'confused' by Yankees' fans reaction
Everything this team does well was on full display as unheralded players continuously rose to the occasion. Junior Caminero, the Rays' sole superstar, went 3-for-10 in the series and worked two walks. Though he did not contribute much in the realm of power, the third baseman had plenty of energy to take up the mantle as chief trash-talker after the final out was recorded.
Caminero threw out a bit of everything in his defiant celebration. First there was the exaggerated sweeping motion to let a dejected Yankees Stadium crowd know just how thoroughly their beloved team had been beaten.
He continued the revelry by channeling David Ortiz and bellowing about the Yankees' loss.
Once in the clubhouse, his fire only burned brighter and by the time those suds-soaked interviews began, he was under the impression he was the best in the world.
There are a lot of not very fun people out there who shame baseball teams for celebrating like they've just won the World Series on every step to winning the World Series. By the time the Fall Classic wraps a squad can have four or five of these out-of-control parties under their belt.
And to be clear, most of them don't age well because only one franchise can win the whole dang thing.
But here's a rebuttal. Baseball is an insane marathon and there are thousands upon thousands of boring hours against the actual game action. Teams are together for seven or eight months and need every excuse they can to blow off some steam and celebrate what they've accomplished together.
Just think of how much Yankees fans are going to hate Caminero for his entire career now based on just a few clips. That is, if they don't use their considerable funds to take him away from small-market Tampa in a couple years. None of that would be possible without carte blanche to party it up and take every available opportunity to twist the knife.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers will play for another National League pennant.
The two-time reigning World Series champions have advanced to a third straight National League Championship Series. No. 2-seeded Los Angeles took down the No. 3 Atlanta Braves in four games in the NLDS of the 2026 MLB playoffs.
Los Angeles now awaits the winner of the other NLDS matchup between the No. 1 Milwaukee Brewers and No. 4 San Diego Padres. The Dodgers are looking to pull off the rare feat of a World Series three-peat.
As the next round of the MLB postseason takes shape, here's what to know for the NLCS and ALCS:
How many games are in the ALCS, NLCS?
The remainder of the MLB postseason will feature best-of-seven series. The higher seed hosts Games 1 and 2, along with the potential Games 6 and 7.
When does the 2026 NLCS start?
The NLCS begins Sunday, Oct. 11.
What is the 2026 NLCS schedule?
The Dodgers will have home-field advantage if they face the Padres. Otherwise, the NLCS will begin in Milwaukee.
Here's what we know about the NLCS schedule:
- Game 1: TBD at TBD -- Oct. 11, time TBD, network TBD
- Game 2: TBD at TBD, -- Oct. 12, time TBD, network TBD
- Game 3: TBD at TBD -- Oct. 14, time TBD, network TBD
- Game 4: TBD at TBD -- Oct. 15, time TBD, network TBD
- Game 5 (if necessary): TBD at TBD -- Oct. 16 time TBD, network TBD
- Game 6 (if necessary): TBD at TBD -- Oct. 18, time TBD, network TBD
- Game 7 (if necessary): TBD at TBD -- Oct. 19, time TBD, network TBD
When does the 2026 ALCS start?
The ALCS starts Monday, Oct. 12.
What is the 2026 ALCS schedule?
No team has emerged from the ALDS just yet. The ALCS will pit the winner of the No. 1 Tampa Bay Rays-No. 4 New York Yankees series against the winner of the No. 2 Cleveland Guardians-No. 6 Chicago White Sox series.
Here's what we know about the ALCS schedule:
- Game 1: TBD at TBD -- Oct. 12, time TBD, TBS and HBO Max
- Game 2: TBD at TBD, -- Oct. 13, time TBD, TBS and HBO Max
- Game 3: TBD at TBD -- Oct. 15, time TBD, TBS and HBO Max
- Game 4: TBD at TBD -- Oct. 16, time TBD, TBS and HBO Max
- Game 5 (if necessary): TBD at TBD -- Oct. 17 time TBD, TBS and HBO Max
- Game 6 (if necessary): TBD at TBD -- Oct. 19, time TBD, TBS and HBO Max
- Game 7 (if necessary): TBD at TBD -- Oct. 20, time TBD, TBS and HBO Max
Where to watch, stream the ALCS and NLCS games
NLCS games will air across FOX and FS1, and can be streamed on FOX One and FOXSports.com.
All ALCS contests will be shown on TBS and can be streamed on TBS.com, the TBS app and HBO Max.
When does the 2026 World Series start?
Game 1 of the Fall Classic is scheduled for Friday, Oct. 23.

item.title: [MLB.com] Rays-Yankees ALDS Game 3 FAQ (Wed., 8 p.m. ET, TBS/HBO Max)
item.dc:creator: Adam Berry; Bryan Hoch
item.description: NEW YORK -- Two weeks ago, the Rays went wild in the visitors’ clubhouse at Yankee Stadium after clinching their first American League East championship in five years. That party started shortly after a win over the Yankees and carried late into the New York night. Could they have another celebration in store in the Bronx? It’s time for the American League Division Series to shift venues, going from the Rays’ home dome at Tropicana Field to Yankee Stadium for Game 3 on Wednesday night. But the R
item.content:encoded:
NEW YORK -- Two weeks ago, the Rays went wild in the visitors’ clubhouse at Yankee Stadium after clinching their first American League East championship in five years. That party started shortly after a win over the Yankees and carried late into the New York night.
Could they have another celebration in store in the Bronx?
It’s time for the American League Division Series to shift venues, going from the Rays’ home dome at Tropicana Field to Yankee Stadium for Game 3 on Wednesday night. But the Rays are still right where they want to be, holding a commanding 2-0 lead in the series with three chances to advance to the AL Championship Series.
“It's amazing, man. It's exactly the way we wanted to start the series,” Rays closer Bryan Baker said. “To be able to play in front of these fans in this building and take a 2-0 series lead was exactly what we wanted, so it feels really good right now.”
Maybe home-field advantage is what the Yankees need after coming up empty against Rays ace Drew Rasmussen in Game 1 and kicking the ball around the infield in a mistake-filled Game 2 defeat. Or maybe it’ll help to send left-hander Max Fried to the mound, knowing how tough he’s been on Tampa Bay throughout his career.
“We've got to get over it,” Yankees manager Aaron Boone said after Game 2. “We've responded all year to difficult times, and we've got to do that again. We've got to get ourselves up off the mat.”
Tampa Bay’s pitching staff held what looked like a red-hot New York lineup to only two runs in the first 18 innings of this series. If the Rays keep that up, they could enjoy another champagne-soaked night in the city that never sleeps.
“I think it's sweet either way. Doesn't matter the clubhouse,” Rays center fielder Jonny DeLuca said. “Obviously, going over there, having the chance to do that would be pretty special.”
When is the game and how can I watch it?
First pitch for Game 3 of the Yankees-Rays Division Series is set for 8 p.m. ET on Wednesday at Yankee Stadium. The game will be broadcast on TBS, truTV and HBO Max.
The ALDS will be available in Spanish on UniMas, while Univision’s TUDN Radio will provide Spanish-language audio coverage. ESPN Radio will provide live national coverage of all 2026 MLB Postseason games.
Who are the starting pitchers?
Rays: Nick Martinez, RHP
Key stats: 7-3, 2.38 ERA in 16 road starts this season
After rolling out Rasmussen in Game 1 and Freddy Peralta in Game 2, Martinez was the logical choice for the Rays with the series moving to the Bronx. The veteran right-hander was a reliable presence on the mound for Tampa Bay all season, as he posted a 3.10 ERA over 180 innings while the club went 22-9 in his starts. He was at his best on the road, including two outings in the Bronx. The first-time All-Star held the Yankees to only three runs over 12 innings in their home ballpark.
Yankees: Max Fried, LHP
Key stats: 5-1, 1.81 ERA in 7 career GS vs. Tampa Bay
Fried is coming off a sharp outing against the Red Sox in the decisive Game 2 of the AL Wild Card Series, holding Boston to a run on three hits over six innings. Fried walked one and struck out six, his third postseason start since joining the Yankees.
This will be Fried’s third time facing the Rays this season. He last saw them on Sept. 22 in New York, taking the loss in a 6 2/3-inning effort as Tampa Bay clinched the AL East.
Fried also went up against the Rays on April 11 at Tropicana Field, taking a no-decision after permitting three runs over eight innings. For his career, Fried is 5-1 with a 1.81 ERA in seven starts vs. Tampa Bay, including 3-0 with a 0.84 ERA in three starts during the 2025 season.
What might the starting lineups look like?
Rays: It seems likely the Rays will change things up a bit against the Yankees’ left-handers, opting for the right-handed side of most platoons and leaving their lefty hitters available off the bench. Here’s one potential look for a more right-handed lineup.
Yankees: The Yankees have used the same lefty-heavy lineup three times this postseason against right-handed pitchers, including twice in the ALDS. Boone said he is considering shaking things up for Game 3. Boone said before Game 2 that he was considering starting Anthony Volpe at third base. Jose Caballero and Paul Goldschmidt could also enter the mix.
How will the bullpens line up after the starter?
Rays: The Rays really couldn’t be in much better shape thanks to their starting rotation. Rasmussen handled eight innings in Game 1, and the duo of Peralta and Ian Seymour combined to work 7 2/3 innings in Game 2. So, their traditional relievers have recorded seven of the 54 outs so far this series: six from Baker and a big one from lefty Cam Booser. They may not turn to Peralta or Seymour in Game 3, but they still have starter Griffin Jax available -- and the Yankees have yet to face setup men Tyler Wells and Kevin Kelly in this series.
Yankees: Ryan Weathers replaced infielder/outfielder Amed Rosario for this series, returning from a left flexor strain sustained in late August. David Bednar, Paul Blackburn and Brent Headrick should all be leaned upon for high-leverage outs. Will Warren is now in the bullpen after appearing in 32 games (29 starts) during the regular season. Warren made one appearance in the Wild Card Series, tossing 1 2/3 innings.
Any injuries of note?
Rays: Nothing new. Everyone who was expected to be available for this series is on the roster. The most notable injury situation to watch moving forward is that of left-hander Shane McClanahan, whose status is unclear except that he will not pitch in this series.
Yankees: Aaron Judge was left off the ALDS roster, though Boone said it was a “close” call. Judge has yet to run the bases as he recovers from a right calf strain, though he has been performing outfield running. He has also been taking numerous live at-bats while throwing. Clarke Schmidt has been ruled out for the remainder of the postseason.
Who is hot and who is not?
Rays: Aranda doesn’t get as much love as the other members of the “Big Three,” but his left-handed bat is key. He hit better than either Caminero or Díaz in September, and he had the lone big hit of the night in Game 1 before picking up two more hits in Game 2. Richie Palacios finished strong, too, posting a .981 OPS with five homers in September before delivering the biggest hit of Game 2, and the Brooklyn native likes hitting against his hometown Yankees. Tampa Bay’s entire rotation surged into the postseason, highlighted by Rasmussen and Peralta, the September AL Pitcher of the Month.
The Rays’ outfield is off to a slow start in this series, offensively, but they all showed the impact they can have by putting the ball in play in Game 2. And their defense has been consistently excellent.
Yankees: Rice has been the Yankees' most productive hitter in the postseason, and given how the ALDS has gone, it hasn't been particularly close. Rice is 7-for-15 (.467) in the playoffs, including his two-homer performance in ALDS Game 2. Rice has four homers and eight RBIs overall. Wells is 5-for-12 (.417) in the playoffs, including a couple of doubles in the ALDS. Everyone except for Rice and Wells has combined to go 1-for-46 (.022) in the ALDS so far.
Anything else fans might want to know?
• The Yankees won four of the six games these clubs played in the Bronx during the regular season, splitting a pair of games in late May, then taking three of four the final week of the season. However, the Rays have already celebrated once at Yankee Stadium, as they clinched the AL East title with a 6-1 win in the second half of a doubleheader on Sept. 22.

item.title: [roundtable.io] How White Sox Turned ‘Organized Chaos’ Into a Postseason Weapon
item.dc:creator: Sam Phalen
item.description: Chicago's unconventional pitching plan has dominated October, but its postseason success was built through a full season of preparation. Now just one win away from advancing to the ALCS, it's becoming undeniable that this group has a little bit of magic to it. These White Sox are young, hungry, and they don't know what they don't know. They show up to the ballpark every day believing they can win. And sometimes in the postseason, that spirit is enough to carry a team. Baseball, however, isn't ju
item.content:encoded:
Chicago's unconventional pitching plan has dominated October, but its postseason success was built through a full season of preparation.
Now just one win away from advancing to the ALCS, it's becoming undeniable that this group has a little bit of magic to it. These White Sox are young, hungry, and they don't know what they don't know.
They show up to the ballpark every day believing they can win. And sometimes in the postseason, that spirit is enough to carry a team.
Baseball, however, isn't just watching Chicago with admiration for the Cinderella story at hand. There's also a somewhat unprecedented strategy being deployed by the White Sox this October, one that could change the way teams shape their pitching staffs moving forward if this level of success continues.
Organized chaos.
That's what the White Sox call their pitching strategy for the postseason.
Right-hander Sean Burke is the only truly reliable traditional starting pitcher the White Sox have on their playoff roster. So Chicago has largely thrown standard pitching roles out the window. Manager Will Venable plays the matchups on a nearly pitch-by-pitch basis, deploying an all-hands-on-deck approach to cover the 27 outs necessary for victory.
Unconventional? Absolutely. But it's also been remarkably effective.
Even Burke hasn't been used as a traditional starting pitcher. And why would he be?
Burke entered Monday's ALDS Game 2 against the Cleveland Guardians in the third inning after Chicago used two openers to begin the game. The White Sox wanted to roll out a pair of left-handers, Anthony Kay and Sean Newcomb, to navigate the top of Cleveland's lineup and neutralize its dangerous left-handed bats before turning things over to Burke.
The strategy also shortened the game for Burke, allowing him to attack hitters without worrying about pacing himself for a traditional six- or seven-inning start.
He was lights out.
Burke pitched into the bottom of the eighth inning and likely could have kept going. At one point, he set a franchise postseason record with 13 consecutive batters retired. Then with the White Sox nursing a 4-2 lead, Venable ultimately decided there was no reason to push it.
The White Sox have now allowed just nine total runs over four postseason games while pitching to a 1.75 team ERA.
All anybody wants to know is how they've managed to make it work. After all, it's not like the White Sox had an incredible pitching staff throughout the regular season. Their 4.12 team ERA was right around the MLB average.
Not to mention, this is an incredibly young White Sox team with plenty of young arms. Many of them are getting their first taste of playoff baseball during this current run. And inexperienced pitchers are usually expected to show some signs of fatigue this late in the season as they blow past previous career highs in innings pitched.
Instead, the opposite has happened. The deeper the White Sox have gotten into the season, the more dominant their pitching staff has become.
So why is it working for Chicago?
Because the White Sox put it into practice during the regular season.
Consistency has been a primary focus for Venable as he takes this young team into the postseason. He wants players in the same positions, doing things they're familiar with. His message in pregame speeches hasn't changed. And when it comes to the pitching staff, they're comfortable being used as Swiss Army knives because that's how they've been deployed all year.
Instead, Chicago learned how to survive without one.
Using an opener in front of a starting pitcher, throwing a bullpen game, asking relievers to cover multiple innings. These are all things the White Sox did during the regular season to get themselves into the playoffs.
Nothing about what Venable is asking his pitchers to do in October is foreign to them. The stakes are higher and the margin for error is smaller, but the roles themselves haven't suddenly changed.
"Organized chaos" from the pitching staff was a necessity for the White Sox to survive 162 games. Now it's becoming a weapon in the postseason.
The young right-hander admitted Chicago's original plan for the game went a bit haywire after Cleveland scored two runs in the first inning, forcing Venable to make an earlier-than-expected move to the bullpen for Newcomb.
But Burke was prepared for the unconventional situation, in part because he leaned on teammates who had already experienced similar roles.
He specifically mentioned Erick Fedde, Sean Newcomb and White Sox bullpen coach Matt Wise as people he leaned on while establishing a routine and rhythm for entering a game after it had already started.
It's another example of why Chicago's organized chaos works. The White Sox aren't improvising in October. They're leaning on the versatility, preparation and experience they spent an entire season developing. Keeping things consistent is an underrated aspect of playoff baseball.
For many teams, the bright lights of October make them tighten up. There's a misconception that you need to play differently and treat these games differently simply because they mean more.
And yes, fundamentally sound baseball becomes increasingly important when the margin for error shrinks. But the White Sox are showing how familiarity, comfort and playing loose can actually be the key to postseason success.
That includes the unconventional approach to team pitching.
It doesn't matter if you're a starter or reliever. It doesn't matter if you're being asked to pitch five innings or throw five pitches. The goal is the same: Get 27 outs.
Guys like Burke are flexible enough to make it work. Venable has continued pushing all the right buttons. And the White Sox have built a pitching staff that's comfortable operating without the traditional roles that have defined the sport for generations.
It started as a necessity during the regular season. It's become one of Chicago's greatest strengths in October.
And if this White Sox playoff run continues, don't be surprised if more teams around Major League Baseball start trying to replicate it.

item.title: [cbssports.com] MLB playoff winners and losers: White Sox one win from ALCS thanks to a trade from two years ago

item.content:encoded:
The 2026 MLB postseason continues Monday with Game 2 of both American League Division Series. The Chicago White Sox continued their perfect start to the playoffs, winning again over the Cleveland Guardians to take a 2-0 series lead. The White Sox are now 4-0 in the postseason, with all four victories coming on the road.
The New York Yankees, meanwhile, are trying to even their series against the Tampa Bay Rays behind Cy Young favorite Cam Schlittler.
Since the best-of-five Division Series became a thing in 1995, the team that won Game 1 has gone on to win the series 73% of the time, and 32% of the time the series ended in a sweep. Winning Game 1 doesn't guarantee a series win, but the White Sox and Rays are in the driver's seat at the moment. Here are the final scores and schedule for Monday's playoff action:
- FINAL: White Sox 4, Guardians 3 (box score); White Sox lead series 2-0
- LIVE: Yankees at Rays (GameTracker); Rays lead series 1-0
To sum up all the ALDS Game 2 action, we're here to declare a winner and loser from both games. You can find those authoritative and inarguable declarations just below.
Winner: The Garrett Crochet trade
For the second time this postseason, the three position players the White Sox received in the Garrett Crochet trade with the Red Sox guided them to a win. , and in Game 2 of the ALDS on Monday. Those three players -- Chase Meidroth, Braden Montgomery, Kyle Teel -- went a combined 4 for 12 with 3 RBI.
Teel helped the White Sox get on the board with his leadoff single in the fourth inning. He later came around to score Chicago's first run on a Munetaka Murakami single. Montgomery provided the game's biggest blow. He drove a two-out, two-run double to right field in the sixth inning, which flipped a 2-1 deficit into a 3-2 lead for the White Sox. This, as the kids say, is a nice piece of hitting:
Meidroth followed with a single to right to score Montgomery and give the White Sox what proved to be an important insurance run. The Crochet trade bounty had four of Chicago's six hits in Game 2 and either scored or drove in all four runs. Sean Burke, who was not part of the Crochet trade, threw 5 ⅓ innings of one-run ball behind a pair of openers. He struck out six. He was terrific.
The White Sox did not want to trade Crochet two years ago. They'd just lost a modern record 121 games, however, and needed to add talent up and down the roster. So, Crochet was dealt to Boston, and it sure seems like GM Chris Getz nailed the trade. Three of the four players he received in the deal are playing major roles in October. This is how you draw it up.
are now one win away from their first ALCS since their 2005 World Series win.
Loser: GuardsBall
It is really, really hard to hit in the postseason. Don't believe me? Teams came into Monday hitting .211/.293/.352 this postseason, and .174/.277/.295 in the Division Series. The pitchers are so nasty, they're well-rested thanks to the built-in off-days, and their matchups are all optimized. Every base hit in the postseason is a tiny little miracle, I swear.
The Guardians, two games into their postseason run, are learning that the hard way. They were shut out in Game 1 and held to three hits. In Game 2, they had only four hits, three of which were singles. To date, Cleveland's biggest offensive play in the ALDS is Sean Newcomb's two-run throwing error in the first inning Monday. Here are two of the three runs the Guardians scored in Game 2 (and in the series):
Including Newcomb's error, four of the first five Guardians reached base in Game 2. Only four of the final 30 reached base, most notably Jo Adell's RBI triple in the eighth inning. With all due respect, this is not a dominant White Sox pitching staff. They've had to cobble it together with openers and bullpen games this postseason. Credit to them for keeping Cleveland in check.
The Guardians are not exactly an offensive powerhouse though. They ranked 24th in runs and 27th in home runs during the regular season. It's the same story every year. The Guardians rally in the second half to win the AL Central, then have a hard time putting points on the board in October. That is certainly the case this year. Three runs on seven hits through two ALDS games. Yeesh.
Cleveland is one loss away from elimination. The Guardians are 2-8 in their last 10 postseason games dating back to 2024.
