item.content:encoded:
As summer comes to a close and the air turns crisp, you know what's coming: the MLB Playoffs. The NFL season is already underway, and if you're also a baseball lover, this next month is essential viewing. The MLB has been through a number of changes in recent years. From the universal DH and the pitch clock to video replay and an automated strike zone, baseball may look very different if you haven't been paying attention.
This week, all Division Series matchups continue with the White Sox vs. Guardians, Braves vs. Dodgers, Yankees vs. Rays, and Padres vs. Brewers. American League games continue tonight, while National League matchups will pick up tomorrow. Don't want to miss a minute of the action? Here's how you can watch live.
What Time Is the White Sox vs. Guardians Game 2?
Today's game between the Chicago White Sox and Cleveland Guardians will take place on Monday, October 5 at 5 p.m. ET.
What Time Is the Yankees vs. Rays Game 2?
Today's game between the New York Yankees and Tampa Bay Rays will take place on Monday, October 5 at 8:00 p.m. ET.
What Time Is the Braves vs. Dodgers Game 3?
Tomorrow's game between the Atlanta Braves and Los Angeles Dodgers will take place on Tuesday, October 6 at 6 p.m. ET.
What Time Is the Padres vs. Brewers Game 3?
Tomorrow's game between the San Diego Padres and Milwaukee Brewers will take place on Tuesday, October 6 at 9:30 p.m. ET.
How to Watch the MLB Division Series Games
American League Division Series games will be broadcast on TBS, while National League games will be on Fox and FS1. You can also watch them with a live TV or sports streaming subscription from DirecTV, Fox One, Fubo, HBO Max, Hulu, Sling, Sportsnet+ (if you're in Canada), or YouTube TV.
How to Watch the Games For Free
If you don't want to subscribe to any of the above platforms, you may be able to sign up for a few free trials to gain access to this weekend's games. Fox One and Hulu offer three-day trials, DirecTV and Fubo offer five days, and YouTube TV gives you 10 days for free.
2026 MLB Playoffs Game Schedule
MLB's expanded postseason means more teams on the playoff schedule. Things started off with the best-of-three Wild Card Series, where the Braves, Padres, White Sox, and Yankees advanced. Now, the best-of-five Division Series starts October 3. The Cleveland Guardians, Tampa Bay Rays, Los Angeles Dodgers, and Milwaukee Brewers will meet them.
After this round, the Championship Series extends to seven games to determine the best team in each league, who then advance to a best-of-seven World Series. Who will make it all the way?
Chicago White Sox vs. Cleveland Guardians - CWS lead 1-0:
- Game 2 on October 5 @ 5:00 p.m. ET - TBS/HBO Max
- Game 3 on October 7 @ 4:00 p.m. ET - TBS/HBO Max
- Game 4 on October 8 @ 5:00 p.m. ET - TBS/HBO Max
- Game 5 on October 10 @ 5:00 p.m. ET - TBS/HBO Max
Atlanta Braves vs. Los Angeles Dodgers - Series tied 1-1:
- Game 3 on October 6 @ 6:00 p.m. ET - FS1/Fox One
- Game 4 on October 7 @ 6:00 p.m. ET - FS1/Fox One
- Game 5 on October 9 @ 8:00 p.m. ET - Fox/Fox One
New York Yankees vs. Tampa Bay Rays - TBR lead 1-0:
- Game 2 on October 5 @ 8:00 p.m. ET - TBS/HBO Max
- Game 3 on October 7 @ 8:00 p.m. ET - TBS/HBO Max
- Game 4 on October 8 @ 8:00 p.m. ET - TBS/HBO Max
- Game 5 on October 10 @ 8:00 p.m. ET - TBS/HBO Max
San Diego Padres vs. Milwaukee Brewers - MIL lead 2-0:
- Game 3 on October 6 @ 9:30 p.m. ET - FS1/Fox One
- Game 4 on October 7 @ 10:00 p.m. ET - FS1/Fox One
- Game 5 on October 9 @ 4:30 p.m. ET - FS1/Fox One
How to Stream the 2026 MLB Playoffs
This year's MLB postseason is stretched across multiple networks and streaming services. All Wild Card Series games for the American League and National League were broadcast on NBC, NBCSN, and Peacock. Additional rounds will be on other networks. ALDS and ALCS games are on TBS/TruTV and HBO Max, while NLDS and NLCS games are on Fox/FS1. For the World Series, all games will be broadcast on Fox and the Fox One streaming service.
- DirecTV: DirecTV's MySports base pack costs $45 per month for the first six months to see every game on Fox, FS1, NBC, and TBS/TruTV.
- Fox One: Fox's own streaming app lets you watch the NLDS, NLCS, and World Series on Fox and FS1 for $20 per month.
- Fubo: Fubo's Sports plan costs $45.99 for the first month to watch the Wild Card Series, NLDS, NLCS, and World Series on Fox, FS1, and NBC/NBCSN.
- HBO Max: If you pay for the $18.49-per-month HBO Max Standard, you'll be able to watch the ALDS and ALCS games on TBS/TruTV.
- Hulu: For $90 per month, you can watch every game on Fox, FS1, NBC, TBS, and TruTV.
- Peacock: Instead of a live TV service, you'd need to pay $10.99 per month for Peacock Premium to see the Wild Card Series games.
- Sling: The $60.99-per-month Sling Orange & Blue bundle will let you watch the ALDS and ALCS on TBS/TruTV and the NLDS and NLCS on FS1. Day Passes are also available for Sling Orange, allowing you to watch games on TBS for up to seven days.
- Sportsnet+ (Canada only): The $30-per-month Standard tier lets you watch every postseason game.
- YouTube TV: Though the standard plan for YouTube TV costs $83 per month, you can actually now pay for the cheaper $65 Sports package to see all games on Fox, FS1, NBC/NBCSN, and TBS/TruTV.
Can I Watch Postseason Games on MLB.TV?
Are you already an MLB.TV subscriber? You can watch the Division Series, Championship Series, and World Series games through MLB's own streaming service—but there's a catch. To watch on MLB.TV, you'll first need to authenticate through a participating pay TV provider. It's such a sticking point that it makes the entire question moot. If you already have a TV provider, then you wouldn't need to use a streaming service. If you don't already have an MLB.TV subscription, don't pay for one now.
How can I listen to the 2026 postseason?
You can also listen to the games via ESPN Radio.
Which Teams Are In the Playoffs?
Since MLB expanded its postseason picture in 2022, a total of 12 teams make the playoffs each year. That includes six teams per league, including the three division winners and three Wild Card teams.
- American League Division Winners: Tampa Bay Rays (1), Cleveland Guardians (2), Houston Astros (3)
- American League Wild Card: New York Yankees (4), Boston Red Sox (5), Chicago White Sox (6)
- National League Division Winners: Milwaukee Brewers (1), Los Angeles Dodgers (2), Atlanta Braves (3)
- National League Wild Card: Chicago Cubs (4), Philadelphia Phillies (5), San Diego Padres (6)
Upgrade Your Streaming Experience
If you decide to watch the MLB postseason, there's still time to get a big-screen television for viewing this beautiful game. Pro tip: Turn on your TV's motion-smoothing option for the best picture while watching sports. Just remember to turn it off before watching other TV shows and movies to avoid the awful "soap opera" effect.
About Our Expert
As PCMag's editor of how to content, I have to cover a wide variety of topics and also make our stories accessible to everyday users. Considering my history as a technical writer, copywriter, and all-around freelancer covering baseball, comics, and more at various outlets, I am used to making myself into an expert.
I believe tech corporations are bad, but you might as well know how to use technology in everyday life. Want more how to content delivered right to your inbox? Sign up for the tips and tricks newsletter that I curate three times a week.
My job as how-to guru means I use just about every gadget under the sun, so I can figure out how everything works. I work from a Lenovo ThinkPad running Windows 11, but also have a very large Dell Inspiron 17 3000 and Apple silicon MacBook. I have a Google Pixel 6a for personal use and use a Galaxy Z Flip 4 for additional Samsung-related testing. For iOS coverage, an iPhone 13 mini works like a charm, though it's already becoming a little long in the tooth.
My desktop situation includes a dual monitor setup with a modest Acer monitor. I also use a Logitech vertical mouse (who can use these ThinkPad trackpads) and a Havit keyboard (my first mechanical keyboard; I love it but my wife hates it!). I'm a recent convert from wired headphones; I have Anker Soundcore Liberty Air wireless earbuds for personal use and have taken to the Sennheiser HD 450BT headphones for work.
Whenever I have a second to myself, I'm probably gaming on my Nintendo Switch 2, Steam Deck, or Xbox Series S. I also still have a bunch of classic consoles lying around as well.

With that in mind, we polled the Rotoworld Baseball staff for their thoughts on how the rest of the postseason will play out. Check out our picks and analysis for the Division Series, Championship Series, and World Series. The 2026 MLB postseason has arrived. Stay up to date with the latest results and more. 2026 ALDS, N
item.content:encoded:
With the Wild Card round of the 2026 MLB Playoffs behind us, it's time for the Division Series to get underway. It all starts on Saturday with all four Division Series matchups.
With that in mind, we polled the Rotoworld Baseball staff for their thoughts on how the rest of the postseason will play out. Check out our picks and analysis for the Division Series, Championship Series, and World Series.
The 2026 MLB postseason has arrived. Stay up to date with the latest results and more.
2026 ALDS, NLDS Predictions
| Writer | White Sox vs. Guardians | Yankees vs. Rays | Braves vs. Dodgers | Padres vs. Brewers |
| Eric Samulski | Guardians | Yankees | Dodgers | Brewers |
| Matthew Pouliot | Guardians | Yankees | Dodgers | Brewers |
| David Shovein | Guardians | Rays | Dodgers | Brewers |
| Christopher Crawford | White Sox | Yankees | Dodgers | Padres |
| D.J. Short | Guardians | Yankees | Dodgers | Padres |
White Sox vs. Guardians
Crawford: I don't think there's much of a difference between the White Sox and the Guardians. I think the fact that the White Sox already won a pair of postseason games on the road, both relatively convincingly, is something working in their favor. I can't quite go team of destiny or any of that stuff, but there does seem to be something about this White Sox team. I realize that's not exactly the most scientific answer, but my heart believes in the Chicago Popes.
Yankees vs. Rays
Short: The Rays and Yankees are set to meet in the postseason for the second time ever, and the first with actual fans in the building. While the Rays were the better regular season team this year, I think the Yankees are better built for the postseason. It starts with the rotation, which was the best in the majors with a 3.30 ERA, but their bullpen was even better with a 3.15 ERA. Drew Rasmussen has dominated the Yankees in his career, but New York has a level of rotation depth the Rays simply can't match.
Aaron Judge's status for the ALDS remains uncertain because of his calf injury, but even without him, one could argue that the Yankees have the more dangerous lineup. Their ability to change the game with one swing is something I think will win out over Tampa Bay's small-ball style in a short series.
Braves vs. Dodgers
Pouliot: Atlanta's pitching staff received 7 2/3 innings from Chris Sale and seven from Tyler Mahle and still seemed hard-pressed to get through the three-game Wild Card series against the Phillies. How are they going to hold up without those two to start the series against the Dodgers? Even without the relief appearance Thursday, starting Sale in Game 2 would have required pitching him on four days' rest, which he hasn't done since early April. As is, it looks like Sale in Game 3 and Mahle in Game 4. Maybe the Dodgers' bats start off cold and the Braves can steal a game in Los Angeles, but as shorthanded as they are in terms of pitching depth, not having their rotation lined puts them at a major disadvantage.
Padres vs. Brewers
Samulski: The Padres have been red hot and dominated the Cubs, but I published an article before the postseason with research from the last 10 years that showed teams coming into the playoffs with tons of momentum don't meaningfully perform better than teams who struggle coming into the postseason. I might as well trust my own research. The Brewers have been arguably the best team in baseball all season. Their lineup is incredibly tough to get out, and they have possibly the deepest overall pitching staff in the postseason.
Full MLB Postseason Predictions
| Writer | ALCS Winner | NLCS Winner | World Series Champion |
| Eric Samulski | New York Yankees | Milwaukee Brewers | Milwaukee Brewers |
| Matthew Pouliot | New York Yankees | Los Angeles Dodgers | Los Angeles Dodgers |
| David Shovein | Tampa Bay Rays | Milwaukee Brewers | Tampa Bay Rays |
| Christopher Crawford | New York Yankees | San Diego Padres | San Diego Padres |
| D.J. Short | New York Yankees | San Diego Padres | New York Yankees |
Samulski: I will admit my bias again when talking about why I picked against the Yankees. I just think this Brewers team is finally going to break through. The Yankees were lights out against the Red Sox, but they have been prone to strikeouts throughout the season. That can make them a volatile offense, and I think the consistency of the Brewers will win the day here.
Pouliot: A few weeks ago, I might have picked another champ, but with the Dodgers' bullpen rounding into form, their biggest potential weakness seems gone. Edwin Díaz still isn't a sure thing, but he was much improved after coming off the IL, allowing just one hit and one walk while striking out nine in his final five innings. Roki Sasaki and Evan Phillips both hit 100 mph last week, and Kris Bubic, if he's even needed, could prove to be a secret weapon. Shohei Ohtani and Freddie Freeman might not be able to carry the offense at this point, but even if the Dodgers are lacking their usual firepower, they should be able to win some low-scoring games.
Crawford: I don't think the Padres are the best team in baseball. I don't think they're even the best team in their division. But I love the way they're playing now, and that bullpen, quality starters at the top of the rotation and just enough star power makes me believe they're built for the postseason, and their first-ever World Series championship.
Short: I love the Yankees' pitching and Aaron Judge should be back eventually in some capacity, which only improves the team's outlook for a potential World Series matchup. As opposed to their meeting in 1998, I would expect the Padres to make this one much more competitive. San Diego's offense has been great in the second half and their bullpen is positively scary. Still, the Yankees would hold the major edge in starting pitching, and that would ultimately make the difference in my hypothetical World Series matchup.

item.dc:creator: Pete Caldera; NorthJersey com

Here's a look at the other Yankees drafted and developed players who could impac
item.content:encoded:
ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. – How the Yankees' Bay State duo of Cam Schlittler and Ben Rice performed in the Wild Card Series against the Red Sox – drafted out of Massachusetts – was also a take-a-bow moment for player development.
"Just impressive to see these young guys step into the biggest stage at the biggest moment,'' said Yankees captain Aaron Judge, their supreme first-round pick (32nd overall) from the 2013 draft.
Here's a look at the other Yankees drafted and developed players who could impact the best-of-five Division Series against the AL champion Tampa Bay Rays:
George Lombard Jr.
Age: 21
Yankees draft info: 1st round (26th overall) in 2023.
In his first taste of postseason – with 42 games of MLB experience – the shortstop handled his position well and went 4-for-8 at the plate.
"A couple of years ago, he was playing high school baseball,'' Judge said of Lombard, while praising the Yanks' rookie and sophomore class in general.
"Just a really good player,'' Max Fried said of Lombard Jr. "He's got a slow heartbeat.''
Spencer Jones
Age: 25
Yankees draft info: 1st round (25th overall) in 2022.
Despite Trent Grisham's return, Jones – who batted .389/1.107 OPS in 59 MLB plate appearances vs. lefties – started in center field against Payton Tolle in the Wild Card opener.
The lefty-hitting Jones was shifted to right field vs. Sonny Gray in Game 2, batting cleanup, with Grisham in center.
Jones went 2-for-8 with a walk and four strikeouts in the ALWC.
Judge's status could impact his late game at-bats, if the captain is on the roster, but the 6-foot-7 slugger has earned his opportunity as a regular in postseason.
Ben Rice
Age: 27
Yankees draft info: 12th round in 2021.
Rice destroyed the Red Sox in the Yanks' 9-0, Wild Card Series Game 1 win, with two homers - including a grand slam - among his four hits, with six RBI as the DH.
With 41 homers this year, Rice joined Judge as the only drafted Yankees to reach the 40-homer mark in a single regular season.
Expect Rice to continue batting leadoff against the Rays' right-handed starters. Also, he's a .458 hitter with five homers and a 1.685 OPS in seven career games at the Trop.
Anthony Volpe
Age: 25
Yankees draft info: 1st round (30th overall) in 2019.
Volpe started the Wild Card opener vs. the lefty Tolle, going 1-for-3 at second base, a new MLB position for him upon his return; he was optioned to Triple-A with Lombard's early August call-up.
Lefty-hitting Jazz Chisholm Jr., on the bench in WC Game 1, started Game 2 vs. the right-handed Gray and went 2-for-3 with a walk in a clinching 9-2 victory.
Given the Rays' right-handed rotation, Volpe might be a bench player this series, utilized later in games for his infield versatility (including some third base) and as a pinch-runner.
Cam Schlittler
Age: 25
Yankees draft info: 7th round in 2022.
Red Sox Nation has already seen enough postseason Schlittler, helping take Boston out of the last two AL Wild Card Series.
After his 117-pitch scoreless effort in Tuesday's Wild Card opener, Schlittler gets the ball in Monday's ALDS Game 2, on one extra day of rest.
That also puts him in line for a possible Game 5 on normal rest. Both games are at Trop, and Schlittler owns a 1.16 ERA in 17 road starts this year.
Will Warren
Age: 27
Yankees draft info: 8th round in 2021.
Moved into a multi-inning relief role in postseason, Warren tossed 1.2 innings (one run) following Fried in Game 2.
He should fit that same role against the Rays, with the ability to take over for a shaky or injured starter, or to provide a bridge to the high-leverage duo of Paul Blackburn and Brent Headrick, leading into David Bednar.
Austin Wells
Age: 27
Yankees draft info: 1st round (28th overall) in 2020.
At the plate, the lefty-hitting Wells picked it up considerably after a brutal first four months, but his value behind the plate - and his knack for ABS challenges - has been a constant.
As for defending the speedy, daring Rays, "they love to run and take advantage,'' said Wells, emphasizing the limiting of walks in this series.
Wells has been paired all year with Game 1 starter Gerrit Cole, who praised the "role Austin has played in run prevention'' for a staff that led the league in ERA.
This article originally appeared on NorthJersey.com: How these 7 Yankees homegrown players can impact ALDS vs Rays

item.content:encoded:
For the Sixth Consecutive Year, TelevisaUnivision’s Sports Audio Network Will Deliver Live, Play-by-Play Coverage of the MLB Playoffs Through the 122nd World Series Across All Platforms.
Courtesy: TelevisaUnivision
MIAMI, FL. – October 2, 2026 – TUDN Radio, the premier Hispanic sports audio network of TelevisaUnivision, will once again serve as the exclusive U.S. Spanish-language radio home for the 2026 Major League Baseball Postseason. Marking the network’s sixth consecutive edition delivering October baseball to Hispanic audiences across the nation, fans can experience the entire postseason journey entirely in Spanish—from the opening pitch of the Wild Card Series through the final out of the historic 122nd World Series.
Continuing its long-standing collaboration with Major League Baseball, TUDN Radio will bring every moment of the postseason to life, led by the voices of acclaimed announcers Luis Quiñones, Alberto “El Beto” Ferreiro, Daniel Alvarez, and Jesus Acosta. This elite broadcast team will provide unparalleled coverage across the network’s nationwide terrestrial radio footprint, as well as digitally via the Uforia app and TUDN’s digital platforms.
“Baseball holds a deep, passionate connection with our Hispanic audience, and we are incredibly proud to return for our sixth postseason as the exclusive Spanish-language audio voice of MLB,” said Carlos F. Azcarate, VP of Sports Radio Network. “We are thrilled to continue bringing fans closer to the diamond, delivering every pivotal moment, dramatic home run, and championship celebration directly to them, wherever they choose to listen.”
Unprecedented Coverage Across All Platforms
TUDN Radio will broadcast key matchups throughout each round of the postseason, culminating in comprehensive Spanish-language audio coverage of the entire Fall Classic. Listeners can tune in across multiple touchpoints:
- TUDN Radio Network: Broadcast across affiliate radio stations in primary Hispanic markets nationwide.
- The Uforia App: TelevisaUnivision’s audio platform, offering live streaming on mobile devices across the United States.
- TUDN.com and TUDN App: Live digital audio integration for fans following games online.
- Smart Speakers & Connected Devices: Voice-activated live streaming through supported home integrations.
The 2026 Postseason Schedule on TUDN Radio
TUDN Radio’s coverage will feature full pre-game, play-by-play, and post-game analysis across every round:
- MLB Wild Card Series: Complete coverage of the best-of-three opening rounds.
- American League and National League Division Series (ALDS & NLDS): In-depth coverage as teams battle for the pennant.
- American League and National League Championship Series (ALCS & NLCS): Live calls deciding the champions of each league.
- The 122nd World Series: Uninterrupted, full-series coverage of baseball’s championship showdown.
Adding to the comprehensive live game broadcasts, fans can catch all the surrounding excitement, expert breakdowns, and exclusive player interviews on TUDN Radio’s premier baseball show, Desde El Diamante.
Complete broadcast schedules, station directories, and talent assignments will be updated throughout the month as matchups advance. Fans can follow along with live game updates, highlights, and behind-the-scenes content on X, Instagram, and Facebook via @TUDNRadio and by visiting TUDN.com.
CONTACT:
Melissa Agudelo – Director of Communications, News & Sports
###

Por sexto año consecutivo, la cadena de audio deportivo de TelevisaUnivision ofrecerá cobertura en vivo, narración jugada a jugada y análisis de los Playoffs de la MLB hasta la 122.ª Serie Mundial en todas sus plataformas
Cortesía: TelevisaUnivision
MIAMI, Florida – 2 de octubre de 2026 – TUDN Radio, la principal cadena de audio deportivo para la audiencia hispana de TelevisaUnivision, volverá a ser la casa exclusiva de radio en español en EE. UU. de la Postemporada de las Grandes Ligas 2026. Por sexto año consecutivo, la cadena llevará el beisbol de octubre a las audiencias hispanas de todo el país, permitiéndoles vivir de principio a fin la emoción de la postemporada en español, desde el primer lanzamiento de la Serie de Comodines hasta el último out de la histórica 122.ª Serie Mundial.
Como parte de su colaboración de larga trayectoria con Major League Baseball, TUDN Radio llevará a los aficionados cada instante de la postemporada de la mano de los reconocidos narradores Luis Quiñones, Alberto “El Beto” Ferreiro, Daniel Alvarez y Jesús Acosta. Este destacado equipo de transmisión ofrecerá una cobertura de primer nivel a través de la red de estaciones de radio terrestre de la cadena en todo el país, así como en formato digital mediante la app de Uforia y las plataformas digitales de TUDN.
“El beisbol mantiene un vínculo profundo y apasionado con nuestra audiencia hispana, y nos llena de orgullo regresar por sexto año consecutivo como la voz exclusiva en español de la postemporada de la MLB”, afirmó Carlos F. Azcarate, VP de Sports Radio Network. “Nos entusiasma seguir acercando a los aficionados al diamante y llevarles cada momento decisivo, cada cuadrangular dramático y cada celebración del campeonato, sin importar dónde elijan escucharnos”.
Cobertura sin precedentes en todas las plataformas
TUDN Radio transmitirá los enfrentamientos más destacados de cada ronda de la postemporada, hasta llegar a una cobertura integral en audio en español de toda la Serie Mundial. Los aficionados podrán seguir la acción a través de múltiples plataformas:
- TUDN Radio Network: Transmisiones a través de estaciones afiliadas en los principales mercados hispanos de todo el país.
- La app de Uforia: La plataforma de audio de TelevisaUnivision ofrecerá streaming en vivo para dispositivos móviles en todo Estados Unidos.
- TUDN.com y la app de TUDN: Integración de audio digital en vivo para los aficionados que sigan los partidos por internet.
- Altavoces inteligentes y dispositivos conectados: Streaming en vivo mediante comandos de voz a través de las integraciones domésticas compatibles.
Calendario de la Postemporada 2026 en TUDN Radio
La cobertura de TUDN Radio incluirá previa, narración jugada a jugada y análisis posterior a cada encuentro durante todas las rondas de la postemporada:
- Serie de Comodines de la MLB: Cobertura completa de la ronda inaugural al mejor de tres juegos.
- Series Divisionales de la Liga Americana y la Liga Nacional (ALDS y NLDS): Análisis en profundidad mientras los equipos compiten por el campeonato de cada liga.
- Series de Campeonato de la Liga Americana y la Liga Nacional (ALCS y NLCS): Narración en vivo de los encuentros que definirán a los campeones de cada liga.
- 122.ª Serie Mundial: Cobertura ininterrumpida y de principio a fin de la gran batalla por el campeonato de las Grandes Ligas.
Además de las transmisiones en vivo de los partidos, los aficionados podrán disfrutar de toda la emoción alrededor de la postemporada, análisis especializados y entrevistas exclusivas con jugadores en Desde El Diamante, el programa insignia de beisbol de TUDN Radio.
Los calendarios completos de transmisiones, directorios de estaciones y asignaciones del talento se actualizarán durante el mes a medida que avancen los enfrentamientos. Los aficionados podrán seguir las novedades de los partidos en vivo, los mejores momentos y contenido exclusivo detrás de cámaras en X, Instagram y Facebook a través de @TUDNRadio, así como en TUDN.com.

The Atlanta Braves have been meticulous in how they handle Chris Sale for the last three years, making sure to give him enough rest so that he can maintain his excellent form for an entire campaign. item.content:encoded:
Braves' Walt Weiss provides update on Chris Sale NLDS plan appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
The Atlanta Braves have been meticulous in how they handle Chris Sale for the last three years, making sure to give him enough rest so that he can maintain his excellent form for an entire campaign. The 2024 National League Cy Young Award winner has still spent time on the injured list, but their plan has helped him become a top-tier starting pitcher once again. All bets are off in the playoffs, though. Right?
Two days after starting Game 1 of the NL Wild Card Series versus the Philadelphia Phillies, Sale made it clear he wanted to take the mound in a do-or-die Game 3. Despite holding a 6-2 lead in the eighth inning, manager Walt Weiss brought in the veteran left-hander to finish off Atlanta's longtime rival. Sale indicated that he still plans to pitch against the Los Angeles Dodgers on Sunday night, but nothing is official yet.
In fact, it sounds like there is serious doubt surrounding the 10-time All-Star's status for Game 2 of the NL Division Series. Although Weiss said a Sale start in LA is "still on the table," the Braves want their ace to be fresh enough for postseason battle.
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
"We're gonna err on the side of giving him (time to rest) if it's even close," the NL Manager of the Year candidate revealed, per ESPN's Alden Gonzalez. That statement is a far cry from Sale's confident remarks following Atlanta's series-clinching win over Philly. Weiss has been in baseball a long time, however.
It is possible the skipper is just engaging in some good old-fashioned gamesmanship before his squad faces the two-time reigning World Series champions. The Braves are a title contender in their own right, but they will want to gain a mental edge on the Dodgers if one is attainable. Disarming the home team with a surprise pitching move seems like the perfect gambit to try in October. Dave Roberts is a veteran of this game as well, though, so he may not be caught off guard.
Of course, there is a possibility that Walt Weiss is merely telling the truth. Perhaps Atlanta will wait until it returns to Truist Park to start Chris Sale. If so, then the team's bullpen move in Game 3 of the Wild Card round will seem even more puzzling.
One thing is for certain. Sale is a warrior who has openly expressed his desire to carry a big workload in the playoffs. We shall see if the Braves trust him to run wild in Chavez Ravine. The time for speculation will soon end. Game 1 of the NLDS begins on Saturday at 4 p.m. ET.

item.title: [MLB.com] Sale's pitch to Weiss pays off: Lefty bookends Braves' Wild Card Series win
item.dc:creator: Paul Casella
item.description: The Braves' ace had an important matter to address before Game 3 of the National League Wild Card Series on Thursday night at Truist Park. "First of all, I was not going to go to Chris Sale and ask him if he could pitch tonight," Weiss said after the Braves’ series-clinching 6-2 win. "I didn't want to put him in that position, because I knew that, even if he was hanging, he would tell me yes. So I was not going to bring it up." Turns out, Weiss didn't need to. "Literally as soon as I stepped in
item.content:encoded:
The Braves' ace had an important matter to address before Game 3 of the National League Wild Card Series on Thursday night at Truist Park.
"First of all, I was not going to go to Chris Sale and ask him if he could pitch tonight," Weiss said after the Braves’ series-clinching 6-2 win. "I didn't want to put him in that position, because I knew that, even if he was hanging, he would tell me yes. So I was not going to bring it up."
Turns out, Weiss didn't need to.
"Literally as soon as I stepped in my office this afternoon, he was sitting in the chair across from my desk," Weiss said. "And he looked at me and he said, 'I feel amazing.'”
Weiss’ response?
“Well, let's talk."
From there, the two laid out a plan that ultimately saw Sale take down the final four outs of the Braves' first postseason series win since the 2021 World Series. Keep in mind, Sale also recorded the club's first 19 outs of this Wild Card Series as the Game 1 starter in Atlanta's 5-3 victory two days earlier.
In doing so, Sale became the first pitcher to start Game 1 of a postseason series and finish off that same series since ... Chris Sale. He previously did the same thing for the Red Sox in the 2018 World Series against the Dodgers.
Sale joined Clayton Kershaw as the only pitchers to accomplish the feat multiple times in postseason history.
"What a warrior, man," Weiss said. "This guy -- I've run out of superlatives for Chris Sale. Been talking about him all year. He's one of the best I've ever been around."
Even with Sale’s mid-afternoon ambush opening up some options for Weiss, their meticulously crafted plan only worked if all of the pieces fell into place.
Ray Kerr had to go out and do his job as the opener. Grant Holmes had to take it from there and relay the torch to a trio of relievers -- Robert Suarez, Didier Fuentes and Dylan Dodd -- who each had to take care of business.
And even then, the offense also needed to do its part. Michael Harris II checked that box early with a three-run homer in the first inning, then Ozzie Albies (a two-run shot in the fourth) and Matt Olson (a solo blast in the seventh) tacked on.
"Unbelievable. I'm just thankful for the opportunity, honestly," Sale said. "This could not be more of a group effort. This was basically a culmination of our entire year. All hands on deck. Everyone is doing everything they can to just get a win for this team."
Safe to say everything went to plan?
Well, sort of.
Knowing the plan was to pitch against the top of the Phillies' order in either the eighth or the ninth inning, Sale started to throw in the bullpen in the top of the seventh. But when Olson's homer extended the Braves' lead to 6-1 in the bottom of the seventh, it altered the strategy.
Even with Philadelphia's 9-1-2 hitters due up, Weiss instead went with the left-handed Dodd to start the eighth. He gave up a leadoff triple to pinch-hitter Derek Hill, who then scored on Trea Turner's sacrifice fly to cut the lead to four.
Needing to face at least three batters, Dodd had to stay in to face Kyle Schwarber -- the same guy who homered in the eighth inning off Dylan Lee one day earlier to trigger the Phillies' Game 2 comeback. Dodd was up to the task, though, getting MLB's regular-season home run leader to fly out for the second out.
Then, it was showtime: Sale vs. Bryce Harper.
"Electric," Harris said of the moment Sale emerged from the bullpen.
"The best," Albies said. "The minute I saw him getting warmed up, I said, 'He's definitely coming in. I love this.' The energy, the excitement there -- everybody was pumped that he came in the game."
Well, everyone except the Phillies.
Sale struck out Harper on four pitches, getting him to chase three sliders well out of the zone. The last one missed badly enough to go to the backstop, but catcher Drake Baldwin tracked it down to throw out Harper.
Now came another decision for Weiss: Let Sale go back out for the ninth or turn it over to closer Raisel Iglesias with a four-run lead?
With Iglesias warming just in case, the home crowd roared as Sale emerged from the dugout to trot back out for the ninth. Four batters later, the Braves had punched their ticket for an NLDS showdown with the Dodgers.
"Was hoping he only had to go one," Weiss said, "but he had to get to four outs."
All told, Sale -- the Braves' presumed starter for Sunday's Game 2 -- threw 21 pitches over 1 1/3 innings.
Is he still good to go for Sunday?
"I don't know. I have no idea," Weiss said. "We weren't even worried about that. It was just, 'Put this thing down and then we'll have those conversations later.' But yeah, we haven't even talked about that. It was all about tonight."
If Weiss has any doubts, he’ll certainly be getting another visit this weekend at Dodger Stadium.
"If I had to pitch tomorrow," Sale said, "I'd pitch tomorrow."

item.content:encoded:
MLB playoff predictions 2026: Expert picks for every ALDS, NLDS series originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
October has officially arrived, just in time for the MLB postseason to ramp up.
With all four Wild Card series now over — three of which ended in two-game sweeps — just eight teams remain alive in the pursuit of a World Series title, with the Guardians, Rays, Dodgers and Brewers entering the picture after watching the first round from home.
Some of baseball's biggest stars, from Shohei Ohtani and Jacob Misiorowski to Junior Caminero and Cam Schlittler, will be on full display for the division series. On both sides of the bracket, the question will be whether the teams carrying their Wild Card momentum can now take down a well-rested heavyweight.
With a chance to reset between rounds, the best-of-five ALDS and NLDS matchups begin Saturday. Who will advance to the championship series?
With Wild Card matchups in the rearview mirror, The Sporting News predicts the 2026 MLB division series matchups.
MORE: Complete MLB playoff schedule for 2026 postseason
No. 6 Chicago White Sox vs. No. 2 Cleveland Guardians
You can certainly debate whether the Guardians (85 regular-season wins) or White Sox (84 regular-season wins) really belong on the postseason stage this season, with neither AL Central squad owning a ton of big-name star power. Regardless, the fact is that Cleveland and Chicago both find themselves with an opportunity to make a serious postseason run in a weaker AL bracket — and the White Sox have already taken advantage.
Chicago enters the ALDS the momentum of its first postseason series win since the 2005 World Series, proving in the Wild Card round that it has the power and pitching depth to challenge opponents. Cleveland, though, has better top-end starting pitching in Parker Messick, Gavin Williams and Tanner Bibee.
These two teams are well familiar with each other; the White Sox won the season series, 7-6. Cleveland's offense isn't very threatening, ranking last among all postseason teams in team OPS (.696) — this matchup will likely come down to how early the White Sox's bats can get to Guardians starters.
Saturday will mark the first time in MLB history that the Chicago White Sox and Cleveland have met in the postseason.
The White Sox began playing baseball in 1894 as the Sioux City Cornhuskers.
The Guardians began playing baseball in 1896 as the Columbus Buckeyes/Senators.
The fact that this is a divisional matchup means it will likely be close, but Chicago's momentum is hard to ignore, and there was only a one-win discrepancy between the sides in the regular season. The White Sox are finally building something serious, seemingly with a new hero every night. The power in Will Venable's lineup is dangerous enough to reach the ALCS.
Prediction: White Sox in 4
No. 4 New York Yankees vs. No. 1 Tampa Bay Rays
It's been clear since the start of the postseason that whichever AL East team emerged from the lower half of the bracket would be favored to reach the World Series. This is the heavyweight matchup of the two ALDS series, featuring elite starting pitching on both sides and some of MLB's premiere sluggers.
Of course, the massive question lingering over this matchup is how much, if at all, Aaron Judge will play for the Yankees. Even as the lower seed, if he's near 100 percent, it's hard not to view New York as the favorite to reach the ALCS; a healthy Judge, alongside Cody Bellinger, Luis Garcia Jr. and Ben Rice, takes Aaron Boone's lineup to a new level, capable of matching the all-around offensive excellence of Tampa Bay's quartet: Caminero, Yandy Siaz, Jonathan Aranda and Chandler Simpson.
The Rays won this season series 7-6, but it may be the most evenly matched division series. Both sides can roll out a trio talented starters — New York with Cam Schlittler, Max Fried and Gerrit Cole, and Tampa Bay with Drew Rasmussen, Nick Martinez and Shane McClanahan — to pair with deep offenses.
Yankees can line up their pitching as follows against the Rays:
Game 1: Gerrit Cole
Game 2: Cam Schlittler
Game 3: Max Fried
Game 4: Gerrit Cole
Game 5: Cam Schlittler
For two reasons, the Yankees are the pick here. For one, between Schlittler and arguably the best bullpen in baseball, New York is loaded with leverage arms. And the Yankees are also riding high off a dominant Wild Card series, biding time for Judge and Giancarlo Stanton to heal. Assuming those two sluggers can at least be used in some key at-bats, the Yankees' lineup is capable of changing games in an instant.
Prediction: Yankees in 5
No. 3 Atlanta Braves vs. No. 2 Los Angeles Dodgers
The Dodgers' path to becoming the first National League team to win three-straight World Series will begin with a matchup against a 94-win Braves squad fresh off a Wild Card win over the Phillies.
Los Angeles' rest advantage could be significant. Even if he's not pitching, Ohtani has been dealing with lingering injury concerns over the last few months. A week off between his last regular season game should only benefit him, not to mention the Dodgers' ability to line up their loaded starting rotation however they choose. With the Braves using Chris Sale in two games against Philadelphia, he may not be available early in the NLDS.
The Dodgers and Braves have built quite the postseason history. 👀🔥
2013 NLDS — LAD def. ATL
2018 NLDS — LAD def. ATL
2020 NLCS — LAD def. ATL
2021 NLCS — ATL def. LAD
2026 NLDS — ??? 🤔 pic.twitter.com/mHhbDO9gDX
The top of Atlanta's lineup is potent enough to make this an interesting series, and the team did beat the Dodgers five times in the regular season, but Ronald Acuna Jr., Austin Riley and Ozzie Albies will have to meet the moment in the NLDS. Yoshinobu Yamamoto has pitched well against Atlanta in his career, as have Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow.
Even if the Braves' bats can keep things close, it's hard to imagine Atlanta's pitching staff beyond Sale being able to contain Ohtani, Freddie Freeman, Kyle Tucker and Mookie Betts over a five-game series. The Braves are a good team, but the Dodgers are far too talented to fall this early in the bracket.
Prediction: Dodgers in 4
No. 4 San Diego Padres vs. No. 1 Milwaukee Brewers
This matchup pins baseball's best team all season, Milwaukee, against one of its hottest over the past month, San Diego. While the Brewers are the clear favorites here, between the best starting pitcher in the game this season and a deep lineup that plays to contact, the Padres do pose some interesting challenges, going 4-2 against Milwaukee in the regular season.
On one hand, San Diego has stars made for October. As shown in the Wild Card round, when the top of the Padres' lineup is on, they're a hard team to beat — Fernando Tatis Jr., Manny Machado, Xander Boegarts, Ty France and Jackson Merrill can look like one of the best 1-through-5 groups in baseball at times. Add in an elite starter (Michael King) and a strong bullpen led by Mason Miller, and there's a path for the Padres to pull off a stunner here.
Most data has shown that the more of a threat a team is to hit the ball out of the yard, the better they'll fare in the postseason. If this is finally going to be the year the Brewers reach a World Series — putting an end to their cycle of regular season success with playoff shortcomings — they'll need to slug more. This is an offense that's outstanding at making contact and getting on base, but has also continually come up short in October and finished second-to-last in team home runs (154) in the 2026 regular season.
Chances are, Milwaukee won't only be able to rely on its strong pitching staff to reach the World Series. The Brewers' bats will need some extra-base hits. But with the Padres' lackluster starting pitching depth, this is still a series the Brewers can claim even if they're not pristine.
San Diego may have some top-end talent and momentum, but the Padres can't match Milwaukee's all-around depth.
Prediction: Brewers in 4

item.content:encoded:
ATLANTA -- Ray Kerr was the left-handed reliever the Braves chose to get through Kyle Schwarber and Bryce Harper during the first inning of Game 3 of the National League Wild Card Series against the Phillies.
Kerr served as the opener in Thursday's series-clinching 6-2 win and dazzled, keeping the Phillies in check with 3 1/3 scoreless innings, allowing one hit and one walk with two strikeouts. Grant Holmes followed Kerr and allowed one run on two hits and one walk, while earning the win.
“This was just another Thursday,” Kerr said. “Growing up, I had a hard time. So, this was nothing.”
The Braves provided a clue they would go this way in Miami on Friday, when they used Kerr as an opener on Holmes’ scheduled start date.
“That was a best-case scenario, and [Kerr] did it,” Weiss said. “He got through the top twice, which kept us from using another guy at the top. So, Ray -- it all started with Ray. Everything fell into place because of Ray Kerr.”
Kerr posted a 1.47 ERA over 18 1/3 innings in nine appearances going back to his Aug. 17 season debut. Left-handed hitters were 4-for-23 (.174) against him in the regular season, with one extra-base hit, a double.
Kerr made two appearances against the Phillies in September, with the most recent a three-inning outing on Sept. 13. He got Schwarber to ground into a double play and then struck out Trea Turner to end the fifth. Harper began the sixth with a double but was left stranded.
Kerr has made just 19 big league appearances since the start of 2024. After tossing three scoreless innings against the Marlins on Friday, he said he would gladly welcome the chance to be an opener in the postseason.
Holmes posted a 3.57 ERA in 29 starts this season and a 2.94 ERA over his final 14 starts. Opponents produced a .590 OPS against him the first time facing him in a game and an .886 OPS during the second plate appearance.

item.content:encoded:
Phillies' Aaron Nola Reportedly Starting vs. Braves over Zack Wheeler For MLB Playoffs Series Finale
The Philadelphia Phillies will go into Thursday's winner-take-all Game 3 against the Atlanta Braves in the National League Wild Card series with Aaron Nola starting on the mound.
Per The Athletic's Matt Gelb, Phillies interim manager Don Mattingly is going with Nola rather than using Zack Wheeler on short rest with a spot in the NLDS at stake.
As a result of their four-game losing streak last week that prevented them from clinching a playoff spot early, the Phillies had to use Wheeler on the final day of the regular season.
Wheeler allowed one run over six innings in a 7-3 win over the Tampa Bay Rays to help Philadelphia secure its postseason berth, but the situation left his status for the wild card round unclear.
Even though Wheeler won't get the start, Mattingly told reporters after Wednesday's 4-3 win to extend the series "it'll be pretty much all hands on deck" for Game 3.
The Phillies are fortunate to have a deep starting staff that allowed them to go with All-Stars Jesús Luzardo and Cristopher Sánchez in the first two games against Atlanta.
However, Game 3 left Mattingly with a decision between Nola or Wheeler. John Clark of NBC Sports Philadelphia noted Wheeler has never started a game in the regular season or playoffs on short rest.
Wheeler's only relief appearance in his MLB career was in Game 7 of the 2023 NLCS against the Arizona Diamondbacks. He tossed 1.2 scoreless innings in a 9-7 loss.
Nola will be pitching on regular rest after starting on Saturday against the Rays. He only made it through one inning, allowing three runs on four hits in a 12-1 loss.
While Nola's overall stat line this season doesn't look great with a 4.67 ERA, he did get better as the year went on. The right-hander had a 3.33 ERA in 14 starts after the All-Star break.
Nola made three starts against Atlanta this season with two coming in a five-day span from Sept. 6-11. He allowed three runs and struck out eight over 13.1 innings in those two outings last month.
The Phillies forced Game 3 against Atlanta thanks to Kyle Schwarber and Bryce Harper hitting back-to-back homers in the eighth to tie the score at three. Alec Bohm delivered the go-ahead solo homer in the top of the 10th.
Andrew Painter finished the game on the mound with three scoreless innings out of the bullpen.
Game 3 between the Phillies and Braves from Truist Park will be played at 8 p.m. ET on Thursday. The winner will advance to play the Los Angeles Dodgers in the NLDS starting on Saturday.

item.content:encoded:
MLB playoff schedule 2026: Full bracket, scores, times, TV channels to watch every postseason series originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
More than seven months after pitchers and catchers reported to spring training, it's time to determine which team will wear the MLB crown in 2026.
Twelve teams reached the postseason bracket, and any discussion about favorites has to start with the two-time defending champion Dodgers. Los Angeles wasn't necessarily dominant during the regular season and enters October with concerns about the health of the planet's best player, Shohei Ohtani, but it has proven unwise to bet against LA lately.
While the Dodgers are in the midst of a dynastic run, neither of the teams that owned the best records in their respective leagues during the regular season — the Brewers and Rays — has won a World Series. Victory would be particularly sweet for either of those fan bases, along with the other postseason entrant without a title, the Padres.
Who will survive the gauntlet to lift the Commissioner's Trophy at the end of October? Here's when and where to watch every game.
Where to watch MLB playoffs 2026
- TV channels: Fox, FS1, TBS, NBC, NBCSN
The 2026 MLB postseason will have a new look for the opening round, with NBC carrying every wild card game on its platforms: NBC, NBCSN and/or Peacock.
After that, the familiar rotation returns. This year's NL playoffs will air on Fox or FS1 while the AL will be on TBS, with the World Series set to air on Fox as it has every year since 2000.
Fans can stream every postseason game except Peacock exclusives with DIRECTV, which offers a free trial to new subscribers.
All games airing on NBC, NBCSN, Fox and FS1 can be streamed with fubo, which also offers a free trial.

It only took two games for the Chicago White Sox to advance to the ALDS where they will face the Cleveland Guardians.
This is the first playoff series win for the team on the south side of Chicago in more than 20 years, so White Sox fans are ready to bring the house down upon playoff baseball's return to Rate Field.
Chicago scored a decisive 7-3 victory over Houston on Wednesday night after a three-run home run from Chase Meredith in the sixth inning pulled the White Sox ahead for good.
The ALDS kicks off on Saturday, Oct. 3 in Cleveland, where the White Sox will face their division rival. Chicago has the head-to-head lead in this one, winning seven of 13 matches between the two teams this season. Only a game separated these two in the division race, which should make for a close ALDS matchup.
Below we'll break down how to buy ALDS tickets and more for the 2026 MLB playoffs:

By winning their division, the Guardians earned a first-round bye directly to the ALDS and home-field advantage for the series, which means they will host Game 1, Game 2 and a potential Game 5. item.dc:creator: Sportsnet Staff
item.description: After dropping Game 1 of their wild-card series to the Chicago White Sox while throwing a bullpen day, the Houston Astros had to feel a sense of relief knowing they were turning to their ace, Hunter Brown, for Game 2. item.content:encoded:
After dropping Game 1 of their wild-card series to the Chicago White Sox while throwing a bullpen day, the Houston Astros had to feel a sense of relief knowing they were turning to their ace, Hunter Brown, for Game 2.
But as the second inning came around on Wednesday, Brown had already been chased from the contest.
Chicago sent 10 batters to the plate in a four-run first, tagging Brown for five hits as it looked to win its first playoff series since 2005.
Brown managed to get two outs — both by way of the strikeout — before manager Joe Espada made the move to the bullpen.
White Sox leadoff hitter Sam Antonacci wasted little time putting Brown on his back foot, opening the game with a double that went off Astros left fielder Yordan Alvarez's glove. Kyle Teel then brought home Antonacci with a single, Miguel Vargas reached on an error, Andrew Benintendi scored both with a single and Tristan Peters completed the rally with an RBI single of his own.
Brown left with the bases loaded and two out, but Tuesday's opener, AJ Blubaugh, entered and escaped the jam.
Houston's pitching staff has been ravaged by injuries this season, leaving the 28-year-old Brown and Hayden Wesneski as their lone healthy starters for the playoffs.
With the Astros not clinching their AL West title until the final day of the regular season, they weren't able to line up their pitching staff, which led to the bullpen day in Game 1 before Brown and Wesneski could return on normal rest.
"Having those guys healthy with regular rest, it's super valuable for us," Espdada said before the series began, making Brown's short start all the more costly for an Astros team already needing length from their pitchers.
Brown finished the 2026 regular season with a 3.19 ERA and 124 strikeouts over 107.1 innings. He was also hit by the injury bug earlier in the season, which limited the six-foot-two right-hander to just 20 starts.

Major League Baseball announced the broadcast schedule for the 2026 Wild Card Series presented by AbbVie. The 2026 postseason will begin with each of the four Wild Card Series scheduled from Tuesday through Thursday under a best-of-three format, all available across NBC Sports platforms, including NBC, Peacock and NBC Sports Network. Coverage of the Wild Card Series marks the return of postseason baseball to NBC for the first time since the 2000 ALCS.
The Wild Card Series will be available in Spanish on Universo, while Univision Radio will provide Spanish language audio coverage. ESPN Radio will provide live national coverage of all 2026 MLB postseason games, beginning with the Wild Card Series. In addition, MLB Network will air extensive studio coverage throughout the postseason across the Emmy Award-winning MLB Tonight, the Emmy-nominated MLB Central and MLB Now, and Intentional Talk, MLB Network’s longest-running talk show.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Pete Crow-Armstrong’s Card Sells for $1.1 Million Before Cubs Elimination Game
item.dc:creator: Erik C Anderson
item.description: Pete Crow-Armstrong's historic season just produced another staggering number, this time away from the baseball field. The Chicago Cubs star's one-of-one 2024 Topps Chrome Update MLB Debut Patch Autograph sold for $1.098 million at Goldin. The PSA Gem Mint 10 card, which also received a PSA 10 autograph grade, features the MLB Debut patch from Crow-Armstrong's first major-league game on September 11, 2023. item.content:encoded:
Pete Crow-Armstrong's historic season just produced another staggering number, this time away from the baseball field.
The Chicago Cubs star's one-of-one 2024 Topps Chrome Update MLB Debut Patch Autograph sold for $1.098 million at Goldin.
The PSA Gem Mint 10 card, which also received a PSA 10 autograph grade, features the MLB Debut patch from Crow-Armstrong's first major-league game on September 11, 2023.
It is a massive sale by itself.
The timing makes it even more striking.
Crow-Armstrong just completed a historic 40-home run, 40-stolen base season and helped Chicago reach the postseason. Now, only days later, his signature rookie card has approached the MLB Debut Patch record while Crow-Armstrong and the Cubs enter an elimination game against the San Diego Padres.
$1,098,000: Winning bid for Pete Crow-Armstrong’s debut patch jersey tonight at @GoldinCo.
PCA’s 2024 rookie salary: $740,000. pic.twitter.com/d21WopsNpx
— Darren Rovell (@darrenrovell) September 30, 2026
Pete Crow-Armstrong Card Sells for $1.098 Million
Crow-Armstrong's card was one of the most significant MLB Debut Patch cards to reach the market since Paul Skenes' one-of-one sold in 2025.
Goldin listed the card as Crow-Armstrong's 2024 Topps Chrome Update MLB Debut Patch Autograph 1/1, graded PSA Gem Mint 10 with a PSA/DNA Gem Mint 10 autograph grade.
The $1.098 million result also produced a remarkable comparison highlighted by Rovell.
Crow-Armstrong earned roughly $740,000 during the 2024 season, meaning a collector just paid considerably more for his one-of-one rookie card than the Cubs paid Crow-Armstrong to play an entire major-league season.
But the final auction price may be even more notable for what it narrowly failed to accomplish.
Pete Crow-Armstrong Falls $12,000 Short of Paul Skenes Record
Crow-Armstrong came extraordinarily close to taking down the benchmark for MLB Debut Patch cards.
Skenes' one-of-one 2024 Topps Chrome Update MLB Debut Patch Autograph sold for $1.11 million through Fanatics Collect in March 2025. The price included the buyer's premium and established the Skenes card as the highest-selling MLB Debut Patch at the time.
Crow-Armstrong finished at $1.098 million.
The difference?
Just $12,000.
That puts Crow-Armstrong and Skenes in remarkably similar territory despite playing dramatically different positions and arriving in the majors with different levels of prospect hype.
Skenes was the No. 1 overall pick in the 2023 MLB Draft and won National League Rookie of the Year in his first season. His Debut Patch became a national story even before it surfaced, with the Pittsburgh Pirates famously offering the young collector who pulled it a package that included 30 years of season tickets.
Crow-Armstrong's card reached seven figures after a different catalyst: one of the greatest individual seasons ever produced by a Cubs player.
Pete Crow-Armstrong Made Cubs History Before $1.1 Million Sale
The auction could hardly have closed at a better moment for Crow-Armstrong's hobby profile.
On September 24, Crow-Armstrong stole his 40th base of the season, joining the exclusive 40-40 club after already reaching 45 home runs.
He became just the seventh player in MLB history to record at least 40 homers and 40 stolen bases in the same season. He also became the first Cubs player to accomplish the feat.
And he did it on the same night Chicago clinched an NL Wild Card berth with a 2-1 victory over the Miami Marlins.
Crow-Armstrong entered the postseason hitting .280 with 45 home runs and 107 RBIs while appearing in all 159 Cubs games through the clinching victory.
That transformed the timing of the Goldin auction.
Collectors were not merely bidding on the Debut Patch of a promising young Cubs player.
They were bidding on the Debut Patch of a 24-year-old who had just completed the first 40-40 season in franchise history.
Now the attention shifts back to what Crow-Armstrong can do on the field.
Cubs Face Elimination Against Padres After 8-0 Loss
Chicago enters Game 2 of its Wild Card Series against San Diego needing a victory to keep its season alive.
The Padres routed the Cubs 8-0 in Game 1 on September 29.
San Diego starter Michael King took a no-hit bid into the seventh inning and ultimately allowed only one hit over seven scoreless frames while striking out eight. Fernando Tatis Jr., Manny Machado and Xander Bogaerts each homered for the Padres.
The Cubs will send Kevin Gausman to the mound for Game 2 opposite Nick Pivetta
There is at least one reason for optimism surrounding Crow-Armstrong specifically.
Chicago dominated San Diego during the regular season, winning five of six games and outscoring the Padres 55-28.
Crow-Armstrong was one of the Cubs' biggest problems for San Diego.
He hit .364 with four home runs in the six regular-season meetings.
Chicago will need another performance like that now.
Crow-Armstrong has already produced one of the defining baseball-card sales of 2026 and one of the most statistically significant seasons in Cubs history.
Whether his week is remembered primarily for a $1.098 million card sale or for what happens in October now depends on what Crow-Armstrong and the Cubs do next.
This article was originally published on HEAVY
The post Pete Crow-Armstrong's Card Sells for $1.1 Million Before Cubs Elimination Game appeared first on HEAVY.

The NL MVP favorite became the seventh player in MLB history to hit 40+ home runs and steal 40+ bases in a single season. item.content:encoded:
Pete Crow-Armstrong Joins Elite Company: The 7 Players In The 40/40 Club
24-year-old Chicago Cubs star Pete Crow-Armstrong joined one of the rarest clubs in Major League Baseball this season. The NL MVP favorite became the seventh player in MLB history to hit 40+ home runs and steal 40+ bases in a single season.
While there are only a select few talented players who have made the club, there are several players from this generation who have made the cut and also invented clubs of their own.
Here is a list of the 7 players to make the 40/40 club:
RELATED | Top 20 All-Time Greatest Baseball Players
RELATED | MLB Players Who Played In The Little League World Series
1988 Jose Canseco – 42 HR, 40 SB, .307 AVG, .391 OBP, .569 SLG
The founding member of this club, Canseco, predicted he would achieve this milestone. He also drove in a league-leading 124 runs and posted a heavy .569 slugging percentage to coast to a unanimous AL MVP.
Canseco would lose to the Dodgers 4-1 in the World Series, winning the only game with a grand
1996 Barry Bonds – 42 HR, 40 SB, .308 AVG, .461 OBP, .615 SLG
Bonds paired pure athleticism with legendary plate discipline, combining 42 home runs and 40 stolen bases with a career-high 151 walks.
His absurd .461 OBP ensured he was constantly on base to leverage his speed, though his 9.7 WAR effort incredibly finished fifth in a hitter-dominated NL MVP vote that season.
Even with Bonds’ historic run, the Giant’s struggled this season, finishing 68-94 and 4th in the NL West.
1998 Alex Rodriguez – 42 HR, 46 SB, .310 AVG, .360 OBP, .560 SLG
At just 22 years old, A-Rod accomplished what remains the most physically demanding 40/40 season by doing it as a everyday shortstop.
He recorded an MLB-leading 213 hits, which helped him finish the season with a 43.9 Power/Speed number—the highest mark ever achieved in baseball history.
Rodriguez’s Mariners failed to reach the playoffs as well, ending the season at 76-85 and 3rd in the AL West.
2006 Alfonso Soriano – 46 HR, 41 SB, .277 AVG, .351 OBP, .560 SLG
After coming just one home run short with the Yankees in 2002, Soriano left no doubt during his single, explosive season in Washington.
He blasted 46 home runs and swiped 41 bags. Soriano’s season stands out unique because he also hit 41 doubles, creating the game’s only 40/40/40 performance.
The Nationals also failed to reach the postseason, finishing 71-91 and 5th in the NL East.
2023 Ronald Acuna Jr. – 41 HR, 73 SB, .337 AVG, .416 OBP, .596 SLG
Acuña weaponized MLB’s larger bases and rules limiting pitcher disengagements to turn the 40/40 club completely on its head.
While maintaining a career-best .337 batting average, he bashed 41 home runs and ran wild for 73 stolen bases, easily taking home NL MVP honors.
After Acuna’s record-breaking season, the superstar struggled in the postseason, hitting 2-14 and only scoring two runs. The Braves would fall in the NLDS to the Philadelphia Phillies.
2024 Shohei Ohtani – 54 HR, 59 SB, .310 AVG, .390 OBP, .646 SLG
Serving strictly as a designated hitter while rehabbing his throwing arm, Ohtani reached 40/40 in a blistering 126 games—shattering Soriano’s previous speed record of 147 games. He hit a walk-off grand slam to secure the milestone, eventually pushing his totals to 54 home runs and 59 steals to create the 50/50 club.
Ohtani is the only player so far to cap off his historic season winning the World Series, beating the Yankees in 5 games.
2026 Pete Crow-Armstrong – 45 HR, 41 SB, .280 AVG, .372 OBP, .570 SLG
Originally known as a spectacular, defense-first center fielder, PCA shocked the baseball world by developing top-tier power to accompany his elite speed. He tied for the MLB lead with 45 home runs and secured his 40th stolen base during the Cubs’ playoff-clinching victory in late September.
The Chicago Cubs will play in the Wild Card round on Tuesday.
Who do you think had the most impressive season? Let us know!
Pete Crow-Armstrong Joins Elite Company: The 7 Players In The 40/40 Club was originally published on wfnz.com

item.content:encoded:
Welcome to the 2026 MLB playoffs, baseball fans. The postseason got started Tuesday with a quartet of Game 1s in the best-of-three Wild Card Series. The Braves came back against the Phillies in the early start, while the White Sox cruised to an easy win against the Astros and . In the late slate, Michael King took a no-hitter into the seventh inning en route to a blowout Padres win over the Cubs.
In these short series, the Game 1 winners are one victory away from the LDS round, and the Game 1 losers are one loss away from their season being over.
The Rays, Guardians, Brewers and Dodgers all secured byes and await the winners in the next round. The Rays are the American League's top seed and will face a division rival in the ALDS, whether it's the Yankees or the Red Sox. The Guardians, despite an 85-77 record that ranks 10th out of the 12 playoff teams, earned the No. 2 seed in the AL and will face either the 84-win White Sox or 81-win Astros in the next round.
The Brewers (103 wins) and Dodgers (100 wins) both hit triple digits in the win column in the regular season, and they will host NLDS Game 1s on Saturday. The Brewers get the Padres-Cubs winner, while the two-time reigning champion Dodgers get either the Braves or the Phillies.

item.title: [New York Daily News] Red Sox’ Sonny Gray compares time with Yankees to a growing downhill snowball
item.dc:creator: James O'Connell
item.description: The Boston Red Sox starter in Game 2 of the AL Wild Card series on Wednesday needs no introduction to the boo birds. He’s got plenty of familiarity with the Bronx cheer, unfortunately for him, coming from his time with the Yankees. Sonny Gray will toe the slab for Chad Tracy’s squad in a pivotal playoff game back in the place that was home to arguably the lowest point of his MLB career. “I came from Oakland, and Oakland to [New York]. I think that maybe during my time there was a lot of outside
item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox starter in Game 2 of the AL Wild Card series on Wednesday needs no introduction to the boo birds. He’s got plenty of familiarity with the Bronx cheer, unfortunately for him, coming from his time with the Yankees.
Sonny Gray will toe the slab for Chad Tracy’s squad in a pivotal playoff game back in the place that was home to arguably the lowest point of his MLB career.
“I came from Oakland, and Oakland to [New York]. I think that maybe during my time there was a lot of outside this, outside that, unfamiliarity with me and my situation and my family,” Gray said before Tuesday’s Game 1. “It’s kind of like one of those things that you have a snowball or whatever, right?
“And there’s a snowball that kind of starts rolling down a hill. If you don’t ever stop it, then the snowball just gets bigger and bigger and bigger, and it picks up traction, and it just gets more snow. And it just continues to go down this thing. And then the bigger the snowball gets, the harder it is to stop it or take a step back.
“And for me, it just took me to get away and get myself into a different environment and then reflect on those things, right, like reflect on what was good, what was bad, what didn’t work. And that took some time.”
Gray pitched 41 games during his season-and-a-half with the Bombers — 4.51 ERA — and Yankee faithful will surely remember his time with the team on Wednesday.
The veteran starter is expecting the obvious in terms of the reception he’ll receive as he goes out to try and win a postseason game for the Red Sox.
“I think it will be a playoff energy on the road, playoff atmosphere on the road,” said Gray. “As far as reception, this or that, it will be what it will be. I’m not going to sit here and try to control something that I can’t control because I ultimately have no control over that.
“It will be what it will be, and I’ll just do my part to be ready to go out there and compete and to pitch and to go win a game.”
Gray was acquired from the Athletics at the 2017 trade deadline prior to the Bombers’ unexpected and memorable run to Game 7 of the ALCS. The 36-year-old was acquired to be a frontline starter behind Luis Severino at the very beginning of the ‘Baby Bombers’ era.
The right-hander’s first run with the Yanks was respectable as he pitched to a 3.72 ERA in 11 games during the 2017 season and even added a strong ALCS start, throwing five innings and allowing one earned run against the Houston Astros. However, the wheels fell off in 2018, when he owned a 4.90 ERA in 30 games and heard an awful amount of boos from the home crowd before being shipped off to the Cincinnati Reds in the offseason.
Despite the rough experience, Gray greatly values his time in New York and attributes it not only to the pitcher, but to the man he is today.
“I do know that playing here made me a stronger person, made me a better man, a better husband. Ultimately, it made me a better pitcher, a better baseball player. And that’s kind of what I take from my time here. …
“I learned a lot. I learned what to do, what not to do. I mean, it was a bump in the road for me, but ultimately it made me a better person.”
Gray found success immediately after departing the Bronx. He was an All-Star for the Reds in 2019 and then again with the Minnesota Twins in 2023. The veteran enters the postseason riding a very successful season in which he pitched to a 2.72 ERA in 29 games with the Red Sox.
The Tennessean is not focused on any sort of revenge and doesn’t need any added motivation to stick it to the Yankees. Instead, he’s solely focused on trying to win for the Bo Sox.
“That’s kind of how I look at it. I don’t look at it as any other thing than that.”

item.title: [heavy.com] Red Sox Make Adley Rutschman Decision for Wild Card Game 1
item.dc:creator: Zach Kaplan
item.description: The Red Sox paid a handsome price for former Orioles catcher Adley Rutschman at the MLB trade deadline, dealing a handful of top prospects for the former No. 1 overall pick. item.content:encoded:
The Red Sox paid a handsome price for former Orioles catcher Adley Rutschman at the MLB trade deadline, dealing a handful of top prospects for the former No. 1 overall pick. After a middling second half, Chad Tracy’s first playoff lineup decision as manager of the Red Sox puts a lot of faith in Rutschman.
Tracy unveiled the Red Sox starting lineup that would hit against Yankees ace and likely Cy Young Cam Schlittler in Game 1 of the American League Wild Card at Yankee Stadium. Unsurprisingly, former top overall prospect in baseball Roman Anthony is leading off, but it’s Rutschman batting second ahead of All-Star first baseman Willson Contreras in the #3 spot.
Rutschman’s place in the order had been messed around with in the final days of the regular season, with Rutschman batting second, third or fifth on a given night. Much of Rutschman’s batting second has to do with the loss of Mickey Gasper to a biceps injury, as Gasper was usually the guy Tracy wanted on base ahead of the Red Sox’ power bats.
Chad Tracy’s Informed Adley Rutschman Lineup Decision
The decision to bat Rutschman second isn’t arbitrary: Rutschman is one of just two Red Sox players currently to have an extra base hit against Schlittler this year, along with third baseman Caleb Durbin, who hit a two-run home run against him earlier this season.
The Red Sox’ starting nine of Anthony, Rutschman, Contreras, Wilyer Abreu, Ceddanne Rafaela, Nick Sogard, Jarren Duran, Trevor Story and Durbin is just a combined 8-for-59 (.136) with the two extra base hits against Schlittler this season.
The lineup appears to be Chad Tracy’s best attempt at getting some runs across against Schlittler. The announcement comes amid musings that the Red Sox reportedly “wore out” the Rays’ Trajekt machine mimicking Schlittler’s arsenal this weekend while they were playing their season finale against the Cubs in the domed Tropicana Field due to heavy rain in Boston.
AL Wild Card Preview
The Yankees put out a platoon-heavy lineup of their own, starting veterans Paul Goldschmidt and Amed Rosario over Luis Garcia Jr. at first and Jazz Chisholm Jr at second. The Yankees got a “mini break” as their games against the Orioles on Saturday and Sunday, with no clinching scenarios on the line, were canceled due to the same nor’easter that pushed the Sox and Cubs to Florida.
It’ll be a rematch of the 2025 American League Wild Card series, which the Yankees won in three electrifying games, but with a different cast of characters, Rutschman chief among them. The Red Sox will surely rely on him finding his bat this series after posting a disappointing .222/.278/.410 slash in the final two months of the season after the trade from Baltimore. He’ll be thrown immediately into the fire against Schlittler, and it should certainly be a fun one.

item.content:encoded:
The Houston Astros enter the postseason with the AL MVP favorite in their lineup.
Yordan Alvarez should be considered the most feared hitter in baseball for this year's playoffs.
But the rest of Houston's lineup has been mediocre at best.
"The Astros have the presumptive AL MVP in Yordan Alvarez, but the rest of the offense has produced a .233/.300/.396 line this year," Bleacher Report's Joel Reuter wrote. "He will need to replicate his memorable performance in the 2023 ALCS for pretty much the entirety of October."
Clearly, the Astros rely on Alvarez to do most of their offensive damage, but he may not be the AL West club's "X-Factor" during the Wild Card Series against the Chicago White Sox.
Instead, Reuter has tabbed rookie center fielder Lucas Spence as someone who can help Houston make a deep postseason run.
"Lucas Spence went 6-for-18 with four home runs in five games after being recalled from Triple-A when [Daulton] Varsho and [Brice] Matthews were placed on the injured list," Reuter added. "He suddenly looks like the no-doubt starting center fielder for the club's playoff run."
MORE: Pirates urged to re-sign Brandon Lowe if they ‘want to be taken seriously’
Varsho is unavailable in the Wild Card Series due to left wrist inflammation caused by cysts.
He is a Gold Glove outfielder but has hit poorly following a midseason trade from the Toronto Blue Jays.
Spence has just 19 MLB games under his belt but looks up for the challenge, hitting the first three home runs of his career in a single game during the last week of the regular season against the Athletics.

item.content:encoded:
As the 2026 MLB postseason prepares to begin, it's a good time for some bold predictions about who will win and why, from the wild-card rounds to the World Series.
Chicago White Sox at Houston Astros
Houston was just 11-13 in September and it felt like neither the Astros nor the Texas Rangers wanted to win the AL West. Houston finally did on the last day, but the Astros aren't inspiring confidence that they can go deep into the postseason.
The White Sox could have been the AL Central champs, but couldn't hang on as Cleveland made a hard charge and overtook them. For a team that has been told all season about they are still living in the shadow of a 121-loss season two years ago, this team has a chip on its shoulder. That should push the White Sox into the next round.
Boston Red Sox at New York Yankees
After a chaotic weather weekend in the Northeast that forced the Red Sox to play Game 162 in Tampa and canceled the final game of the season for the Yankees, that extra day of rest (and far less travel) may help New York when the wild-card series opens in the Bronx.
New York's pitching lineup of Cam Schlittler, Max Fried and Gerrit Cole will be enough to overcome any of the Yankees' offensive issues in a series that will last just two games.
Philadelphia Phillies at Atlanta Braves
Like Houston, Philadelphia did little to inspire confidence in its postseason future at the end of the regular season. It's also been a season where the Braves have Philadelphia's number, winning nine of the 13 games the two rivals have played. Atlanta sweeps Philadelphia.
Chicago Cubs at San Diego Padres
The Padres are red-hot entering the wild card, going 18-6 in September to secure a home series. Having the home fans on their side, San Diego will continue its solid play by sweeping the Cubs into the offseason.
New York Yankees vs. Tampa Bay Rays
While the Yankees may have had enough to get into the ALDS, there's little doubt that the Rays are the better team.
All season, it was a question of if New York could catch Tampa Bay for the AL East title. The Rays kept showing they weren't going to crack under any pressure, and that continues with a 3-1 series win to move on to the ALCS.
Chicago White Sox vs. Cleveland Guardians
Chicago's story has been incredible, but there's a reason why the Guardians won the division ... and keep a reputation as the team that doesn't die easily. They're built for pressure and the postseason and will dispatch the White Sox in four games.
Atlanta Braves vs. Los Angeles Dodgers
This will be must-see TV as two of the NL's behemoths battle it out. The home advantage will make a difference for the Dodgers, who will win in Game 5 to seal another trip to the NLCS.
San Diego Padres vs. Milwaukee Brewers
Milwaukee is for real. There have been plenty of instances in the past where the Brewers have stumbled in the postseason, but this won't be a repeat of those mistakes. Jacob Misiorowski will set the tone in the first game and the Brewers will win in four.
Tampa Bay Rays vs. Cleveland Guardians
The Rays went 5-1 against Cleveland this season. With homefield advantage, there's no reason to think that trend won't continue. Look for the Rays to oust the Guardians in six games.
Los Angeles Dodgers vs. Milwaukee Brewers
This season, the Brewers are 4-3 against the Dodgers. With Milwaukee holding home-field advantage, this is the year that Los Angeles is finally stopped short of winning it all.
There is a lot to like for Milwaukee in their relief pitching options, and it may come down to that. While the Dodgers may have the better rotation, Milwaukee has the better pitching staff overall. Pitching wins in October, and the Brewers win a classic in seven games in front of their home fans.
Tampa Bay Rays vs. Milwaukee Brewers
A World Series without a "major market" in it? Oh this will set up plenty of conversations for what will be a contentious offseason.
Neither of these teams have won a World Series, making for another fascinating storyline in what will be an epic Fall Classic. Milwaukee has the home-field advantage thanks to their 103 regular-season wins, and that makes a big difference in this battle of the top seeds.
Brewers in six.
